Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. For $a\ge9\pi$ and $b=a-\frac14$ let $\delta=\delta(a)$ be the constant of the uniform Lorentzian bound, $r_1(a)=\frac1{2(1-\delta)b}\big(1+\frac{a^2}{(b-2)^2}+\frac a{(b-1)^2}+\frac{2a}{b-1}\big)$ and $r_2(a)=\frac1{4(1-\delta)b}\big(\frac4b+\frac{2a^2}{(b-2)^3}+\frac{2a}{(b-1)^3}+\frac{4a}{(b-1)^2}\big)$; these bound $|C_a'|/C_a$ and $|C_a''|/C_a$ uniformly in $t$, where $C_a$ is the cosine transform of $e^{-ae^w}e^{w/4}$ at $t/2$. For every prime $P$ and $t\ge14$, with $a_q=\pi q^2$, $(\log D_P)''(t)\ge-2/t^2-r_2(a_q)-r_1(a_q)^2\ge-0.0239$.

Source: [`ch/mi1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi1.tex), label `mi:thm:curv`.

<a id="real_zeros_of_the_friable_approximant_live_in_negative_humps_of_xi_in_pairs"></a>

### Real zeros of the friable approximant live in the negative humps of Xi, in pairs, and surviving humps are nested in P

Theorem 22.4.1, page 807 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. A negative hump is a maximal interval $I_j\subset(0,\infty)$ on which $\Xi<0$, of length $\ell_j$. (1) Every real zero of $\Xi_P$ lies in a negative hump, and $\Xi_P(\gamma)=D_P(\gamma)>0$ at every zero $\gamma$ of $\Xi$. (2) Each hump holds an even number of zeros of $\Xi_P$ counted with multiplicity, and the number $R_P$ of positive real zeros is even. (3) Suppose every zero of $\Xi$ whose real part lies within $\frac12$ of $I_j$ is real (by the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis of Platt and Trudgian (2021) this holds for every hump below $3\cdot10^{12}$) and $\ell_j<18.29$. Then $I_j$ holds no zero, one double zero or two simple zeros of $\Xi_P$, and two simple zeros exactly when $\max_{I_j}(|\Xi|-D_P)>0$. (4) If $I_j$ carries zeros of $\Xi_P$ then it carries zeros of $\Xi_{P'}$ for every prime $P'>P$.

Source: [`ch/mi1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi1.tex), label `mi:thm:humps`.

<a id="count_of_real_zeros_of_the_friable_approximant_is_twice_the_number_of_deep_humps"></a>

### Count: the number of positive real zeros of the friable approximant is twice the number of negative humps of Xi deeper than the deficit

Theorem 22.4.2, page 808 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. Let $N(T)$ count the zeros of $\Xi$ in $(0,T]$ with multiplicity, $A(t)=\frac12(t^2+\frac14)\pi^{-1/4}|\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{it}2)|$, so that $\Xi=-AZ$ with $Z$ Hardy's function, and $I_j$ the negative humps of $\Xi$. Assume that for every hump meeting $(0,\tau_P^+)$ the local hypotheses hold (all zeros of $\Xi$ within $\frac12$ of the hump are real, by the verification of the Riemann Hypothesis of Platt and Trudgian (2021) below height $3\cdot10^{12}$, and its length is below $18.29$). Then $R_P=2\#\{j:\max_{I_j}(|\Xi|-D_P)>0\}$. Let $\tau_P^+$ solve $D_P(\tau)=0.63A(\tau)\tau^{1/6}\log\tau$; the solution is unique for $\tau\ge14$ and $\Xi_P>0$ on $(\tau_P^+,\infty)$ (this uses Hiary's bound $|\zeta(\frac12+it)|\le0.63t^{1/6}\log t$). Then $R_P\le2\lceil N(\tau_P^+)/2\rceil$.

Source: [`ch/mi1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi1.tex), label `mi:thm:count`.

<a id="conjecture_on_the_number_of_real_zeros_of_the_friable_approximant_and_the_peaks_of_hardys_function"></a>

### Conjecture: the number of real zeros of the friable approximant is the zero count at the breakdown height plus a correction from the peaks of Hardy's function

Conjecture 22.5.1, page 810 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. Let $N(T)$ count the zeros of $\Xi$ in $(0,T]$, $R_P$ the number of positive real zeros of $\Xi_P$, $\tau_P^*$ the breakdown height, the solution of $A(\tau)=D_P(\tau)$ (about $4q^2$, a heuristic formula checked by computation) and $m_Z(T)$ the mean of $\log\max|Z|$ over the negative humps near $T$, for $Z$ Hardy's function. Conjecture: $R_P=N(\tau_P^*)+\frac2{\pi^2}\log\frac{\tau_P^*}{2\pi}\,m_Z(\tau_P^*)+O\big((\log q)^{1/2}(\log\log q)^{1/2}\big)$.

Source: [`ch/mi2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi2.tex), label `mi:conj:survey`.

<a id="kink_budget_when_the_pole_kernel_is_replaced_by_a_smooth_even_kernel"></a>

### Kink budget: the limit of the friable approximant with a smooth even kernel replacing the pole term

Proposition 22.8.1, page 814 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. Let $c_P=\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}(4\pi m^2-1)e^{-\pi m^2}$ be the kink constant. Replace the pole kernel $e^{-u/2}$ in the folded kernel $k_P(u)=e^{-u/2}-2e^{u/2}\psi_P(e^{2u})$ by an even kernel $\kappa$, smooth on $[0,\infty)$ with all derivatives $O(e^{-u/2})$, and let $\Xi_P^\kappa(t)=(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty(k_P+\kappa-e^{-u/2})(u)\cos(tu)\,du$. Then $\lim_{t\to\infty}\Xi_P^\kappa(t)=c_P-\frac12-\kappa'(0+)$ along $\mathbb{R}$.

Source: [`ch/mi3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi3.tex), label `mi:prop:kinkbudget`.

<a id="reweighting_with_weights_in_zero_one_has_smallest_deficit_for_the_indicator_of_the_complement"></a>

### Reweighting: among weights in [0,1] vanishing on a given set, the indicator of the complement has the smallest deficit

Proposition 22.8.2, page 814 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. For weights $w=(w_n)$ let $\Xi_w(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_w(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ with $\psi_w(x)=\sum_nw_ne^{-\pi n^2x}$, and $D_w=\Xi_w-\Xi=(t^2+\frac14)\sum_n(1-w_n)C_{\pi n^2}$, where $C_a$ is the cosine transform of $e^{-ae^w}e^{w/4}$ at $t/2$. If $0\le w_n\le w_n'\le1$ for every $n$ then $D_w\ge D_{w'}\ge0$ on $\mathbb{R}$, with $D_{w'}>0$ unless every $w_n'=1$. So among weights in $[0,1]$ that vanish on a given set of integers, the indicator of its complement has the smallest deficit.

Source: [`ch/mi3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi3.tex), label `mi:prop:reweight`.

<a id="friable_approximant_is_uniformly_close_to_xi_on_the_imaginary_axis_for_p_2_and_3"></a>

### The friable approximants for P = 2 and 3 are uniformly close to Xi on the imaginary axis and have no zero there

Proposition 22.9.1, page 815 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\mathcal F(P)$ be the set of positive integers all of whose prime factors are at most $P$ (the $P$ friable integers), $\psi_P(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathcal F(P)}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, and let the friable approximant be $\Xi_P(t)=\frac12-2(t^2+\frac14)\int_0^\infty\psi_P(e^{2u})e^{u/2}\cos(tu)\,du$ (the same formula with all integers $n$ gives $\Xi$). Let $q$ be the least prime above $P$ and $D_P=\Xi_P-\Xi$ the deficit. For $P=2$ and $P=3$, $\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}}|\Xi_P(iy)/\Xi(iy)-1|$ is at most $6.8\times10^{-13}$ for $P=2$ and at most $3.4\times10^{-35}$ for $P=3$. In particular $\Xi_P$ has no zero on $i\mathbb{R}$. The bound rests on the proved estimate $|\Xi_P(iy)-\Xi(iy)|\le|y^2-\frac14|\sum_{m\notin\mathcal F(P)}(\pi m^2)^{-s}\Gamma(s,\pi m^2)$ with $s=\frac12(|y|+\frac12)$, whose supremum after division by $\Xi(iy)=\xi(\frac12+y)>0$ was computed at $30$ digits on a grid of step $0.1$ on $[0,40]$ and shown to decrease beyond it; it is a computation, not a certified enclosure.

Source: [`ch/mi3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi3.tex), label `mi:prop:axis`.

<a id="shift_identity_xi_is_the_cosine_of_a_shift_applied_to_the_transform_of_phi_over_cosh"></a>

### Shift identity: Xi is the average of two shifts of the transform of Phi divided by cosh, which contains Miyatake's identity

Proposition 22.11.1, page 818 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. For $b>0$ put $g_b(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\operatorname{sech}(bu)\,e^{izu}\,du$ (the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$), an entire even function of order at most one, real on $\mathbb{R}$. For every $b>0$ and $z\in\mathbb{C}$, $\Xi(z)=\frac12\{g_b(z+ib)+g_b(z-ib)\}$, that is $\Xi=\cos(b\partial)g_b$ with $\partial=d/dz$. Miyatake's identity is the case $b=\frac92$ (with his transform $g(x)=g_{9/2}(2x)/(4\pi^2)$).

Source: [`ch/mi4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi4.tex), label `mi:prop:shiftb`.

<a id="transform_of_phi_over_cosh_is_a_levy_area_smoothing_and_a_polya_gamma_mixture_of_the_flow"></a>

### Levy area, Polya Gamma clock and Thorin atoms: the transform of Phi over cosh is Xi smoothed by Levy's stochastic area

Theorem 22.11.2, page 819 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. For $b>0$ put $g_b(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\operatorname{sech}(bu)\,e^{izu}\,du$ (the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$), an entire even function of order at most one, real on $\mathbb{R}$. Let $\mathcal A=\frac12\int_0^1(W^1dW^2-W^2dW^1)$ be Lévy's stochastic area of a planar Brownian motion $(W^1,W^2)$, with $\mathbb{E}e^{i\lambda\mathcal A}=\operatorname{sech}(\lambda/2)$, let $\varpi$ be a Pólya Gamma variable $\mathrm{PG}(1,0)$ with $\mathbb{E}e^{-s\varpi}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{s/2}$, and $\mathcal H_\lambda(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{\lambda u^2}e^{izu}\,du$ the de Bruijn Newman family. For real $x$, $g_b(x)=\mathbb{E}\,\Xi(x+2b\mathcal A)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Xi(x-y)\frac1{2b}\operatorname{sech}\frac{\pi y}{2b}\,dy=\mathbb{E}_\varpi[\mathcal H_{-2b^2\varpi}(x)]$, and $2b\mathcal A\overset d=2b\sqrt\varpi\,\mathcal N\overset d=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{2b}{(2k-1)\pi}L_k$ with $\mathcal N$ standard normal and $L_k$ independent standard Laplace variables. Hence $\Xi\mapsto g_b$ is convolution with an extended generalised gamma convolution whose Thorin measure has atoms at $\pm(2k-1)\pi/(2b)$.

Source: [`ch/mi4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi4.tex), label `mi:thm:levyarea`.

<a id="logistic_partition_of_unity_splits_xi_into_two_pieces_of_the_transform_over_cosh"></a>

### Logistic partition: 2 xi is the sum of two logistic weighted expectations of a power of a random variable

Proposition 22.11.3, page 819 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Upsilon=V^{1/2}$ with $V$ the random variable of the Biane Pitman Yor identity for $\xi$ (as defined in the book), and $\varpi\sim\mathrm{PG}(1,0)$ a Pólya Gamma variable. For $c>0$, $2\xi(s)=\mathbb{E}[\Upsilon^s/(1+\Upsilon^c)]+\mathbb{E}[\Upsilon^{s+c}/(1+\Upsilon^c)]$; with $c=2b$ and $s=\frac12+iz$ the two terms are $g_b(z+ib)$ and $g_b(z-ib)$, for $g_b$ the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$. The logistic weight is the Pólya Gamma mixture $\Upsilon^c/(1+\Upsilon^c)=\frac12\Upsilon^{c/2}\mathbb{E}_\varpi\exp(-\frac12\varpi c^2(\log\Upsilon)^2)$ (Polson, Scott and Windle 2013).

Source: [`ch/mi4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi4.tex), label `mi:prop:logistic`.

<a id="exponential_tail_of_the_transform_of_phi_over_cosh_appears_exactly_above_b_equal_two"></a>

### Exponential tail: the transform of Phi over cosh has a residue term C_b e^{-pi z/(2b)} exactly when b exceeds 2

Theorem 22.12.1, page 820 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. For $b>0$ put $g_b(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\operatorname{sech}(bu)\,e^{izu}\,du$ (the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$), an entire even function of order at most one, real on $\mathbb{R}$. Let $b>2$, $\pi/(2b)<\tau<\min(\pi/4,3\pi/(2b))$ and $Y>0$. Then, uniformly for $\operatorname{Re}z\ge0$ and $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le Y$, $g_b(z)=C_be^{-\pi z/(2b)}+O(e^{-\tau\operatorname{Re}z})$ with $C_b=\frac{2\pi}b\,\Phi(\frac{i\pi}{2b})$. For $b<2$ there is no residue and $g_b(x)=O(e^{-\tau x})$ for every $\tau<\pi/4$.

Source: [`ch/mi4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi4.tex), label `mi:thm:tail`.

<a id="cusp_asymptotics_of_the_residue_constant_as_b_decreases_to_two"></a>

### Cusp asymptotics: the residue constant C_b of the transform of Phi over cosh as b decreases to 2

Theorem 22.12.2, page 820 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. For $b>2$ put $C_b=\frac{2\pi}b\Phi(\frac{i\pi}{2b})$ (the residue constant of the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$) and $\delta=\pi(b-2)/(4b)$. As $b\downarrow2$, $C_b=-\frac{\pi^3}{32b}(2\delta)^{-1/2}\delta^{-4}e^{-\frac\pi8\cot\delta}(1+O(b-2))$.

Source: [`ch/mi4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi4.tex), label `mi:thm:cusp`.

<a id="transform_of_phi_over_cosh_for_b_above_two_is_not_in_the_laguerre_polya_class"></a>

### For b above 2 with C_b nonzero the transform of Phi over cosh has finitely many real zeros and is not in the Laguerre Polya class

Corollary 22.12.3, page 821 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. For $b>0$ put $g_b(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\operatorname{sech}(bu)\,e^{izu}\,du$ (the transform of $\Phi/\cosh(bu)$), an entire even function of order at most one, real on $\mathbb{R}$. For $b>2$ with $C_b=\frac{2\pi}b\Phi(\frac{i\pi}{2b})\ne0$, $g_b$ has finitely many real zeros, infinitely many nonreal zeros, and is not in the Laguerre Pólya class. In particular Miyatake's transform, for which $b=\frac92$ and $C_{9/2}>0$, is not.

Source: [`ch/mi4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi4.tex), label `mi:cor:notLP`.

<a id="polar_part_of_the_psi_m_kernel_is_a_simple_pole_at_cos_two_pi_over_nine_with_positive_residue"></a>

### Polar part of the Miyatake kernel in the variable cosh t: a simple pole at cos(2 pi/9) with positive residue r_0

Proposition 22.13.1, page 823 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, analytic for $|\operatorname{Im}u|<\frac\pi4$, and let $\psi_{\mathrm M}(t)=\Phi(t/2)/(8\pi^2\cosh(9t/4))$, an even function of $t$ on the strip $|\operatorname{Im}t|<\frac\pi2$. The map $t\mapsto c=\cosh t$ sends this strip, modulo $t\mapsto-t$, one to one onto the half plane $\operatorname{Re}c>0$, so $\psi_{\mathrm M}$ is a function of $c$ there. As a function of $c$, $\psi_{\mathrm M}$ is analytic on $\operatorname{Re}c>0$ except for a simple pole at $c_0=\cos\frac{2\pi}9$ with residue $r_0=\frac{\sin(2\pi/9)}{18\pi^2}\Phi(\frac{i\pi}9)=\frac{\sin(2\pi/9)}{8\pi^3}C_{9/2}>0$, where $C_{9/2}=\frac{4\pi}9\Phi(\frac{i\pi}9)>0$ is the residue constant of the transform of $\Phi$ divided by $\cosh(9u/2)$. Consequently $\psi_{\mathrm M}(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^4e^{-2\pi n^2\cosh t}+\psi_{\mathrm E}(t)+\psi_{\mathrm A}(t)$, where $\psi_{\mathrm E}(t)=r_0e^{-2\pi(\cosh t-c_0)}/(\cosh t-c_0)=r_0\int_{2\pi}^\infty e^{c_0a}e^{-a\cosh t}\,da$ (the integral for $\operatorname{Re}\cosh t>c_0$) and $\psi_{\mathrm A}$ is analytic in $c$ on all of $\operatorname{Re}c>0$. Moreover $r_0=0.009206406367$, computed in interval arithmetic with all digits shown certified. The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson.

Source: [`ch/mi4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi4.tex), label `mi:prop:polar`.

<a id="exponential_mixture_of_polya_bessel_functions_has_nonreal_zeros_unless_the_exponent_is_cos_two_pi_over_nine"></a>

### The exponent is forced: an exponential mixture of Pólya Bessel functions has finitely many real zeros unless its exponent is cos(2 pi/9)

Proposition 22.13.2, page 823 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $0<\theta<\frac\pi2$ and $a_0>0$, let $K_\nu$ be the modified Bessel function of the second kind, and put $\mathcal E_\theta(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\frac{\cosh(9u/2)\,e^{-a_0(\cosh2u-\cos\theta)}}{\cosh2u-\cos\theta}e^{izu}\,du=\int_{a_0}^\infty e^{a\cos\theta}\,\frac12\{K_{\frac94+\frac{iz}2}(a)+K_{\frac94-\frac{iz}2}(a)\}\,da$, the exponential mixture with exponent $\cos\theta$ of the Pólya functions $\frac12\{K_{\frac94+\frac{iz}2}(a)+K_{\frac94-\frac{iz}2}(a)\}$ (the transforms of $\cosh(9u/2)e^{-a\cosh2u}$). For $\theta/2<\tau<\frac\pi4$ and $Y>0$, uniformly for $\operatorname{Re}z\ge0$ and $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le Y$, $\mathcal E_\theta(z)=\frac{\pi\cos(9\theta/4)}{\sin\theta}e^{-\theta z/2}+O(e^{-\tau\operatorname{Re}z})$. If $\theta\ne\frac{2\pi}9$, then $\mathcal E_\theta$ has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros, and it is not in the Laguerre Pólya class. The conclusion leaves only $\theta=\frac{2\pi}9$, where $\cos(9\theta/4)=0$; whether $\mathcal E_{2\pi/9}$ is in the Laguerre Pólya class is open. The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson.

Source: [`ch/mi4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi4.tex), label `mi:prop:rigid`.

<a id="polar_transform_is_a_meixner_convolution_of_a_laguerre_polya_function_and_the_meixner_law_is_a_polya_frequency_function"></a>

### A Meixner convolution: the polar transform is a Pólya frequency density convolved with a Laguerre Pólya function

Proposition 22.13.3, page 824 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $c_1=\cos\frac\pi9$ and $c_0=\cos\frac{2\pi}9=2c_1^2-1$, and let $\mathcal U(u)=\frac{\cosh(9u/2)}{2(\cosh u-c_1)}=\cosh\frac{7u}2+2c_1\cosh\frac{5u}2+(1+2c_0)\cosh\frac{3u}2+(1+2c_1)\cosh\frac u2$, so that $\cosh(9u/2)/(\cosh2u-c_0)=\mathcal U(u)/(\cosh u+c_1)$. Let $P(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}e^{-2\pi\cosh2u}e^{izu}\,du$ and $\Xi^{\mathcal U}(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\mathcal U(u)e^{-2\pi\cosh2u}e^{izu}\,du=\sum_jm_j\cos(\frac{b_j}2\partial)P$ with $(b_j,m_j)=(7,1),(5,2c_1),(3,1+2c_0),(1,1+2c_1)$, where $\cos(\beta\partial)f(z)=\frac12\{f(z+i\beta)+f(z-i\beta)\}$. (i) $\mathcal U$ is a universal factor in the sense of Pólya, and $\Xi^{\mathcal U}$ is in the Laguerre Pólya class. (ii) For $0\le\varphi<\pi$ let $q_\varphi(x)=\frac{(1+\cos\varphi)\sinh(\varphi x)}{\sin\varphi\,\sinh(\pi x)}$, with $q_0(x)=2x/\sinh(\pi x)$. Then $q_\varphi$ is a probability density with $\int_{\mathbb{R}}q_\varphi(x)e^{iux}\,dx=\frac{1+\cos\varphi}{\cosh u+\cos\varphi}$ and variance $1/(1+\cos\varphi)$, and it is a Pólya frequency function (by Schoenberg's characterisation). Moreover $\frac{1+\cos\varphi}{\cosh u+\cos\varphi}=\mathbb{E}\,e^{-\varsigma_\varphi u^2}$ with $\varsigma_\varphi=\sum_{k\ge0}\big(\frac{e_k}{((2k+1)\pi-\varphi)^2}+\frac{e_k'}{((2k+1)\pi+\varphi)^2}\big)$, $\mathbb{E}\varsigma_\varphi=\frac1{2(1+\cos\varphi)}$, for independent standard exponential variables $e_k,e_k'$. Hence for every kernel $k$ for which the integrals converge, the transform of $k(u)(1+\cos\varphi)/(\cosh u+\cos\varphi)$ is $q_\varphi*\hat k$ ($\hat k$ the transform of $k$); for $k=\Phi$, Riemann's kernel $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$ (so that $\Xi(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{izu}\,du$), it is $\mathbb{E}\,\mathcal H_{-\varsigma_\varphi}$ with $\mathcal H_\lambda(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{\lambda u^2}e^{izu}\,du$ the de Bruijn Newman family, a flow at a random negative time. (iii) Let $r_0=\frac{\sin(2\pi/9)}{18\pi^2}\Phi(\frac{i\pi}9)=0.009206406367$, the residue at $\cosh t=c_0$ of the Miyatake kernel $\Phi(t/2)/(8\pi^2\cosh(9t/4))$ as a function of $\cosh t$, and let $\Xi^{\mathrm E}(z)=8\pi^2r_0\int_{\mathbb{R}}\frac{\cosh(9u/2)\,e^{-2\pi(\cosh2u-c_0)}}{\cosh2u-c_0}e^{izu}\,du$, the transform of the polar part. Then $\Xi^{\mathrm E}=\frac{8\pi^2r_0e^{2\pi c_0}}{1+c_1}\,q_{\pi/9}*\Xi^{\mathcal U}$. The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson, using Pólya's theorems on universal factors and on the zeros of $K_{iz}$ and Schoenberg's theorem.

Source: [`ch/mi4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi4.tex), label `mi:prop:meixner`.

<a id="bottom_of_the_cosh_ladder_is_bounded_by_the_quasi_riemann_abscissa"></a>

### The bottom of the cosh ladder is at most the largest real part of a zero of zeta minus one half

Proposition 22.14.1, page 826 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function and $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, an even entire function, real on $\mathbb{R}$, whose zeros are the ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. For real $b$ let $F_b(z)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)\cosh(bu)e^{izu}\,du=\frac12\{\Xi(z+ib)+\Xi(z-ib)\}$, so that $F_b(x)=\operatorname{Re}\xi(\frac12+b+ix)$ on $\mathbb{R}$. Let $B_{\cosh}=\inf\{b\ge0: F_b\text{ has only real zeros}\}$ (the bottom of the cosh ladder; $B_{\cosh}\le\frac12$ by de Bruijn's strip theorem) and $\sigma_{\max}=\sup\operatorname{Re}\rho$ over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$ of zeta. Then $B_{\cosh}\le\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$.

Source: [`ch/mi5.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi5.tex), label `mi:prop:BTheta`.

<a id="conjecture_bottom_of_the_cosh_ladder_equals_the_asymptotic_quasi_riemann_abscissa"></a>

### Conjecture: the bottom of the cosh ladder lies between the asymptotic and the global quasi Riemann abscissa

Conjecture 22.14.2, page 827 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. With $F_b(z)=\int\Phi(u)\cosh(bu)e^{izu}\,du$, so that $F_b(x)=\operatorname{Re}\xi(\frac12+b+ix)$ on $\mathbb R$, the cosh ladder of Riemann's xi function, $B_{\cosh}=\inf\{b\ge0: F_b\text{ has only real zeros}\}$ its bottom rung, $\sigma_{\max}=\sup\operatorname{Re}\rho$ and $\sigma_{\max}^\infty=\limsup_{\gamma\to\infty}\beta$ over the nontrivial zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ of zeta: conjecturally $\sigma_{\max}^\infty-\frac12\le B_{\cosh}\le\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$. The upper bound is proved; the lower bound is conjectured. Under the conjecture, lowering the unconditional bound $B_{\cosh}\le\frac12$ is equivalent to a quasi Riemann hypothesis whenever $\sigma_{\max}$ is approached at large height.

Source: [`ch/mi5.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi5.tex), label `mi:conj:quasi`.

<a id="paired_form_of_the_cosh_ladder_hermite_biehler_equivalence_with_zero_free_half_plane"></a>

### Paired form: zeta has no zero to the right of alpha exactly when the real and imaginary parts of xi on the line alpha interlace

Theorem 22.14.3, page 828 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $\alpha>\frac12$, $E_\alpha(z)=\xi(\alpha-iz)$ and $E^\#(z)=\overline{E(\bar z)}$. The following are equivalent: (i) $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s\ge\alpha$; (ii) $E_\alpha$ is Hermite Biehler, that is $|E_\alpha(z)|>|E_\alpha^\#(z)|$ for $\operatorname{Im}z>0$; (iii) $\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ and $\operatorname{Im}\xi(\alpha+it)$, as entire functions of $t$, have only real simple zeros, and these strictly interlace. Hence the paired bottom rung, the infimum of the $\alpha-\frac12$ for which these hold, is exactly $\sigma_{\max}-\frac12$ (with $\sigma_{\max}$ the supremum of the real parts of the nontrivial zeros), and the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if (iii) holds for every $\alpha>\frac12$.

Source: [`ch/mi5.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi5.tex), label `mi:thm:paired`.

<a id="density_of_real_zeros_of_the_real_and_imaginary_parts_of_xi_on_a_line_to_the_right_of_one_half"></a>

### Real zeros of the real and imaginary parts of xi on a vertical line right of one half have asymptotically full density

Theorem 22.14.4, page 830 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $N^\pm(T)$ the number of nontrivial zeros $\beta+i\gamma$ of zeta with $|\gamma|\le T$, $N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T)$ the number of them with $\beta>\alpha$, and $\theta_\alpha(t)=\arg\xi(\alpha+it)$. For $\alpha>\frac12$ with $\beta\ne\alpha$ for every zero, $\theta_\alpha(T)-\theta_\alpha(-T)=\pi(N^\pm(T)-2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T))+O(\log T)$. Hence $\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ and $\operatorname{Im}\xi(\alpha+it)$ each have at least $N^\pm(T)-2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T)-O(\log T)$ real zeros in $[-T,T]$. If moreover $F_b$, for $b=\alpha-\frac12$ and $F_b(z)=\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+iz)$, satisfies the Riemann von Mangoldt formula with error $O(\log T)$, its nonreal zeros with $|\operatorname{Re}z|\le T$ number at most $2N^\pm_{>\alpha}(T)+O(\log T)$.

Source: [`ch/mi5.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi5.tex), label `mi:thm:density`.

<a id="zeros_of_real_parts_and_imaginary_parts_of_xi_on_two_lines_to_the_right_of_one_alternate_or_fail_to_alternate_by_the_euler_product"></a>

### Interlacing across rungs: criteria for the zeros of the real and imaginary parts of xi on two lines to alternate or to fail to alternate

Proposition 22.14.5, page 831 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$ be Riemann's xi function. For $\alpha>1$ let $A_\alpha(t)=\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ and $B_\alpha(t)=\operatorname{Im}\xi(\alpha+it)$ for real $t$, and write $\xi(\alpha+it)=|\xi(\alpha+it)|e^{i\theta_\alpha(t)}$ with $\theta_\alpha$ continuous and $\theta_\alpha(0)=0$. Let $1<\alpha<\alpha'$, $h=\alpha'-\alpha$, $D=\theta_{\alpha'}-\theta_\alpha$, $\mathcal I=\int_\alpha^{\alpha'}M(\sigma)\,d\sigma=\log\frac{\zeta(\alpha)}{\zeta(\alpha')}$ where $M(\sigma)=-\zeta'(\sigma)/\zeta(\sigma)=\sum_n\Lambda(n)n^{-\sigma}$ ($\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function), $\arg\zeta(\sigma+it)=\operatorname{Im}\log\zeta(\sigma+it)$ with $\log\zeta(s)=\sum_n\Lambda(n)n^{-s}/\log n$, and $J=\sum_p(\arctan p^{-\alpha}-\arctan p^{-\alpha'})\le\mathcal I$ with the sum over primes $p$. Then $D(t)=\frac{h\pi}4+\arg\zeta(\alpha'+it)-\arg\zeta(\alpha+it)+O(1/t)$, so $|D(t)-\frac{h\pi}4|\le\mathcal I+O(1/t)$. Two sequences of zeros alternate if between any two consecutive zeros of either there is exactly one zero of the other. (i) If $[\frac{h\pi}4-\mathcal I,\frac{h\pi}4+\mathcal I]\subset(k\pi,(k+1)\pi)$ for an integer $k$, the zeros of $A_\alpha$ and $A_{\alpha'}$ alternate for large $t$, and so do those of $B_\alpha$ and $B_{\alpha'}$. (ii) If $[\frac{h\pi}4-\mathcal I,\frac{h\pi}4+\mathcal I]\subset(k\pi-\frac\pi2,k\pi+\frac\pi2)$ for an integer $k$, the zeros of $A_\alpha$ and $B_{\alpha'}$ alternate for large $t$, and so do those of $B_\alpha$ and $A_{\alpha'}$. (iii) If a multiple of $\pi$ lies in $(\frac{h\pi}4-J,\frac{h\pi}4+J)$, the zeros of $A_\alpha$ and $A_{\alpha'}$ fail to alternate at arbitrarily large $t$ (two consecutive zeros of one function with no zero of the other between them); if an odd multiple of $\frac\pi2$ does, so do those of $A_\alpha$ and $B_{\alpha'}$. The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson.

Source: [`ch/mi5.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi5.tex), label `mi:prop:pairs`.

<a id="zeros_of_the_real_part_of_xi_on_a_line_to_the_right_of_one_do_not_alternate_with_the_zeros_of_xi"></a>

### Non interlacing: the zeros of A_alpha and of the Bessel functions K do not alternate with the real zeros of Xi

Proposition 22.14.6, page 832 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $\Xi(t)=\xi(\frac12+it)$, $\vartheta$ the Riemann Siegel theta function, $N(T)=\frac{\vartheta(T)}\pi+1+S(T)$ the number of zeros $\gamma$ of $\Xi$ with $0<\gamma\le T$ and $S(T)=\frac1\pi\arg\zeta(\frac12+iT)$. (i) For $\alpha>1$, $A_\alpha(t)=\operatorname{Re}\xi(\alpha+it)$ has $N(T)-S(T)+O_\alpha(1)$ zeros in $(0,T]$; hence the zeros of $A_\alpha$ do not alternate with the real zeros of $\Xi$ for large $t$. (ii) For $a>0$ and $K_\nu$ the modified Bessel function of the second kind, $\operatorname{Re}K_{\frac94+\frac{it}2}(a)$ has $\frac T{2\pi}(\log\frac Ta-1)+O_a(1)$ zeros in $(0,T]$; hence two of these functions with different $a$ do not alternate for large $t$, and none alternates with the real zeros of $\Xi$ for large $t$ if $a\le2\pi$, or, under the Riemann Hypothesis, if $a>2\pi$. Alternation means that between any two consecutive zeros of either sequence there is exactly one zero of the other. The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson.

Source: [`ch/mi5.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi5.tex), label `mi:prop:noninter`.

<a id="collision_of_one_pair_of_zeros_under_a_vertical_random_average_is_decided_by_the_variance_and_the_kurtosis"></a>

### Collision of one pair of zeros under a random vertical average: the critical spread depends on the variance and the fourth moment

Proposition 22.14.8, page 834 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $G$ be a real entire function of order less than two, $a\in\mathbb{R}$ with $G(a)\ne0$, $\tau_j=G^{(j)}(a)/G(a)$ and $F_\eta(z)=((z-a)^2+\eta^2)G(z)$ for $\eta>0$. Let $\ell$ be a symmetric random variable, bounded or standard normal, with $\mathbb{E}\ell^2=1$ and fourth moment $m_4=\mathbb{E}\ell^4$, and put $d_c=\tau_1^2-\frac{m_4-1}2\tau_2$. For every $K>|d_c|$ there are $r>0$ and $\eta_0>0$ such that for $0<\eta<\eta_0$ and $s>0$ with $|s^2-\eta^2|\le K\eta^4$ the function $z\mapsto\mathbb{E}F_\eta(z+is\ell)$ has exactly two zeros in $|z-a|<r$, and there is $s_c$ with $s_c^2=\eta^2-d_c\,\eta^4+O(\eta^6)$ such that the two zeros are a nonreal conjugate pair for $s<s_c$, a double real zero at $a+\tau_1\eta^2+O(\eta^4)$ for $s=s_c$, and real and distinct for $s>s_c$. The result is from a note of Nicholas Polson.

Source: [`ch/mi5.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/mi5.tex), label `mi:prop:collision`.

## Chapter 23. Haseo Ki and the Thorin programme

<a id="after_any_positive_time_the_reciprocal_of_the_flowed_function_is_a_ggc_transform_up_to_a_rational_factor"></a>

### Eventually Thorin: after any positive time the reciprocal of the flowed Xi function is a GGC transform times a finite rational factor

Proposition 23.2.1, page 842 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. For real $t$ let $\Xi_t(\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{tu^2/4}\cos(\theta u)\,du$ be the de Bruijn Newman flow of Riemann's kernel $\Phi$ (so $\Xi_0=\Xi$, Riemann's Xi function). For every $t>0$ there are a finite, conjugation invariant multiset $E_t\subset\mathbb{C}\setminus(0,\infty)$ and a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) Laplace transform $L_t$, with discrete Thorin measure on $(0,\infty)$ whose atoms are simple beyond a finite level, such that $\Xi_t(0)/\Xi_t(i\sqrt s)=L_t(s)\prod_{\eta\in E_t}(1+s/\eta)^{-1}$. The function $\Xi_t$ has only real zeros exactly when $E_t=\emptyset$. (This is the theorem of Ki, Kim and Lee on the zeros of $\Xi_t$, written through the Thorin dictionary.)

Source: [`ch/ki1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ki1.tex), label `ki:prop:eventual`.

<a id="thorin_atoms_of_the_flowed_function_lie_right_of_a_shrinking_parabola"></a>

### Shrinking parabolas: Thorin atoms of the flowed Xi function lie to the right of a parabola that collapses at t = 1/2

Corollary 23.2.2, page 843 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. For real $t$ let $\Xi_t(\theta)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{tu^2/4}\cos(\theta u)\,du$ be the de Bruijn Newman flow of Riemann's kernel $\Phi$ (so $\Xi_0=\Xi$, Riemann's Xi function). For $0<t<\frac12$ put $\Delta(t)^2=\frac14-\frac t2$. Every Thorin atom of $\Xi_t$, that is every square of a zero of $\Xi_t$ and in particular every $\eta\in E_t$ of the eventually Thorin factorisation, lies in the closed region $\{x+iy:\ x\ge y^2/(4\Delta(t)^2)-\Delta(t)^2\}$ to the right of the parabola with focus $0$ and vertex $-\Delta(t)^2$. The parabolas are nested and collapse onto $[0,\infty)$ at $t=\frac12$, where de Bruijn's theorem takes over.

Source: [`ch/ki1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ki1.tex), label `ki:cor:parab`.

<a id="no_property_closed_under_a_gaussian_tilt_of_the_polya_density_can_imply_rh"></a>

### No slack in the Gaussian direction: no class of kernels closed under Gaussian damping and containing Phi has only real zeros

Proposition 23.2.3, page 843 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. Let $\mathcal K$ be a class of positive even kernels closed under $K\mapsto Ke^{-bu^2}$ for every $b>0$. If every $K\in\mathcal K$ has a Fourier transform with only real zeros, then $\Phi\notin\mathcal K$. (The proof uses the theorem of Rodgers and Tao, $\Lambda\ge0$, for the de Bruijn Newman constant $\Lambda$.)

Source: [`ch/ki1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ki1.tex), label `ki:prop:obstruction`.

<a id="reciprocals_of_derivatives_of_xi_converge_to_the_laplace_transform_of_the_brownian_exit_time"></a>

### Brownian exit time limit: the reciprocals of the even derivatives of Xi, rescaled, converge to 1 over cosh of the square root of 2s

Proposition 23.3.1, page 844 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. Let $X_n$ be the symmetric random variable with density proportional to $u^{2n}\Phi(u)$ and $m_n=\mathbb{E}|X_n|$, so that $\Xi^{(2n)}(\theta)/\Xi^{(2n)}(0)=\mathbb{E}\cos(\theta X_n)$ for the even derivatives of $\Xi$, and put $\psi_n(s)=\Xi^{(2n)}(0)/\Xi^{(2n)}(i\sqrt{2s}/m_n)=1/\mathbb{E}[\cosh(\sqrt{2s}X_n/m_n)]$. Then $\psi_n(s)\to1/\cosh\sqrt{2s}$ locally uniformly off the poles of the limit. The limit is $\mathbb{E}[e^{-sT}]$ for $T$ the exit time of standard Brownian motion from $(-1,1)$, a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) with Thorin measure $\sum_{k\ge1}\delta_{c_k^2/2}$, $c_k=(2k-1)\pi/2$. For each $K$ there is $n_K$ such that for $n\ge n_K$ the $K$ smallest Thorin atoms of $\psi_n$ are positive and simple and converge to $c_k^2/2$. If the Riemann Hypothesis holds, each $\psi_n$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC $T_n$ and $T_n\to T$ in law.

Source: [`ch/ki2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ki2.tex), label `ki:prop:bm`.

<a id="conjecture_on_the_edgeworth_rate_of_convergence_of_the_derivative_clocks"></a>

### Conjecture: the Edgeworth rate of convergence of the zeros and clocks of the derivatives of Xi

Remark 23.3.3, page 845 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Let $\Phi$ be Riemann's kernel, $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})e^{-\pi n^2e^{2u}}$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ and $\Phi$ is positive and even. With $X_n$ the symmetric variable of density proportional to $u^{2n}\Phi(u)$, $m_n=\mathbb{E}|X_n|$, $V_n=|X_n|-m_n$, $\sigma_n^2=\mathbb{E}V_n^2$, $\kappa_n=\mathbb{E}V_n^3$, $c_k=(2k-1)\pi/2$ and $\psi_n(s)=1/\mathbb{E}[\cosh(\sqrt{2s}X_n/m_n)]$, conjecturally, as $n\to\infty$ and for each fixed $k$, the $k$th positive zero $z_{k,n}$ of $\Xi^{(2n)}$ satisfies $z_{k,n}m_n=c_k+\frac{\kappa_nc_k^3}{6m_n^3}(1+o(1))$, and for every $S>0$, $\sup_{0\le s\le S}|\psi_n(s)-1/\cosh\sqrt{2s}|=\big(\sup_{x\le\sqrt{2S}}\frac{x^2}{2\cosh x}\big)\frac{\sigma_n^2}{m_n^2}(1+o(1))$. For $S\ge2.133$ the constant is $\max_xx^2/(2\cosh x)=0.53222$, attained at $x=2.06534$, the root of $\tanh x=2/x$ (computed).

Source: [`ch/ki2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ki2.tex), label `ki:conj:rate`.

## Chapter 24. Hitting times and the reciprocal xi function

<a id="grouped_residue_expansion_of_the_density_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law_with_no_hypothesis"></a>

### The density of the reciprocal xi law is the limit of grouped residue sums, with no hypothesis on the zeros

Theorem 24.1.1, page 854 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. There are radii $R_n\to\infty$ with $R_n\in[n,2n]$ such that for every $y>0$, $f(y)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{|u_\rho|<R_n}\operatorname{Res}_{u=u_\rho}e^{uy}/G(u)$, with no hypothesis on the zeros. A simple zero contributes $e^{u_\rho y}/G'(u_\rho)$, a zero of multiplicity $m$ contributes $e^{u_\rho y}P_\rho(y)$ with $P_\rho$ a polynomial of degree $m-1$, and a pair of zeros $\frac12\pm\delta+i\gamma$ off the line contributes $2\operatorname{Re}(e^{u_\rho y}/G'(u_\rho))$. For $y$ in a compact subset of $(0,\infty)$ the error after the $n$th group is at most $R_n\exp(-\frac12R_ny+C\sqrt{R_n}\log R_n)+\exp(-c\sqrt{R_n}\log R_n)$ for constants $c,C>0$.

Source: [`ch/ht1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht1.tex), label `ht:thm:grouped`.

<a id="absolutely_convergent_residue_series_for_the_density_given_a_lower_bound_for_xi_prime_at_zeros"></a>

### Residue expansion: absolute convergence of the density series given a lower bound for the derivative of xi at the zeros

Theorem 24.1.2, page 854 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Assume that the zeros of $\zeta$ are simple and that $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros (a hypothesis not known to hold). Then $f(y)=\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{u_\rho y}/G'(u_\rho)$, $y>0$, converges absolutely and locally uniformly. Under RH it reads $f(y)=\sum_{\gamma>0}w_\gamma e^{-\gamma^2y}$ with $w_\gamma=\gamma^2\prod_{\gamma'\ne\gamma}(1-\gamma^2/\gamma'^2)^{-1}$.

Source: [`ch/ht1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht1.tex), label `ht:thm:res`.

<a id="tail_of_the_density_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law_has_two_exponential_terms"></a>

### Upper tail of the density of the reciprocal xi law: two exponential terms and an explicit remainder

Proposition 24.1.3, page 855 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Let $c_3=\frac12(\gamma_2^2+\gamma_3^2)$. With no hypothesis, $f(y)=w_1e^{-\gamma_1^2y}+w_2e^{-\gamma_2^2y}+O(e^{-c_3y})$ as $y\to\infty$, with the same bound for each derivative, where $w_1=1.01635\times10^4>0$ and $w_2=-1.17754\times10^6<0$.

Source: [`ch/ht1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht1.tex), label `ht:prop:tail`.

<a id="kent_formula_is_the_residue_expansion_under_rh_with_simple_zeros"></a>

### Kent's eigenfunction expansion is the residue expansion under RH with simple zeros

Proposition 24.2.1, page 856 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. If RH holds and the zeros are simple, the residue series $\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{u_\rho y}/G'(u_\rho)$ is Kent's expansion with $\lambda_n=\gamma_n^2$, and $f$ is the density of the hitting time of a Krein string with Dirichlet spectrum $\{\gamma_n^2\}$. Without these hypotheses the grouped expansion is the formal continuation of Kent's formula to complex eigenvalues: an off line pair contributes $2\operatorname{Re}(e^{u_\rho y}/G'(u_\rho))$, a multiple zero contributes a polynomial times an exponential, and no string has such a spectrum.

Source: [`ch/ht1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht1.tex), label `ht:prop:kent`.

<a id="xi_of_one_half_plus_it_is_not_in_krein_class_and_the_partial_fraction_series_diverges"></a>

### The function xi(1/2+it) is not in Krein's class and the partial fraction series of 1/G diverges under RH

Proposition 24.2.2, page 857 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. The function $\xi(\frac12+it)$ does not belong to Krein's class, whether or not RH holds. Moreover, under RH the partial fraction series of $1/G$ over the points $u_\rho=-\gamma_n^2$ does not converge absolutely.

Source: [`ch/ht1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht1.tex), label `ht:prop:krein`.

<a id="rh_equivalent_to_weak_approximation_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law_by_ggc_laws"></a>

### RH holds if and only if the reciprocal xi law is a weak limit of GGC laws

Proposition 24.3.1, page 858 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. RH holds if and only if there are GGC laws, for instance hitting times of strings, converging weakly to $\mu$.

Source: [`ch/ht1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht1.tex), label `ht:prop:red`.

<a id="truncated_hadamard_product_laws_are_ggc_exactly_while_the_zeros_used_lie_on_the_line"></a>

### Truncations of the Hadamard product: GGC if and only if the first N zeros lie on the line, and GGC up to the verified height

Proposition 24.5.1, page 859 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Order the zeros in the upper half plane by height, let $G_N(u)=\prod_{n\le N}(1-u/u_{\rho_n})$, $\varphi_N=1/G_N$, $\varphi=1/G$, and let $\mu_N$ be the law with Laplace transform $\varphi_N$. (i) $\varphi_N\to\varphi$ pointwise on $[0,\infty)$, and for each fixed zero $1/G_N'(u_\rho)\to1/G'(u_\rho)$, with correction factor $\prod_{n>N}(1-u_\rho/u_{\rho_n})^{-1}\approx\exp(u_\rho\sum_{n>N}u_{\rho_n}^{-1})$, which under RH equals $\exp(\gamma^2\sum_{n>N}\gamma_n^{-2})>1$. (ii) $\mu_N$ is a GGC if and only if the first $N$ zeros lie on the line; in particular it is a GGC, unconditionally, for every $N\le N_0(H)$, the number of zeros below the verified height $H=3\cdot10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian). (iii) RH holds if and only if every $\mu_N$ is a GGC, and then $\mu$ is a GGC by Bondesson's continuity theorem. (iv) Under RH, for $u\ge0$, $0\le\log G(u)-\log G_N(u)\le u\,\tau_1(N)$ with $\tau_1(N)=\sum_{n>N}\gamma_n^{-2}\approx(\log(T_N/2\pi)+1)/(2\pi T_N)$, where $T_N$ is the height of the $N$th zero.

Source: [`ch/ht1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht1.tex), label `ht:prop:trunc`.

<a id="density_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law_is_log_concave_far_in_the_tail"></a>

### The density of the reciprocal xi law is strictly log concave on a half line, with no hypothesis

Theorem 24.5.2, page 861 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. There is $Y$ such that $f$ is strictly log concave on $[Y,\infty)$, with no hypothesis.

Source: [`ch/ht1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht1.tex), label `ht:thm:lctail`.

<a id="log_concavity_of_the_density_near_the_origin_given_the_saddle_point_approximation"></a>

### Log concavity of the reciprocal xi density near the origin, given the saddle point approximation

Proposition 24.5.3, page 861 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on the saddle point approximation of $\log f(y)$ holds as $y\to0$ together with two derivatives.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Let $\psi=\log G$, $\Lambda_f(y)=\sup_{u>0}(\psi(u)-uy)$ and $u_y$ the solution of $\psi'(u_y)=y$. Suppose the saddle point approximation $\log f(y)\approx-\Lambda_f(y)-\frac12\log(2\pi|\psi''(u_y)|)$ holds as $y\to0$ together with two derivatives (this is assumed, not proved). Then $f$ is strictly log concave on $(0,y_0]$ for some $y_0>0$.

Source: [`ch/ht1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht1.tex), label `ht:prop:lc0`.

<a id="explicit_truncation_error_for_the_density_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law_with_120_zeros"></a>

### The density of the reciprocal xi law is the sum of its first 120 residue terms up to an explicit exponentially small error

Proposition 24.5.4, page 862 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. With no hypothesis, for every $y>0$ and $j\ge0$, $|f^{(j)}(y)-\sum_{n\le120}w_n(-\gamma_n^2)^je^{-\gamma_n^2y}|\le M_je^{-cy}$, where $c$ is the constant of the book's contour shift beyond the 120th zero, $w_n$ and $\gamma_n$ are the weights and ordinates of the first $120$ zeros, and $M_j=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^\infty|{-c}+it|^j/|G(-c+it)|\,\mathrm dt$. Numerically $\log M_0=206.26$ and $M_{j+1}/M_j=1.0000185\,c$ for $j=0,1,2$ (computed).

Source: [`ch/ht1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht1.tex), label `ht:prop:explicit`.

<a id="density_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law_is_log_concave_from_0_008_given_computed_constants"></a>

### Log concavity of the reciprocal xi density on [0.008, infinity) from computed constants

Theorem 24.5.5, page 863 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Assume the values of the constants $M_j$, $j\le8$, of the explicit truncation bound for $f$ with its first $120$ residue terms (computed by quadrature). Then, with no hypothesis on the zeros, $f$ is strictly log concave on $[Y_*,\infty)$ with $Y_*=0.008$.

Source: [`ch/ht1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht1.tex), label `ht:thm:lc`.

<a id="hcm_density_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law_would_imply_ggc_and_rh"></a>

### If the density of the reciprocal xi law were HCM then RH would hold

Proposition 24.5.6, page 864 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. If the density $f$ of $\mu$ is HCM (hyperbolically completely monotone), then $\mu$ is a GGC and RH holds.

Source: [`ch/ht1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht1.tex), label `ht:prop:hcm`.

<a id="no_hcm_density_for_sums_of_exponentials_and_a_computed_zero_of_the_continued_density"></a>

### No HCM: sums of exponentials are not HCM, and the continued reciprocal xi density has a computed zero in the right half plane

Theorem 24.5.7, page 865 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on for part (ii), an explicit remainder bound for the omitted terms on a sector containing $z_*$.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. (i) No density of a sum of $n\ge2$ independent exponential variables with distinct rates is HCM. (ii) With the first $120$ terms of the residue series for $f$, the continuation of $f$ to $\operatorname{Re}z>0$ vanishes at $z_*=0.013831874754506+0.020001801712034\,i$ (computed). If the omitted terms are controlled by an explicit remainder bound on a sector containing $z_*$, this proves that $f$ is not HCM.

Source: [`ch/ht1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht1.tex), label `ht:thm:nohcm`.

<a id="jensen_laws_of_the_reciprocal_xi_function_exist_iff_rh_and_for_degrees_up_to_2e17"></a>

### Jensen polynomial laws mu_d of the reciprocal xi function: convergence, existence if and only if RH, and existence up to degree 2e17

Proposition 24.6.1, page 866 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. Write $G(u)=\sum_{k\ge0}c_ku^k$, so that $G(u)=\mathbb E\cosh(\sqrt u\,V)$ with $V$ symmetric with density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$ ($\Phi$ Riemann's kernel, $\Xi(z)=\xi(\frac12+iz)$) and $c_k=\mathbb E V^{2k}/(2k)!>0$. For $d\ge1$ let $J_d(u)=\sum_{k=0}^d\binom dk\frac{k!}{d^k}c_ku^k=\sum_{k=0}^dc_k\prod_{j<k}(1-\frac jd)u^k$ (up to scaling the Jensen polynomial of degree $d$ and shift $0$ of Griffin, Ono, Rolen and Zagier). (1) $J_d\to G$ uniformly on compact sets, without any hypothesis. (2) If $J_d$ has only real zeros, they are negative, $J_d(u)=\prod_{j\le d}(1+u/\ell_{d,j})$, and $1/J_d$ is the Laplace transform of the GGC law $\mu_d$ of $\sum_{j\le d}e_j/\ell_{d,j}$, the time a pure birth chain with rates $\ell_{d,1},\dots,\ell_{d,d}$ takes to pass through $d$ states. (3) RH holds if and only if $\mu_d$ exists for every $d$, and then $\mu_d\Rightarrow\mu$. (4) $\mu_d$ exists for every $d\le2\cdot10^{17}$, unconditionally (quoted from Griffin, Ono, Rolen and Zagier, who quote Chass\'e). (5) Every $\mu_d$ has the same mean $c_1$ as $\mu$, and its variance exceeds that of $\mu$ by $2c_2/d$.

Source: [`ch/ht2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht2.tex), label `ht:prop:jensen`.

<a id="b_spline_and_dirichlet_mean_form_of_the_density_of_a_sum_of_exponentials"></a>

### Density of a sum of independent exponentials as a Laplace transform of a B spline, the Dirichlet mean form

Proposition 24.7.1, page 871 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $0<\lambda_1<\dots<\lambda_N$, let $e_k$ be independent standard exponential variables and $f_N$ the density of $\sum_{k\le N}e_k/\lambda_k$. Then $f_N(y)=(\prod_{k\le N}\lambda_k)\frac{y^{N-1}}{(N-1)!}\int M(x;\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_N)e^{-xy}\,\mathrm dx$, where $M(\cdot;\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_N)$ is the Curry and Schoenberg B spline with knots $\lambda_k$, normalised to integral one. Equivalently $M$ is the density of the Dirichlet mean $D_N=\sum_kW_k\lambda_k$ with $(W_k)$ uniform on the simplex, and the formula is the case of Dirichlet parameter $N$ of the density formula of James, Roynette and Yor.

Source: [`ch/ht2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht2.tex), label `ht:prop:bspline`.

<a id="sum_of_exponentials_as_a_linear_functional_of_the_gumbel_extremal_process"></a>

### A sum of exponentials is a linear functional of the Gumbel extremal process

Theorem 24.7.2, page 872 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $e_k$ be independent standard exponential variables and $G_1>G_2>\cdots$ the points of the Gumbel extremal process of the book. For any $0<\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\le\cdots$ with $\sum1/\lambda_k<\infty$, and $b_k=k/\lambda_k$, $\sum_ke_k/\lambda_k\overset d=\sum_{k\ge1}b_k(G_k-G_{k+1})$, and if moreover $k\log k/\lambda_k\to0$ the series may be rearranged: $\sum_{k\ge1}b_k(G_k-G_{k+1})=b_1G_1+\sum_{k\ge2}(b_k-b_{k-1})G_k$. In particular, under RH, the reciprocal xi law $\mu$ is the law of $\sum_kk\gamma_k^{-2}(G_k-G_{k+1})$. For finite $N$ the truncation $\mu_N$ is the L statistic $\sum_{k\le N}b_k(e_{(N-k+1)}-e_{(N-k)})$ of $N$ exponentials, with $e_{(0)}=0$.

Source: [`ch/ht2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht2.tex), label `ht:thm:extremal`.

<a id="truncated_euler_products_give_ggc_laws_and_first_passage_decomposition_at_the_mean_level"></a>

### Truncated Euler products give GGC laws Y_P, and first passage to the mean level decomposes as Y_P plus the first passage to the log of N_P

Proposition 24.8.1, page 875 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. For $P\ge2$ let $\zeta_P(z)=\prod_{p\le P}(1-p^{-z})^{-1}$, fix $\alpha>0$, and let $N_P$ be the random integer with $\Pr(N_P=n)=n^{-\alpha}/\zeta_P(\alpha)$ for $n$ composed of primes up to $P$. Let $L=\log N_P$, $B_{\alpha,P}=\mathbb EL=\sum_{p\le P}\log p\,p^{-\alpha}/(1-p^{-\alpha})$, and $T_a$ the first passage time of standard Brownian motion to the level $a$. For every $\alpha>0$ and every $P$ the function $\Phi_{\alpha,P}(u)=e^{-B_{\alpha,P}\sqrt{2u}}/\mathbb Ee^{-\sqrt{2u}L}=\frac{\zeta_P(\alpha)}{\zeta_P(\alpha+\sqrt{2u})}e^{-B_{\alpha,P}\sqrt{2u}}$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC law $Y_P$ with zero drift, whose Thorin measure has density in the ordinate $\tau$ (atom positions $\tau^2/2$) equal to $\frac1\pi\sum_{p\le P}\sum_{k\ge1}\log p\,p^{-k\alpha}(1-\cos(k\tau\log p))\ge0$. In particular this holds on the critical line $\alpha=\frac12$, unconditionally. If $Y_P$ is independent of $N_P$ and of the Brownian motion, then $T_{\mathbb E\log N_P}\overset d=Y_P+T_{\log N_P}$.

Source: [`ch/ht2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht2.tex), label `ht:thm:trunc`.

<a id="one_prime_blocks_mobius_liouville_and_polya_gamma_laws"></a>

### One prime blocks, Möbius and Liouville factors and the Pólya Gamma law

Remark 24.8.2, page 876 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Fix a prime $p$, write $\ell=\log p$, $q=p^{-\alpha}$ with $\alpha>0$, $w=\sqrt{2u}$ and $\vartheta=\tau\ell$. For the Möbius (Euler factor) case the Thorin density of the one prime GGC is $\frac1\pi\sum_{k\ge1}\ell q^k(1-\cos k\vartheta)=\frac1\pi\frac{\ell q(1+q)(1-\cos\vartheta)}{(1-q)(1-2q\cos\vartheta+q^2)}$, which vanishes at $\tau=2\pi k/\ell$. For the Liouville factor, $\Phi^{+}_{p,\alpha}(u)=\frac{1+q}{1+qp^{-w}}\exp\big(-\frac{w\ell q}{1+q}\big)$ is, for every $\alpha>0$, the Laplace transform of a GGC with zero drift and Thorin density in the ordinate $\tau$ equal to $\frac1\pi\frac{\ell q(1-q)(1-\cos\vartheta)}{(1+q)(1+2q\cos\vartheta+q^2)}\ge0$, with bumps at $\tau=\pi(2k-1)/\ell$; the proof applies the sine squared lemma to the signed measure $\sum_k(-1)^{k+1}\ell q^k\delta_{k\ell}$, whose total variation is that of the Möbius case. As $\alpha\downarrow0$, $\Phi^{+}_{p,\alpha}(u)\to1/\cosh(\ell\sqrt{u/2})$, the Laplace transform of $\ell^2\omega$ with $\omega$ a Pólya Gamma variable $\mathrm{PG}(1,0)$, and the Thorin densities converge vaguely to $\sum_{k\ge1}\delta_{\pi(2k-1)/\ell}$. For $\alpha>1$ the products over all primes converge and give the GGC Laplace transforms $\frac{\zeta(\alpha)}{\zeta(\alpha+w)}e^{w\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(\alpha)}$ and $\frac{\zeta(2\alpha+2w)\zeta(\alpha)}{\zeta(\alpha+w)\zeta(2\alpha)}e^{wG_\lambda(\alpha)}$, with $G_\lambda(s)=\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(s)-2\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(2s)$, whose Thorin densities are $\pi^{-1}[\operatorname{Re}\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(\alpha+i\tau)-\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(\alpha)]$ and $\pi^{-1}[\operatorname{Re}G_\lambda(\alpha+i\tau)-G_\lambda(\alpha)]$. For $0<\alpha<1$ neither continued function is the Laplace transform of a probability law, whatever the zeros of $\zeta$ do: the first vanishes at $u=(1-\alpha)^2/2$, and the second, defined for $\alpha\ne\frac12$, vanishes there when $\frac12<\alpha<1$ and has a pole at $u=(\frac12-\alpha)^2/2$ when $0<\alpha<\frac12$. Credited to a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.

Source: [`ch/ht2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht2.tex), label `ht:rem:blocks`.

<a id="brownian_truncated_euler_product_identity_centred_at_one_half"></a>

### Brownian truncated Euler product identity for xi centred at one half

Theorem 24.8.3, page 878 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, $\gamma$ the zeros of $\xi(\frac12+iz)$ counted with multiplicity (so that $\frac12+i\gamma$ runs over the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$), $\gamma_1=14.1347\ldots$ the least ordinate of a zero, with $\operatorname{Re}\gamma^2\ge\gamma_1^2$ for every zero because zeros off the critical line have ordinate above $3\times10^{12}$, $T_x$ the first passage time of standard Brownian motion to the level $x>0$, $U>0$, and $s\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re}(s^2)>-\gamma_1^2$. Put $B_U(x,s)=\mathbb{E}[1-e^{-s^2T_x/2};T_x\le U]=\operatorname{erfc}\frac{x}{\sqrt{2U}}-\frac12\big[e^{-xs}\operatorname{erfc}\frac{x-sU}{\sqrt{2U}}+e^{xs}\operatorname{erfc}\frac{x+sU}{\sqrt{2U}}\big]$, $k_\infty(u)=e^{u/8}-\frac{\log\pi}{2\sqrt{2\pi u}}+\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^\infty e^{-ur^2/2}\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(\frac14+\frac{ir}2)dr$, $A_U(s)=\int_0^U(1-e^{-s^2u/2})k_\infty(u)\frac{du}u$, $R_U(s)=\sum_{\operatorname{Re}\gamma>0}[E_1(\frac{\gamma^2U}2)-E_1(\frac{(\gamma^2+s^2)U}2)]$ with $E_1(z)=\int_1^\infty e^{-zv}\frac{dv}v$, and $E_{p,U}(s)=\exp\big(\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{p^{-m/2}}mB_U(m\log p,s)\big)$. Then, with no hypothesis on the zeros, $\frac{\xi(1/2)}{\xi(1/2+s)}=e^{-A_U(s)}\prod_pE_{p,U}(s)e^{-R_U(s)}$, the product converging absolutely, and $|R_U(s)|\le\frac2Ue^{-m_sU/2}\sum_{\operatorname{Re}\gamma>0}\big(\frac1{\operatorname{Re}\gamma^2}+\frac1{\operatorname{Re}(\gamma^2+s^2)}\big)$ with $m_s=\gamma_1^2+\min(0,\operatorname{Re}(s^2))>0$. If moreover $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ and $\operatorname{Re}(s^2)\ge0$, then $E_{p,U}(s)\to(1-p^{-1/2-s})/(1-p^{-1/2})$ as $U\to\infty$. The proof uses the ordinate bound $3\times10^{12}$ for zeros off the critical line (Platt and Trudgian 2021). Credited to a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.

Source: [`ch/ht2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht2.tex), label `ht:thm:euler`.

<a id="universal_three_halves_stable_limit_of_the_euler_hitting_times"></a>

### The Euler hitting times converge after scaling to a spectrally positive stable law of index 3/2

Theorem 24.8.4, page 880 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Take $\alpha=\frac12$ in the truncated Euler product laws: $Y_P$ is the GGC law with transform $\zeta_P(\frac12)e^{-B\sqrt{2u}}/\zeta_P(\frac12+\sqrt{2u})$, $L_P=\log N_P$, $\kappa_j(P)$ the $j$th cumulant of $L_P$ (so $K_P(w)=\log\mathbb Ee^{-w(L_P-\mathbb EL_P)}=\sum_{p\le P}\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{p^{-m/2}}m(e^{-wm\log p}-1+wm\log p)$), and $\rho_j(P)=\kappa_j(P)/\kappa_3(P)^{j/3}$; $Y_P$ has mean $\kappa_2(P)=\operatorname{Var}L_P$. As $P\to\infty$, $Z_P=(Y_P-\kappa_2(P))/\kappa_3(P)^{2/3}\Rightarrow Z$, $\log\mathbb Ee^{-sZ}=(2s)^{3/2}/6$ for $\operatorname{Re}s\ge0$, a spectrally positive stable law of index $\frac32$. More precisely, for $\operatorname{Re}s\ge0$, $|\log\mathbb Ee^{-sZ_P}-(2s)^{3/2}/6|\le\frac{|s|^2}6\rho_4(P)$, and $\rho_4(P)\to0$.

Source: [`ch/ht2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht2.tex), label `ht:thm:32`.

<a id="brownian_truncated_euler_product_numerical_check"></a>

### Numerical check of the Brownian truncated Euler product identity

Table 24.8, page 880 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. For the Brownian truncated Euler product identity for $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+s)$ with truncation time $U$, the two sides $\log\frac{\xi(1/2+s)}{\xi(1/2)}$ and $A_U-\sum_p\log E_{p,U}$ were computed at $(s,U)=(0.1,0.05)$, $(0.1,1)$, $(0.49,0.05)$, $(0.49,1)$, $(2,1)$ and $(0.3+3i,0.25)$, with primes up to $10^3$ for $U\le0.25$ and $10^6$ for $U=1$ and the first $1700$ zeros for the zero remainder $R_U$ (the rest being bounded by the identity's own bound). The residual of the identity is below $10^{-30}$ in every row; at $U=0.05$ the zero remainder is visible (for example $3.39\times10^{-7}$ at $s=0.1$ against a bound of $1.25\times10^{-2}$) and at $U=1$ it is below the working precision of $30$ digits. This is a computation at these six points and says nothing about other $(s,U)$.

Source: [`ch/ht2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht2.tex), label `ht:tab:euler`.

<a id="thorin_rigidity_of_ggc_factorisations_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law"></a>

### Thorin rigidity: any factorisation of the reciprocal xi law into two GGC laws forces RH and splits the zeros

Theorem 24.9.1, page 881 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros, and for each zero in the upper half plane let $u_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ (equal to $-\gamma^2$ under the Riemann Hypothesis, RH). Let $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ (entire of order one half) and let $\mu$ be the law on $[0,\infty)$, the law of the clock $T$ of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$ and density $f$; $\mu$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if and only if RH holds, and then $T=\sum_{\gamma>0}e_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_\gamma$. Write $w_\gamma=1/G'(-\gamma^2)$ under RH, and $\gamma_1<\gamma_2<\gamma_3<\dots$ for the ordinates. If $\mu=\mu_1*\mu_2$ with $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ GGC laws, then RH holds and the Thorin measures are $U_1=\sum_{\gamma>0}a_\gamma\delta_{\gamma^2}$ and $U_2=\sum_{\gamma>0}(m_\gamma-a_\gamma)\delta_{\gamma^2}$ with $0\le a_\gamma\le m_\gamma$, where $m_\gamma$ is the multiplicity of the zero ($m_\gamma=1$ for simple zeros), and $\mu_1$ is the law of $\sum_\gamma g_\gamma/\gamma^2$ with independent gamma variables $g_\gamma$ of shapes $a_\gamma$. No GGC law with drift or with a nonzero absolutely continuous Thorin part is a GGC factor of $\mu$ with a GGC cofactor.

Source: [`ch/ht2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht2.tex), label `ht:thm:rigid`.

<a id="small_time_enclosure_of_the_boundary_of_the_reciprocal_xi_law_independent_of_rh"></a>

### Small time enclosure of the inverse first passage boundary of the reciprocal xi law, independent of RH

Proposition 24.12.1, page 884 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\mu$ be the reciprocal xi law of the book, with Laplace transform $1/G$, $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ over the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, and let $b$ be the boundary of the inverse first passage problem for $\mu$: $b$ is such that $\tau_b=\inf\{t>0:W_t\ge b(t)\}$ for a standard Brownian motion $W$ has law $\mu$.
