Write $F(t)=\mu(0,t]$ and $m(t)=\inf_{0<s\le t}b(s)$, and let $\Phi_{\mathrm N}$ be the standard normal distribution function, $\bar\Phi_{\mathrm N}=1-\Phi_{\mathrm N}$. For every $t>0$, $\sqrt t\,\bar\Phi_{\mathrm N}^{-1}(F(t))\le b(t)$ and $m(t)\le\sqrt t\,\bar\Phi_{\mathrm N}^{-1}(\frac12F(t))$. Moreover $-\log F(t)\sim(\log(1/t))^2/(16t)$ as $t\downarrow0$, so $\liminf_{t\downarrow0}b(t)/\log(1/t)\ge\frac1{2\sqrt2}$ and $\limsup_{t\downarrow0}m(t)/\log(1/t)\le\frac1{2\sqrt2}$, and if $b$ is nonincreasing near $0$ then $b(t)\sim\log(1/t)/(2\sqrt2)$. None of this depends on RH.

Source: [`ch/ht3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht3.tex), label `ht:prop:smallb`.

<a id="first_order_response_of_the_laplace_transform_to_moving_a_zero_off_the_line"></a>

### Moving a pair of zeros off the line by delta multiplies the Laplace transform by 1+6 delta^2 s/gamma^4 to first order

Proposition 24.12.2, page 887 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\mu$ be the reciprocal xi law, with Laplace transform $1/G$, $G(u)=\prod_{\gamma>0}(1-u/u_\rho)$ over the zeros of the Riemann zeta function (the control being the case of all zeros on the line). Moving the pair of zeros at height $\gamma$ off the line by $\delta$ multiplies the Laplace transform, relative to the control, by $1+6\delta^2s/\gamma^4+O(\delta^2s^2/\gamma^6)$ for $|s|\ll\gamma^2$. To first order this is the shift $\tau\mapsto\tau-6\delta^2/\gamma^4$ of the mean $\tau$.

Source: [`ch/ht3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht3.tex), label `ht:prop:resp`.

<a id="biane_pitman_yor_variable_gives_the_reciprocal_xi_law_as_a_harmonic_mean_of_cosh"></a>

### The reciprocal xi law as the reciprocal of an expected cosh under the size biased Biane Pitman Yor measure

Proposition 24.13.1, page 890 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $Y=\sqrt{2/\pi}(\max_ub_u-\min_ub_u)$ for a standard Brownian bridge $b$, so that $\mathbb EY^s=2\xi(s)$, and let $\tau$ be the clock with $\mathbb Ee^{-s\tau}=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$. Let $\mathbb P^*$ have density $Y^{1/2}/\mathbb EY^{1/2}$ with respect to $\mathbb P$ and let $U=\log Y$. Under $\mathbb P^*$ the variable $U$ is symmetric with density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$, where $\Xi(z)=\xi(\frac12+iz)$ and $\Phi$ is the kernel of Riemann and P\'olya; equivalently $U/2$ has density $2\Phi(2u)/\Xi(0)$. Moreover $\mathbb Ee^{-s\tau}=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)=1/\mathbb E^*\cosh(\sqrt sU)=1/\mathbb E^*[\mathbb E[e^{-sT}|U]^{-1}]$, where, given $U$, $T$ is the exit time of a standard Brownian motion from $(-|U|/\sqrt2,|U|/\sqrt2)$.

Source: [`ch/ht3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht3.tex), label `ht:prop:bpy`.

<a id="law_of_excursion_maximum_gives_the_biane_pitman_yor_identity_term_by_term"></a>

### The law of the maximum of a Brownian excursion gives the Biane, Pitman and Yor identity for xi term by term

Result 24.13.2, page 890 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $M$ be the maximum of a standard Brownian excursion, whose law is (Chung 1976; Kennedy 1976) $\mathbb{P}(M\le m)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}(1-4n^2m^2)e^{-2n^2m^2}$ for $m>0$, and $Y=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,M$, which has the law of $\sqrt{2/\pi}$ times the range of a Brownian bridge, by the path transformation of Vervaat. Let $\psi(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}e^{-\pi n^2x}$, $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$ and $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$. Then for $y>0$, $\mathbb{P}(Y>y)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi n^2y^2-1)e^{-\pi n^2y^2}$, $\mathbb{E}(Y-y)^+=2y\,\psi(y^2)$ and the density of $Y$ is $f_Y(y)=2\Phi(\log y)\,y^{-3/2}$. Hence $\mathbb{E}Y^s=2\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Phi(u)e^{(s-\frac12)u}\,du=2\xi(s)$ for every complex $s$, the identity of Biane, Pitman and Yor derived term by term from the law of $M$. With $y=e^u$, the function $k(u)=e^{-u/2}-2e^{u/2}\psi(e^{2u})$ equals $e^{-u/2}\,\mathbb{E}\min(Y,e^u)$ for $u\in\mathbb{R}$; its evenness is the case $g(y)=\min(1,e^u/y)$ of the size bias identity $\mathbb{E}g(1/Y)=\mathbb{E}\,Yg(Y)$ of Biane, Pitman and Yor, and its derivative at $0$ vanishes, which reads $\mathbb{P}(M>\sqrt{\pi/2})=\mathbb{P}(Y>1)=\frac12-\psi(1)=0.456783$ (computed). The derivation is from a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.

Source: [`ch/ht3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht3.tex), label `ht:res:chung`.

<a id="davenport_heilbronn_theta_function_is_positive_so_the_same_positive_structure_exists_without_rh"></a>

### The Davenport Heilbronn theta function is positive, giving a symmetric variable and a positive Polya kernel for a function violating RH

Proposition 24.13.3, page 891 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $a_n$ be the Davenport and Heilbronn coefficients, periodic modulo $5$ with $(a_0,\dots,a_4)=(0,1,\kappa,-\kappa,-1)$ and $\kappa=0.2840790438$, let $\xi_{DH}$ be the completed Davenport and Heilbronn function (a function with a functional equation and an off line zero, as in the book), and $\theta_{DH}(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nn\,e^{-\pi n^2x/5}$. Then $\theta_{DH}(x)>0$ for every $x>0$. Consequently there is a probability law on $(0,\infty)$ whose Mellin transform is a constant multiple of $\xi_{DH}$, a symmetric $U_{DH}$ with $\mathbb E^*e^{wU_{DH}}=\xi_{DH}(\frac12+w)/\xi_{DH}(\frac12)$, and a positive P\'olya kernel $\Phi_{DH}$.

Source: [`ch/ht3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht3.tex), label `ht:prop:dhtheta`.

<a id="wiener_gamma_representation_of_base_point_laws_and_rh_as_monotonicity_of_the_zero_counting_smoothing"></a>

### Wiener and Gamma representation of the base point laws, and RH as monotonicity of the smoothed zero counting functions N_alpha

Proposition 24.13.4, page 893 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. For $\alpha>\frac12$ let $\mu^{(\alpha)}$ be the base point law with Laplace transform $\xi(\alpha)/\xi(\alpha+\sqrt s)$ and $N_\alpha'(t)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\alpha+it)=\frac1\pi\sum_\rho\frac{\alpha-\beta}{(\alpha-\beta)^2+(t-\gamma)^2}$ ($\beta=\operatorname{Re}\rho$), $N_\alpha(0)=0$, and $h_\alpha(u)=N_\alpha^{-1}(u)^{-2}$. On one gamma process $\gamma$, set $X_\alpha=\int_0^\infty h_\alpha(u)\,\mathrm d\gamma_u$. Then $X_\alpha$ has law $\mu^{(\alpha)}$ for every $\alpha\ge\sup_\rho\operatorname{Re}\rho$, in particular for every $\alpha\ge1$. RH holds if and only if $N_\alpha$ is nondecreasing for every $\alpha>\frac12$.

Source: [`ch/ht3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht3.tex), label `ht:prop:wg`.

<a id="partial_complete_monotonicity_of_the_canonical_function_up_to_the_verified_height"></a>

### Partial complete monotonicity of the canonical function of the reciprocal xi law up to an order growing with x, from the verified zeros

Theorem 24.15.1, page 895 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\gamma_1$ be the first ordinate, $s_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ and $\Theta(x)=\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{s_\rho x}$ the canonical function of the reciprocal xi law. Let $T=3\cdot10^{12}$, so that every zero with $0<\gamma\le T$ is on the line (Platt and Trudgian). For every $x\ge1/T$ and every integer $0\le n\le\frac{(T^2-\gamma_1^2-1)x-5}{\log(T^2/\gamma_1^2)}$ we have $(-1)^n\Theta^{(n)}(x)>0$. Numerically the bound is $n\le1.7\cdot10^{23}x$. RH holds if and only if the bound can be replaced by $n<\infty$ for every $x>0$.

Source: [`ch/ht4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht4.tex), label `ht:thm:partialcm`.

<a id="quasi_riemann_hypothesis_equivalent_forms_through_the_prime_sum_and_base_point_laws"></a>

### Equivalent forms of the quasi Riemann hypothesis QRH(alpha) through the prime counting error, the prime Dirichlet series and the base point laws

Proposition 24.15.2, page 897 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Write $\mathrm{QRH}(\alpha)$ for the statement that every nontrivial zero of $\zeta$ has real part at most $\alpha$, $\frac12\le\alpha<1$. Let $\psi$ be the Chebyshev function, $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, and $\mu^{(\beta)}$ the base point law with Laplace transform $\xi(\beta)/\xi(\beta+\sqrt s)$. For $\frac12\le\alpha<1$ the following are equivalent. (1) $\mathrm{QRH}(\alpha)$. (2) $\psi(x)=x+O(x^{\alpha+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. (3) The Dirichlet series $D(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}(\Lambda(n)-1)n^{-s}$ converges for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$, so that $-\zeta'/\zeta=\zeta+D$ there. (4) $\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi(s)>0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha$. (5) The base point laws $\mu^{(\beta)}$ are GGCs, that is diffusion hitting times, for every $\beta>\alpha$.

Source: [`ch/ht4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht4.tex), label `ht:prop:qrh`.

<a id="reciprocal_xi_is_never_a_one_sided_or_two_sided_laplace_transform_of_a_positive_measure_in_the_translation_variable"></a>

### The function 1/xi(beta+w) is never a Laplace transform of a positive measure in w

Lemma 24.15.3, page 898 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function. For no real $\beta$ is $w\mapsto1/\xi(\beta+w)$ the one or two sided Laplace transform of a positive measure.

Source: [`ch/ht4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht4.tex), label `ht:lem:landau`.

<a id="prime_built_ggc_hitting_times_converge_to_the_base_point_laws_under_qrh_theta"></a>

### Prime built GGC hitting times converge to the base point laws for theta < beta < 2 - theta under QRH(theta)

Theorem 24.15.4, page 899 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on the quasi Riemann hypothesis QRH($\theta$) for some $\theta<1$ (every nontrivial zero has real part at most $\theta$).

Statement. Assume $\mathrm{QRH}(\theta)$ for some $\theta<1$ (every nontrivial zero of $\zeta$ has real part at most $\theta$) and let $\theta<\beta<2-\theta$. Let $w(u)=(1-u)_+^3$ with Mellin transform $W(z)=6/(z(z+1)(z+2)(z+3))$, and for $\beta>\theta$ let $d_X(t)=\frac1\pi(\operatorname{Re}A(\beta+it)-\operatorname{Re}\sum_{n\le X}\Lambda(n)n^{-\beta-it}(1-n/X)^3+\operatorname{Re}X^{1-\beta-it}W(1-\beta-it))$, where $A$ is the archimedean (gamma function) term of the explicit formula as defined in the book, so that $d_X$ uses only the primes up to $X$. Then $|d_X(t)-\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\xi'/\xi(\beta+it)|\ll_\beta X^{\theta-\beta}\log(t+2)$ uniformly in $t$, and there is $X_0(\beta,\theta)$ such that for $X\ge X_0$ the function $d_X$ is nonnegative. The GGC laws $\mu^{(\beta)}_X$ with Thorin density $d_X$ in the variable $z=t^2$ are then hitting times built from the primes up to $X$, and $\mu^{(\beta)}_X\Rightarrow\mu^{(\beta)}$ as $X\to\infty$, where $\mu^{(\beta)}$ has Laplace transform $\xi(\beta)/\xi(\beta+\sqrt s)$. Conversely, if for some $\beta$ and every $t$ the values $d_X(t)$ are nonnegative for all large $X$, then $\mathrm{QRH}(\beta)$ holds. The unconditional range $1<\beta<2$ is not covered.

Source: [`ch/ht4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht4.tex), label `ht:thm:primebuilt`.

<a id="coefficient_sequence_of_xi_is_a_polya_frequency_sequence_iff_rh_and_unconditionally_log_concave"></a>

### The Taylor coefficients of xi(1/2+sqrt s) are a Polya frequency sequence if and only if RH, and unconditionally PF2

Theorem 24.16.1, page 902 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $F(s)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)/\xi(\frac12)=\sum_{n\ge0}c_ns^n$, so that $c_n=\mathbb EV^{2n}/(2n)!>0$ for the symmetric variable $V$ with density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$ ($\Phi$ Riemann's kernel), $c_0=1$, and let $s_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ for the zeros $\rho$ of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane, with $\theta_\rho\in[0,\pi)$ the angle between $s_\rho$ and the negative real axis ($\theta_\rho=0$ for a zero on the line). A sequence is PF$_k$ if all minors of its Toeplitz matrix of order at most $k$ are nonnegative, and a P\'olya frequency (PF) sequence if it is PF$_k$ for every $k$. (i) RH holds if and only if $(c_n)$ is a P\'olya frequency sequence, that is, every minor of the Toeplitz matrix $(c_{i-j})$ is nonnegative. (ii) Unconditionally, $(c_n)$ is PF$_2$: $c_n^2\ge c_{n-1}c_{n+1}$ for all $n\ge1$.

Source: [`ch/ht5.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht5.tex), label `ht:thm:coef`.

<a id="three_term_sequence_is_pf_k_iff_the_angle_is_at_most_pi_over_k_plus_one"></a>

### A three term quadratic coefficient sequence is PF_k if and only if its angle is at most pi/(k+1)

Lemma 24.17.1, page 904 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. A sequence is PF$_k$ if all minors of order at most $k$ of its Toeplitz matrix are nonnegative. For $r>0$ and $0\le\theta<\pi$, the sequence $(1,\,2r^{-1}\cos\theta,\,r^{-2})$, the coefficient sequence of $(1+s/re^{i\theta})(1+s/re^{-i\theta})$, is PF$_k$ if and only if $\theta\le\pi/(k+1)$.

Source: [`ch/ht5.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht5.tex), label `ht:lem:three`.

<a id="angle_theorem_for_the_coefficients_of_xi_zeros_within_pi_over_k_plus_one_of_the_axis_give_pf_k"></a>

### Angle theorem: if every zero has angle at most pi/(k+1) then the coefficient sequence of xi is PF_k

Theorem 24.17.2, page 904 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $F(s)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)/\xi(\frac12)=\sum_{n\ge0}c_ns^n$, so that $c_n=\mathbb EV^{2n}/(2n)!>0$ for the symmetric variable $V$ with density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$ ($\Phi$ Riemann's kernel), $c_0=1$, and let $s_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ for the zeros $\rho$ of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane, with $\theta_\rho\in[0,\pi)$ the angle between $s_\rho$ and the negative real axis ($\theta_\rho=0$ for a zero on the line). A sequence is PF$_k$ if all minors of its Toeplitz matrix of order at most $k$ are nonnegative, and a P\'olya frequency (PF) sequence if it is PF$_k$ for every $k$. If every zero of $\zeta$ satisfies $\theta_\rho\le\pi/(k+1)$, then the Taylor coefficients $(c_n)$ of $F$ form a PF$_k$ sequence.

Source: [`ch/ht5.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht5.tex), label `ht:thm:angle`.

<a id="unconditional_pf_k_for_the_coefficients_of_xi_up_to_k_of_order_9e12"></a>

### Unconditional rung count: the coefficient sequence of xi is PF_k for every k up to about 9.4e12

Corollary 24.17.3, page 904 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be Riemann's xi function, $F(s)=\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)/\xi(\frac12)=\sum_{n\ge0}c_ns^n$, so that $c_n=\mathbb EV^{2n}/(2n)!>0$ for the symmetric variable $V$ with density $\Phi/\Xi(0)$ ($\Phi$ Riemann's kernel), $c_0=1$, and let $s_\rho=(\rho-\frac12)^2$ for the zeros $\rho$ of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane, with $\theta_\rho\in[0,\pi)$ the angle between $s_\rho$ and the negative real axis ($\theta_\rho=0$ for a zero on the line). A sequence is PF$_k$ if all minors of its Toeplitz matrix of order at most $k$ are nonnegative, and a P\'olya frequency (PF) sequence if it is PF$_k$ for every $k$. Unconditionally, $(c_n)$ is PF$_k$ for every $k\le\lfloor\pi H\rfloor-1=9424777960768$, where $H=3\cdot10^{12}$ is the height to which all zeros are known to lie on the line (Platt and Trudgian). More generally, $(c_n)$ is PF$_K$ as soon as every zero with $\gamma\le(K+1)/\pi$ lies on the line.

Source: [`ch/ht5.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ht5.tex), label `ht:cor:rungs`.

## Chapter 25. Extreme values, hitting times and a path to RH

<a id="gumbel_decomposition_of_each_term_of_the_theta_series_kernel"></a>

### Each term of the theta series kernel is an explicit combination of two Gumbel kernels of fractional order

Theorem 25.1.1, page 916 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\phi_n(u)$ with $\phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$ and let $g_k(x)=e^{-kx}\exp(-e^{-x})/\Gamma(k)$ be the density of $-\log G_k$ for a gamma variable $G_k$ of shape $k$. With $x=-4u-\log(\pi n^2)$, as densities in $x$, $\phi_n(u)\,du=\pi^{-1/4}n^{-1/2}\Gamma(\frac54)[\frac58g_{9/4}(x)-\frac34g_{5/4}(x)]\,dx$. The signed mass of the term is $-\frac18\pi^{-1/4}\Gamma(\frac54)n^{-1/2}$, and the formal sum of the masses, regularised by $\zeta$, is $-\frac18\pi^{-1/4}\Gamma(\frac54)\zeta(\frac12)=\frac14\xi(\frac12)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi$. With $s=(1+iz)/2$, $\int_{\mathbb R}\phi_n(u)e^{izu}\,du=\frac14n^{-s}\xi(s)/\zeta(s)$.

Source: [`ch/ev1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev1.tex), label `ev:thm:decomp`.

<a id="dyck_chain_polynomial_has_thirteen_zeros_left_of_the_line_below_height_sixty_at_n_25600"></a>

### Zeros of the Dirichlet polynomial of the Dyck chain at n equal to 25600 below height 60 (computed)

Result 25.1, page 918 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $H_n$ be the height of a uniform Dyck path of length $2n$, $Y_n=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,H_n/\sqrt{2n}$, $F_n(s)=\mathbb{E}Y_n^s$ (a Dirichlet polynomial in $s$), and $\gamma_k$ the positive ordinates of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma_k$ of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line. The number of Dyck paths of length $2n$ and height at most $h$ is $\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\big[\binom{2n}{n+k(h+2)}-\binom{2n}{n-1+k(h+2)}\big]$, out of $\binom{2n}{n}/(n+1)$. At $n=25600$, with these probabilities as balls at $256$ bits, the argument principle on the boundary of $-4<\operatorname{Re}s<6$, $0<\operatorname{Im}s<60$ counts $13$ zeros of $F_n$, in the bands $0<\operatorname{Im}s<20$, $20<\operatorname{Im}s<40$ and $40<\operatorname{Im}s<60$ the numbers $1$, $5$ and $7$ that the ordinates $\gamma_k$ have (there are $13$ of them below $60$). There is no zero with $\frac12<\operatorname{Re}s<6$ and $0<\operatorname{Im}s<60$, and the real parts of the $13$ zeros run from $0.0907$ (the highest, at height $59.126$) to $0.4553$ (the lowest, at height $14.072$). Followed in $n$ from $25600$ through $12800$, $6400$ and $3200$ down to $1600$, with Newton's method started at the zero found for the next larger $n$, the $13$ zeros stay distinct and to the left of the line, and the zero of lowest height lies at distance $0.3082$, $0.1544$ and $0.0773$ from $\frac12+i\gamma_1$ for $n=1600$, $6400$ and $25600$. The count is for $n=25600$ only: at $n=1600$ the same contour holds $14$ zeros. This is a computation and no proof for other $n$. The computation follows a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.

Source: [`ch/ev1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev1.tex), label `ev:res:dyckcensus`.

<a id="open_lattice_bias_expansion_of_dyck_chain_dirichlet_polynomial"></a>

### Lattice bias expansion of the Dirichlet polynomial of the Dyck chain (conjecture)

Conjecture 25.1.2, page 918 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Let $H_n$ be the height of a uniform Dyck path of length $2n$, $Y_n=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,H_n/\sqrt{2n}$, $F_n(s)=\mathbb{E}Y_n^s$, and $\xi$ the Riemann xi function. Conjecture (open): uniformly on every compact subset of $\operatorname{Re}s>0$, $F_n(s)=2\xi(s)-\frac{3s}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\xi(s-1)+O(1/n)$. At $s=1$ it says $\mathbb{E}H_n=\sqrt{\pi n}-\frac32+O(n^{-1/2})$, which agrees with the expansion of de Bruijn, Knuth and Rice, and it implies that $F_n\to2\xi$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$. The zeros computed for the chain agree with its consequence (computed). The conjecture follows a heuristic about the lattice of heights in a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.

Source: [`ch/ev1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev1.tex), label `ev:conj:lbias`.

<a id="dyck_chain_zeros_first_order_displacement_given_lattice_bias_conjecture"></a>

### First order displacement of the zeros of the Dyck chain polynomial from the zeros of xi (conditional)

Proposition 25.1.3, page 919 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on The lattice bias conjecture, that $F_n(s)=2\xi(s)-\frac{3s}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\xi(s-1)+O(1/n)$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$.

Statement. Let $F_n(s)=\mathbb{E}Y_n^s$ be the Dirichlet polynomial of the Dyck chain ($Y_n=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,H_n/\sqrt{2n}$, $H_n$ the height of a uniform Dyck path of length $2n$), $\xi$ the Riemann xi function and $\delta_n=3/(2\sqrt{2n})$. Assume that, uniformly on compact subsets of $\operatorname{Re}s>0$, $F_n(s)=2\xi(s)-\frac{3s}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\xi(s-1)+O(1/n)$. Let $\rho$ be a simple zero of $\xi$ and put $c_{\rm D}(\rho)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,\rho\,\xi(\rho-1)/\xi'(\rho)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,\rho\,\xi(2-\rho)/\xi'(\rho)$. There is a constant $C$ such that for all large $n$, $F_n$ has exactly one zero $z_n(\rho)$ in the disc $|s-\rho-\delta_nc_{\rm D}(\rho)|<C/n$; thus $z_n(\rho)=\rho+\delta_nc_{\rm D}(\rho)+O(1/n)$. The conditional statement is proved by Rouch\'e's theorem from the conjecture.

Source: [`ch/ev1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev1.tex), label `ev:prop:lbias`.

<a id="lattice_bias_coefficient_phase_formula_on_critical_line"></a>

### Phase formula for the lattice bias coefficient at a zero on the critical line

Proposition 25.1.4, page 919 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function, $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$, $\gamma>0$, a simple zero of $\zeta$ on the critical line, $Z$ the Hardy function with Riemann Siegel phase $\theta$ ($\zeta(\frac12+it)=e^{-i\theta(t)}Z(t)$), and $c_{\rm D}(\rho)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,\rho\,\xi(\rho-1)/\xi'(\rho)$. Then $c_{\rm D}(\rho)=-C_{\rm D}(\gamma)e^{-i\Theta(\gamma)}/Z'(\gamma)$ with $C_{\rm D}(\gamma)=\frac{\sqrt2}{\pi}\,|\frac32-i\gamma|\,\big|\Gamma(\frac34+\frac{i\gamma}2)/\Gamma(\frac14+\frac{i\gamma}2)\big|\,|\zeta(\frac32+i\gamma)|>0$ and $\Theta(\gamma)=\theta(\gamma)+\arctan\tanh\frac{\pi\gamma}2+\arg\zeta(\frac32+i\gamma)-\arctan\frac3{2\gamma}$, so that $\operatorname{Re}c_{\rm D}(\rho)$ has the sign of $-\cos\Theta(\gamma)/Z'(\gamma)$.

Source: [`ch/ev1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev1.tex), label `ev:prop:lbphase`.

<a id="lattice_bias_displacement_computed_first_200_zeros_and_zero_near_rho_64"></a>

### Lattice bias displacement of the Dyck chain zeros, computed for 200 zeros of xi and the zero near the 64th (computed)

Result 25.1, page 920 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $\rho_k=\frac12+i\gamma_k$ be the zeros of $\zeta$ on the critical line in order of height, $c_{\rm D}(\rho)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,\rho\,\xi(\rho-1)/\xi'(\rho)$, $\delta_n=3/(2\sqrt{2n})$, and $F_n(s)=\mathbb{E}Y_n^s$, with $Y_n=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,H_n/\sqrt{2n}$ and $H_n$ the height of a uniform Dyck path of length $2n$, the Dirichlet polynomial of the Dyck chain with zero $z_n(\rho_k)$ near $\rho_k$. In ball arithmetic, from the first $200$ zeros of a stored list, $\xi'(\rho_k)\ne0$ for every $k\le200$, $\operatorname{Re}c_{\rm D}(\rho_k)<0$ for every $k\le63$, $c_{\rm D}(\rho_1)=-6.72018-9.54303i$, $c_{\rm D}(\rho_{64})=53.08757-266.82638i$ (radius below $10^{-55}$), and among $k\le200$, $\operatorname{Re}c_{\rm D}(\rho_k)>0$ exactly for $k=64$, $92$, $115$, $126$, $136$, $160$, $165$, $183$ and $187$. At $n=6400$ and $25600$, Newton's method started at $\rho_k+\delta_nc_{\rm D}(\rho_k)$, $k\le13$, converges to the zeros of the census of $F_n$, each alone in a square of half side $0.25$ by the argument principle, and the distance $|z_n(\rho_k)-\rho_k-\delta_nc_{\rm D}(\rho_k)|$ falls by a factor between $3.77$ and $4.64$ from $n=6400$ to $n=25600$, for $11$ of the $13$ zeros between $3.94$ and $4.14$, as a remainder $O(1/n)$ predicts; for $\rho_1$ at $n=25600$ the law gives the real part $\frac12-0.04455$ against $\frac12-0.04470$. The zero of $F_n$ near $\rho_{64}$, followed from $n=10^8$ down to $10^5$, lies to the right of the line at every computed $n$: $\operatorname{Re}z_n(\rho_{64})-\frac12$ is $0.1615$, $0.1348$, $0.0837$, $0.0456$, $0.0223$, $0.0118$ and $0.0061$ at $n=10^5$, $3\cdot10^5$, $10^6$, $3\cdot10^6$, $10^7$, $3\cdot10^7$ and $10^8$, against the first order values $\delta_n\operatorname{Re}c_{\rm D}(\rho_{64})$ from $0.1781$ down to $0.00563$, and for $10^6\le n\le10^8$ the product $n\,|z_n(\rho_{64})-\rho_{64}-\delta_nc_{\rm D}(\rho_{64})|$ lies between $6.33\cdot10^4$ and $6.61\cdot10^4$. The first order regime needs $\delta_n|c_{\rm D}(\rho_{64})|$ small: $|c_{\rm D}(\rho_{64})|=272.1$, so this is $0.91$ at $n=10^5$ and $0.029$ at $n=10^8$. The neighbours $\rho_{63}$ and $\rho_{65}$ stay to the left, with real parts $\frac12-0.0283$ and $\frac12-0.0227$ at $n=10^8$. The computation uses Newton's method on ball enclosures of the exact law with the terms below $10^{-110}$ dropped and not bounded, checked against a second law with another cut, and uniqueness by the argument principle, sampled; it is a computation. The result follows a note of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.

Source: [`ch/ev1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev1.tex), label `ev:res:lbias`.

<a id="rh_equivalent_to_ggc_reciprocal_xi_law_and_to_the_existence_of_a_string"></a>

### All zeros of Xi are real if and only if the reciprocal xi law is a GGC, and real and simple if and only if it is the hitting time of a string

Corollary 25.3.1, page 922 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Xi$ be the Riemann Xi function, $\xi$ the Riemann xi function, $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\phi_n(u)$ with $\phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$ the theta series kernel, and $H(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$. Write $\pm\gamma_k$ for the zeros of $\Xi$, so that $\frac12+i\gamma_k$ are the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$, ordered by real part (under the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) they are all real and $0<\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\cdots$), $L(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)=H(0)/H(2i\sqrt s)$, which under RH equals $\prod_k(1+s/\gamma_k^2)^{-1}$, and $T$ for the random variable with Laplace transform $L$. Then the following are equivalent: all zeros of $\Xi$ are real (RH); $L$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) whose Thorin measure $\sum_k\delta_{\gamma_k^2}$ is positive. Moreover, all zeros of $\Xi$ are real and simple if and only if there is a Krein string with positive mass whose hitting time $T$ satisfies $\mathbb Ee^{-sT}=L(s)$. The same statements hold with $\widehat H$ and $\widehat L(s)=\widehat H(0)/\widehat H(2i\sqrt s)$ in place of $H$ and $L$, for $\widehat H$ an even real entire function of order less than two with $\widehat H(0)>0$.

Source: [`ch/ev1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev1.tex), label `ev:cor:rh`.

<a id="principal_eigenvalue_of_the_string_from_the_tail_of_the_hitting_time_under_rh"></a>

### Under RH with simple zeros the tail of the hitting time is a sum of exponentials and its excess is exponential with rate the first squared ordinate

Proposition 25.3.2, page 923 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on RH, simple zeros, and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$.

Statement. Let $\Xi$ be the Riemann Xi function, $\xi$ the Riemann xi function, $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\phi_n(u)$ with $\phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$ the theta series kernel, and $H(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$. Write $\pm\gamma_k$ for the zeros of $\Xi$, so that $\frac12+i\gamma_k$ are the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$, ordered by real part (under the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) they are all real and $0<\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\cdots$), $L(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)=H(0)/H(2i\sqrt s)$, which under RH equals $\prod_k(1+s/\gamma_k^2)^{-1}$, and $T$ for the random variable with Laplace transform $L$. If RH holds, the zeros are simple and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros $\rho$, then $\mathbb P(T>x)=\sum_kc_ke^{-\gamma_k^2x}$ with $c_k=\prod_{j\ne k}(1-\gamma_k^2/\gamma_j^2)^{-1}=2i\xi(\frac12)/(\gamma_k\xi'(\frac12+i\gamma_k))$. In particular the excess of $T$ over a high threshold is asymptotically exponential with rate $\lambda_1=\gamma_1^2$, the bottom of the spectrum of the string; this last clause needs only the two term tail, which has no hypothesis on $\xi'$.

Source: [`ch/ev1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev1.tex), label `ev:prop:tail`.

<a id="hankel_determinants_positive_if_and_only_if_all_zeros_of_a_candidate_kernel_are_real"></a>

### Hankel test: the zeros of an even entire kernel with infinitely many zeros are real if and only if two families of Hankel determinants are positive

Proposition 25.6.1, page 927 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\widehat H$ be an even real entire function of order less than two with $\widehat H(0)>0$ and infinitely many zeros $\pm\widehat\gamma_k$ (counted in the variable $s$ with $\widehat H(2i\sqrt s)=\widehat H(0)\prod_k(1+s/\widehat\gamma_k^2)$), let $\mu_j=\sum_k\widehat\gamma_k^{-2j}$ be the power sums of the inverse atoms (the cumulants of the candidate hitting time divided by $(j-1)!$), $w_k=\widehat\gamma_k^{-2}$, and assume $\sum_k|w_k|<\infty$. The zeros of $\widehat H$ are all real (and nonzero) if and only if all the Hankel determinants $D_n=\det[\mu_{i+j+1}]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}$ and $D_n'=\det[\mu_{i+j+2}]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}$, $n\ge1$, are positive.

Source: [`ch/ev1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev1.tex), label `ev:prop:hankel`.

<a id="height_rule_for_the_folded_kernels_reduces_rh_to_real_zeros_in_a_growing_disc"></a>

### If the folded kernels have only real zeros in the disc of radius 2c(N+1)^2 for every N then RH holds

Proposition 25.7.1, page 929 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi^F_N=\sum_{n\le N}\phi_n$ be the folded kernel and $H^F_N$ its cosine transform, $R_N=\Phi-\Phi^F_N=\sum_{n>N}\phi_n$ on $u\ge0$ and $E_N=H-H^F_N$, so that $E_N(z)=\int_0^\infty R_N(u)\cos(zu)\,du$, where $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\phi_n(u)$ with $\phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$, and $H(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$ with $\Xi$ the Riemann Xi function. Suppose there is $c>0$ such that for every $N\ge1$ all zeros of $H^F_N$ in the disc $|z|<2c(N+1)^2$ are real. Then RH holds. (The hypothesis, the height rule, is a heuristic balance of the kink against the size of $H$ and is verified in the book only for $N=1,\dots,4$ with $c=3.6$, by a Rouch\'e certificate, and for $N=5$ in floating point.)

Source: [`ch/ev2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev2.tex), label `ev:prop:reduction`.

<a id="kink_bound_for_the_error_of_the_folded_kernel_on_the_real_axis"></a>

### Kink bound: the error of the folded kernel decays like 1/x^2 with an explicit constant

Lemma 25.8.1, page 930 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi^F_N=\sum_{n\le N}\phi_n$ be the folded kernel and $H^F_N$ its cosine transform, $R_N=\Phi-\Phi^F_N=\sum_{n>N}\phi_n$ on $u\ge0$ and $E_N=H-H^F_N$, so that $E_N(z)=\int_0^\infty R_N(u)\cos(zu)\,du$, where $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\phi_n(u)$ with $\phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$, and $H(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$ with $\Xi$ the Riemann Xi function. For real $x\ne0$, $E_N(x)=-R_N'(0)/x^2-x^{-2}\int_0^\infty R_N''(u)\cos(xu)\,du$ and $|E_N(x)|\le B_N/x^2$ with $B_N=|R_N'(0)|+\|R_N''\|_{L^1(0,\infty)}$.

Source: [`ch/ev2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev2.tex), label `ev:lem:kink`.

<a id="rouche_certificate_that_the_folded_kernel_has_only_real_zeros_below_a_height"></a>

### Rouche certificate: a circle inequality and a sign change count show that all zeros of the folded kernel below a height are real

Proposition 25.8.2, page 930 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi^F_N=\sum_{n\le N}\phi_n$ be the folded kernel and $H^F_N$ its cosine transform, $R_N=\Phi-\Phi^F_N=\sum_{n>N}\phi_n$ on $u\ge0$ and $E_N=H-H^F_N$, so that $E_N(z)=\int_0^\infty R_N(u)\cos(zu)\,du$, where $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\phi_n(u)$ with $\phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$, and $H(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$ with $\Xi$ the Riemann Xi function. Let $\mathcal N(T)$ be the number of ordinates $\gamma\in(0,T)$ of nontrivial zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ of $\zeta$ and let $T$ lie strictly between two consecutive ordinates, and suppose $\Xi$ has exactly $2\mathcal N(T)$ zeros in $|w|<T$, all real and simple. If $|E_N(2Te^{i\vartheta})|<|H(2Te^{i\vartheta})|$ for $\vartheta\in[0,\pi/2]$, and $H^F_N(2x)$ has $\mathcal N(T)$ sign changes on $(0,T)$, then every zero of $H^F_N(2x)$ with $|x|<T$ is real. (In the book the inequality is certified in ball arithmetic for $N=1,2,3,4$ at $T=14.4,17.5$ ($N=1$), $31.7,35.3$ ($N=2$), $51.4,57.9$ ($N=3$), $86.1,97.3$ ($N=4$), given the count of zeros of $\Xi$ in the disc, and tested in floating point only for $N=5$.)

Source: [`ch/ev2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev2.tex), label `ev:prop:rouche`.

<a id="shifted_bessel_kernels_give_a_liouville_boundary_value_problem_with_rational_boundary_law"></a>

### Zeros of Re K_{mu+i nu}(a) for integer mu solve a Liouville problem with a rational spectral boundary condition

Theorem 25.8.3, page 932 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\mu\ge0$ be an integer, $a>0$ and $K$ the modified Bessel function. By the recurrence $K_{\nu+1}(x)=K_{\nu-1}(x)+(2\nu/x)K_\nu(x)$, $\operatorname{Re}K_{\mu+i\nu}(a)=A_\mu(\nu^2)K_{i\nu}(a)+B_\mu(\nu^2)\,aK_{i\nu}'(a)$ with real polynomials $A_\mu,B_\mu$. Hence at a point with $B_\mu(\nu^2)\ne0$, $\nu$ is a zero exactly when $g(\tau)=K_{i\nu}(ae^\tau)$ solves the Liouville problem $-g''+a^2e^{2\tau}g=\lambda g$, $\lambda=\nu^2$, with the spectral boundary condition $g'(0)=\beta_\mu(\lambda)g(0)$, $\beta_\mu=-A_\mu/B_\mu$. The first cases are Dirichlet for $\mu=0$, Neumann ($\beta_1=0$) for $\mu=1$, $\beta_2=a^2/2-\lambda$ and $\beta_3=4(a^2-3\lambda)/(a^2+8-4\lambda)$.

Source: [`ch/ev2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev2.tex), label `ev:thm:shift`.

<a id="extended_boundary_problem_is_self_adjoint_with_real_eigenvalues"></a>

### The boundary problem with a boundary law with a point mass and poles is self adjoint with real eigenvalues, positive under a sign condition

Proposition 25.8.4, page 932 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Consider the Liouville problem $-g''+a^2e^{2\tau}g=\lambda g$ on $(0,\infty)$ with boundary condition $g'(0)=\beta_\mu(\lambda)g(0)$. Suppose $\beta_\mu(\lambda)=\alpha-m\lambda-\sum_{j=1}^J\sigma_j/(q_j-\lambda)$ with $m\ge0$, $\sigma_j>0$ and $q_j$ real. Then the eigenvalue problem, away from the poles, is the eigenvalue problem of a self adjoint operator built from the Liouville operator on $(0,\infty)$ with a point mass $m$ at $0$ and $J$ extra coordinates $w_j$ coupled to $g(0)$, with stiffness $q_j$, unit mass and coupling $-\sqrt{\sigma_j}$. Its eigenvalues are real. If in addition the energy form is nonnegative, for example if every $q_j>0$ and $\alpha\ge\sum_j\sigma_j/q_j$, they are positive, so that the corresponding $\nu$ are real. This does not make the extended system a string: no hitting time is constructed for it.

Source: [`ch/ev2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev2.tex), label `ev:prop:ext`.

<a id="mean_of_the_de_bruijn_newman_hitting_time_increases_with_the_flow_time"></a>

### The mean of the candidate hitting time of the de Bruijn and Newman family increases in the flow time

Proposition 25.8.5, page 933 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$, so that $\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$, $H_t(z)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du$ and let $U$ have density proportional to $e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)$ on $(0,\infty)$. Let $T_t$ be the candidate hitting time, with Laplace transform $H_t(0)/H_t(2i\sqrt s)$. The mean of the candidate hitting time is $\mu_1(t)=\mathbb ET_t=2\mathbb E_t[U^2]$, and $d\mu_1/dt=2\operatorname{Var}_t(U^2)>0$. Equivalently $\mu_1(t)=\sum_k\gamma_k(t)^{-2}$, with $\pm2\gamma_k(t)$ the zeros of $H_t$ counted with multiplicity.

Source: [`ch/ev2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev2.tex), label `ev:prop:dbn`.

<a id="cotangent_law_for_the_boundary_law_of_the_shifted_bessel_kernels_with_fractional_shift"></a>

### Cotangent law: the boundary values of the shifted Bessel kernels grow like cot(pi mu/2) times sqrt(lambda_k)

Proposition 25.9.1, page 936 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on the asymptotic $K_{\mu+i\nu}(a)=\frac12\Gamma(\mu+i\nu)(a/2)^{-\mu-i\nu}(1+O((a/2\nu)^{2\mu}))$ for large $\nu$, used in a sketch with heuristic error terms (only the leading term, from the phase computation, is derived).

Statement. Let $a>0$, $\mu>0$ not an integer, $K$ the modified Bessel function of the second kind, $\nu_k$ the positive zeros of $\nu\mapsto\operatorname{Re}K_{\mu+i\nu}(a)$, $\lambda_k=\nu_k^2$ and $\beta_k=g'(0)/g(0)$ for $g(\tau)=K_{i\nu_k}(ae^\tau)$, that is $\beta_k=aK_{i\nu_k}'(a)/K_{i\nu_k}(a)$. As $k\to\infty$, $\beta_k=\cot(\pi\mu/2)\sqrt{\lambda_k}\,(1+O((a/2\nu_k)^{2\mu}))+O(1)$. The statement is proved by a sketch only for the leading term (the phase computation $\arg\Gamma(\mu+i\nu)-\nu\log(a/2)=\frac\pi2+k\pi$ with Stirling's formula); the error terms are heuristic. It matches every integer case of the shift theorem.

Source: [`ch/ev3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev3.tex), label `ev:prop:cot`.

<a id="signs_of_the_tail_coefficients_alternate_for_real_simple_atoms"></a>

### The coefficients of the tail expansion alternate in sign when the atoms are real and simple

Proposition 25.10.1, page 941 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\gamma_1^2<\gamma_2^2<\cdots$ be real and simple atoms and $c_k=\prod_{j\ne k}(1-\gamma_k^2/\gamma_j^2)^{-1}$. Then $\operatorname{sign}c_k=(-1)^{k-1}$.

Source: [`ch/ev4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev4.tex), label `ev:prop:sign`.

<a id="rh_equivalent_to_the_reciprocal_xi_law_being_a_polya_frequency_density"></a>

### RH holds if and only if the reciprocal xi law is a Polya frequency density

Corollary 25.10.4, page 942 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Xi$ be the Riemann Xi function, $\xi$ the Riemann xi function, $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\phi_n(u)$ with $\phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$ the theta series kernel, and $H(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$. Write $\pm\gamma_k$ for the zeros of $\Xi$, so that $\frac12+i\gamma_k$ are the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$, ordered by real part (under the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) they are all real and $0<\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\cdots$), $L(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)=H(0)/H(2i\sqrt s)$, which under RH equals $\prod_k(1+s/\gamma_k^2)^{-1}$, and $T$ for the random variable with Laplace transform $L$. Let $X$ have the law with Laplace transform $L$ (so $X=T$). Then RH holds if and only if $L(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)$ is the Laplace transform of a P\'olya frequency density. Under RH that density is log concave, the hazard rate of $X$ is increasing, and the mean excess function decreases monotonically, $e(0)=\sum_k\gamma_k^{-2}=0.0231050$ (computed) down to $e(\infty)=\gamma_1^{-2}=0.00500524$.

Source: [`ch/ev4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev4.tex), label `ev:cor:pf`.

<a id="expansion_of_the_mean_excess_function_with_exponential_rate_under_rh"></a>

### Mean excess function: two term expansion with an exponential rate under RH, simple zeros and a lower bound for xi prime

Proposition 25.10.5, page 943 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on RH (all zeros of $\Xi$ are real), all zeros simple, and $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$.

Statement. Let $\Xi$ be the Riemann Xi function, $\xi$ the Riemann xi function, $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}\phi_n(u)$ with $\phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$ the theta series kernel, and $H(z)=\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(zu)\,du=\frac18\Xi(z/2)$. Write $\pm\gamma_k$ for the zeros of $\Xi$, so that $\frac12+i\gamma_k$ are the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$, ordered by real part (under the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) they are all real and $0<\gamma_1\le\gamma_2\le\cdots$), $L(s)=\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)=H(0)/H(2i\sqrt s)$, which under RH equals $\prod_k(1+s/\gamma_k^2)^{-1}$, and $T$ for the random variable with Laplace transform $L$. Assume RH, that the zeros are simple and that $|\xi'(\rho)|\ge e^{-C|\gamma|}$ for some constant $C$ and all zeros $\rho$ (a hypothesis not known to hold), put $\lambda_k=\gamma_k^2$ and let $e(u)$ be the mean excess function of $X$ with $\mathbb P(X>x)=\sum_kc_ke^{-\lambda_kx}$. Then $e(u)=\sum_kc_ke^{-\lambda_ku}/\lambda_k\big/\sum_kc_ke^{-\lambda_ku}=\frac1{\lambda_1}+Ae^{-(\lambda_2-\lambda_1)u}+O(e^{-\min(\lambda_3-\lambda_1,\,2(\lambda_2-\lambda_1))u})$ with $A=\frac{c_2}{c_1}(\frac1{\lambda_2}-\frac1{\lambda_1})>0$. The excess law of $X$ over $u$ converges to the exponential law with rate $\lambda_1$ in total variation at rate $e^{-(\lambda_2-\lambda_1)u}$. Without simple zeros the two term form follows from the two term tail with $w_k/\lambda_k$ in place of $c_k$ for $k=1,2$.

Source: [`ch/ev4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev4.tex), label `ev:prop:meexp`.

<a id="dyck_chain_one_sided_approach_criterion_fails_for_t_above_gamma_64_conditionally"></a>

### One sided approach in the Dyck chain: the criterion implies RH, and conditionally on the lattice bias conjecture it fails for T above gamma 64

Result 10, page 947 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on The lattice bias conjecture, that $F_n(s)=2\xi(s)-\frac{3s}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\xi(s-1)+O(1/n)$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ (for the failure of the hypothesis).

Statement. Let $H_n$ be the height of a uniform Dyck path of length $2n$, $Y_n=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,H_n/\sqrt{2n}$, $F_n(s)=\mathbb{E}Y_n^s$ (a Dirichlet polynomial), $\xi$ the Riemann xi function, and $\rho_k=\frac12+i\gamma_k$ the zeros of $\xi$ on the critical line in order of height, with $\gamma_{64}=169.9119\ldots$. (1) Proved: if $F_n\to2\xi$ locally uniformly on $\operatorname{Re}s>0$ and, for every $T>0$, $F_n$ has no zero in $\frac12<\operatorname{Re}s<1$, $0<\operatorname{Im}s<T$ for all large $n$, then the Riemann Hypothesis holds: if it fails, the functional equation and the symmetry $\xi(\bar s)=\overline{\xi(s)}$ give a zero $\rho$ of $\xi$ with $\frac12<\operatorname{Re}\rho<1$ and $\operatorname{Im}\rho>0$, and by Hurwitz's theorem, for $T>\operatorname{Im}\rho$, $F_n$ has zeros in that rectangle for all large $n$. (2) Conditional on the conjecture that, uniformly on compact subsets of $\operatorname{Re}s>0$, $F_n(s)=2\xi(s)-\frac{3s}{\sqrt{\pi n}}\xi(s-1)+O(1/n)$: the zero free hypothesis holds for $T<\gamma_{64}$ and fails for every $T>\gamma_{64}$. The zeros of $\xi$ below height $170$ are $\rho_1,\dots,\rho_{64}$, simple and on the line. For $T>\gamma_{64}$ the zero $z_n(\rho_{64})$ of $F_n$ near $\rho_{64}$ tends to $\rho_{64}$ and has real part $\frac12+\delta_n\operatorname{Re}c_{\rm D}(\rho_{64})+O(1/n)>\frac12$ for large $n$, with $\delta_n=3/(2\sqrt{2n})$ and $c_{\rm D}(\rho)=\sqrt{2/\pi}\,\rho\,\xi(\rho-1)/\xi'(\rho)$, since $\operatorname{Re}c_{\rm D}(\rho_{64})>53.08$ (computed in ball arithmetic). For $T<\gamma_{64}$, $F_n\to2\xi$ uniformly on the closed rectangle, and the only zeros of $F_n$ near $\rho_1,\dots,\rho_{63}$ are to the left of the line for large $n$ because $\operatorname{Re}c_{\rm D}(\rho_k)<0$ (computed in ball arithmetic). So conditionally on the conjecture the hypothesis fails, and this criterion of one sided approach cannot prove RH along this chain. For $10^5\le n\le10^8$ the zero near $\rho_{64}$ lies to the right of the line (computed). Open: prove the conjecture, which would also give the locally uniform convergence of the first hypothesis. The implication and the argument are from notes of Nicholas Polson merged into the book.

Source: [`ch/ev4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/ev4.tex), label `ev:res:dyckside`.

## Chapter 26. Weil positivity as the Thorin condition

<a id="explicit_formula_for_the_heat_trace_agrees_with_zeros_to_all_printed_digits"></a>

### The heat trace computed from Gamma and the primes agrees with the sum over the first 1700 zeros

Result 26.1, page 952 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $\rho_j=\beta_j+i\tau_j$ with $\tau_j>0$ be the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function $\zeta$ in the upper half plane, counted with multiplicity (the zeros are closed under $\rho\mapsto1-\bar\rho$), let $\gamma_j=\tau_j+i(\frac12-\beta_j)$, so that $\rho_j=\frac12+i\gamma_j$ and $\gamma_j$ is real exactly when $\rho_j$ is on the critical line, let $\lambda_j=\gamma_j^2$, and let $W(t)=\sum_je^{-\lambda_jt}$ for $t>0$ be the heat trace of the zeros (absolutely convergent because the number of zeros of height at most $T$ is $O(T\log T)$). Let $g_t(u)=(4\pi t)^{-1/2}e^{-u^2/4t}$, $\psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma$, $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, $\mathcal A(t)=e^{t/4}-\frac12g_t(0)\log\pi+\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-tr^2}\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac{ir}2)\,dr$ and $\mathcal P(t)=\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}g_t(\log n)$, so that $W=\mathcal A-\mathcal P$ for every $t>0$ by the Guinand and Weil explicit formula. Computed with code/wt_heat.py at 110 digits: at each of $t=0.005,0.02,0.05,0.1,0.2$ the value $\mathcal A(t)-\mathcal P(t)$ equals $W(t)$ summed over the first 1700 zeros to $10^{-70}$ or better, with $W(0.005)=0.5371919640910408957$, $W(0.02)=0.018541291731319482254$, $W(0.05)=4.5878350485735742685\times10^{-5}$, $W(0.1)=2.1047997958223512845\times10^{-9}$ and $W(0.2)=4.4301821802236448843\times10^{-18}$. This is a computation, not an interval enclosure.

Source: [`ch/wt1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt1.tex), label `wt:res:check`.

<a id="weil_positivity_in_gaussian_form_is_the_thorin_condition_rh_iff_heat_trace_completely_monotone"></a>

### RH holds if and only if the heat trace of the zeros is completely monotone, if and only if the Thorin measure lies on the positive axis

Theorem 26.2.1, page 953 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\rho_j=\beta_j+i\tau_j$ with $\tau_j>0$ be the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function $\zeta$ in the upper half plane, counted with multiplicity (the zeros are closed under $\rho\mapsto1-\bar\rho$), let $\gamma_j=\tau_j+i(\frac12-\beta_j)$, so that $\rho_j=\frac12+i\gamma_j$ and $\gamma_j$ is real exactly when $\rho_j$ is on the critical line, let $\lambda_j=\gamma_j^2$, and let $W(t)=\sum_je^{-\lambda_jt}$ for $t>0$ be the heat trace of the zeros (absolutely convergent because the number of zeros of height at most $T$ is $O(T\log T)$). Let $g_t(u)=(4\pi t)^{-1/2}e^{-u^2/4t}$, $\psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma$, $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, $\mathcal A(t)=e^{t/4}-\frac12g_t(0)\log\pi+\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-tr^2}\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac{ir}2)\,dr$ and $\mathcal P(t)=\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}g_t(\log n)$, so that $W=\mathcal A-\mathcal P$ for every $t>0$ by the Guinand and Weil explicit formula. Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function, $U=\sum_j\delta_{\lambda_j}$ and $T$ the reciprocal Xi variable, the law (when it exists) with Laplace transform $\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+\sqrt s)=\prod_j(1+s/\lambda_j)^{-1}$. The following are equivalent: (i) the Riemann Hypothesis (RH); (ii) every $\lambda_j$ lies in $(0,\infty)$, that is, $U$ is supported on $(0,\infty)$ and $T$ is a generalised gamma convolution; (iii) $W$ is completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$, $(-1)^nW^{(n)}(t)\ge0$ for all $n\ge0$ and $t>0$; (iv) $\mathcal A-\mathcal P$ is completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$. The proof of (iii) implies (i) uses $S(s)=\sum_j(s+\lambda_j)^{-1}=\int_0^\infty e^{-sx}W(x)\,dx$ for real $s>\frac14$: if $W=\int e^{-ux}\mu(du)$ with $\mu\ge0$ (Bernstein), then $S(s)=\int(s+u)^{-1}\mu(du)$ is holomorphic off $(-\infty,0]$, while a pole $-\lambda_j$ outside $(-\infty,0]$ has residue the positive integer multiplicity of $\lambda_j$, so it cannot be removable; hence every $\lambda_j\ge0$, and $\operatorname{Im}\lambda_j=2\tau_j(\frac12-\beta_j)$ gives $\beta_j=\frac12$.

Source: [`ch/wt1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt1.tex), label `wt:thm:main`.

<a id="archimedean_part_of_the_heat_trace_is_u_times_a_gumbel_type_levy_density_of_order_one_quarter"></a>

### The archimedean part of the heat trace is a compensated integral against u times the Levy density of minus half the logarithm of a Gamma(1/4) variable

Result 26.3, page 954 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $g_t(u)=(4\pi t)^{-1/2}e^{-u^2/4t}$, $\psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma$, $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, $\mathcal A(t)=e^{t/4}-\frac12g_t(0)\log\pi+\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-tr^2}\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac{ir}2)\,dr$ and $\mathcal P(t)=\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}g_t(\log n)$, so that $\mathcal A-\mathcal P$ equals the heat trace of the zeros $W(t)=\sum_je^{-\lambda_jt}$ with $\lambda_j=-(\rho_j-\frac12)^2$ and $\rho_j$ the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane counted with multiplicity, for every $t>0$ by the Guinand and Weil explicit formula. Let $k(u)=e^{-u/2}/(1-e^{-2u})$ for $u>0$. Then $\mathcal A(t)=e^{t/4}+\frac12[\psi(\frac14)-\log\pi]\,g_t(0)+\int_0^\infty[g_t(0)-g_t(u)]\,k(u)\,du$, where the compensation $g_t(0)-g_t(u)=O(u^2)$ is essential because $k(u)\sim1/2u$ at the origin and $\int g_tk$ and $\int g_t(0)k$ diverge separately. Moreover $k(u)$ is $u$ times the Levy density $e^{-u/2}/(u(1-e^{-2u}))$ of $-\frac12\log G_{1/4}$ for $G_{1/4}$ with the Gamma$(\frac14)$ law, and more generally $-\frac12\log G_a$ has Levy density $e^{-2au}/(u(1-e^{-2u}))$ on $u>0$, with compensation. The prime part is $\mathcal P(t)=\int_0^\infty e^{-u/2}g_t(u)\,d\psi_{\mathrm C}(e^u)$ with the atom at $u=0$ left out, where $\psi_{\mathrm C}(y)=\sum_{n\le y}\Lambda(n)$.

Source: [`ch/wt1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt1.tex), label `wt:res:acomp`.

<a id="prime_part_of_the_heat_trace_is_a_weighted_series_of_frechet_distribution_functions_governed_by_the_prime_2"></a>

### The prime part is a positive weighted series of Frechet distribution functions and for small t is governed by the prime 2

Result 26.3, page 955 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $g_t(u)=(4\pi t)^{-1/2}e^{-u^2/4t}$, $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function and $\mathcal P(t)=\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}g_t(\log n)$. With $\Phi_1(y)=e^{-1/y}$ the Frechet distribution function of index one, $\mathcal P(t)=(4\pi t)^{-1/2}\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}\Phi_1(4t/(\log n)^2)$, a positive weighted series of Frechet distribution functions with scales $(\log n)^2/4$; the weights are not summable ($\sum_{n\le N}\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}\sim2\sqrt N$), so it is not a probability mixture. As $t\downarrow0$, $\mathcal P(t)=\frac{\log2}{\sqrt{8\pi t}}\exp[-(\log2)^2/4t]\{1+O(\exp[-((\log3)^2-(\log2)^2)/4t])\}$, by isolating $n=2$ and factoring out the exponential of the term $n=3$.

Source: [`ch/wt1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt1.tex), label `wt:res:frechet`.

<a id="first_sign_changes_of_the_archimedean_derivatives_for_orders_one_to_six_computed"></a>

### Computed first sign changes of the derivatives of the archimedean part for orders one to six

Result 26.4.1, page 957 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $\psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma$ and $w(\lambda)=\big(\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac i2\sqrt\lambda)-\log\pi\big)/(4\pi\sqrt\lambda)$ for $\lambda>0$, so that $\mathcal A(t)=e^{t/4}+\int_0^\infty e^{-\lambda t}w(\lambda)\,d\lambda$, let $\lambda_*=r_*^2$ where $r_*=6.28984$ is the unique positive root of $\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac{ir}2)=\log\pi$ (the critical point of the Riemann Siegel theta function), and let $D_n(t)=(-1)^n\mathcal A^{(n)}(t)=(-\frac14)^ne^{t/4}+\int_0^\infty\lambda^ne^{-\lambda t}w(\lambda)\,d\lambda$. Computed by bisection at 35 and 45 digits (code/wt_window.py, the two runs agree): the first sign change $t_n$ of $D_n=(-1)^n\mathcal A^{(n)}$ is $0.025332$, $0.051040$, $0.076135$, $0.101334$, $0.126561$, $0.151805$ for $n=1,\dots,6$, against $n/\lambda_*=0.025277$, $0.050554$, $0.075830$, $0.101107$, $0.126384$, $0.151661$ with $\lambda_*=39.5620$, a relative deviation of $0.22\%,0.96\%,0.40\%,0.22\%,0.14\%,0.095\%$. Since $t_1<\dots<t_6$, the conditions of all orders up to $n$ hold together for $\mathcal A$ only on $(0,t_1]$. For $n=2,4,6$ a scan on $[0.005,7]$ finds a second sign change at $1.3612$, $3.2456$ and $5.2669$.

Source: [`ch/wt1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt1.tex), label `wt:res:window`.

<a id="spectral_density_of_the_archimedean_part_changes_sign_exactly_once_at_the_square_of_the_critical_point_of_theta"></a>

### The spectral density of the archimedean part has exactly one sign change, at the square of the critical point of the Riemann Siegel theta function

Lemma 26.8.1, page 960 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma$ and $w(\lambda)=\big(\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac i2\sqrt\lambda)-\log\pi\big)/(4\pi\sqrt\lambda)$ for $\lambda>0$. Then $w$ has exactly one sign change on $(0,\infty)$, from negative to positive, at $\lambda_*=r_*^2$ with $r_*=6.28984$ the unique positive root of $\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac{ir}2)=\log\pi$, and $w'(\lambda_*)>0$. The reason is that $r\mapsto\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac{ir}2)$ increases strictly from $\psi(\frac14)=-4.227$ to $+\infty$, since $\operatorname{Im}\psi'(\frac14+\frac{ir}2)=-\sum_{k\ge0}(\frac14+k)r|z+k|^{-4}<0$ for $r>0$ with $z=\frac14+\frac{ir}2$.

Source: [`ch/wt2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt2.tex), label `wt:lem:w`.

<a id="first_sign_change_of_the_derivatives_of_the_archimedean_part_lies_near_n_over_lambda_star"></a>

### Sign structure of the derivatives of the archimedean part: one sign change for odd order, at most two for even order, and a first change near n over lambda star

Proposition 26.8.2, page 960 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma$ and $w(\lambda)=\big(\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac i2\sqrt\lambda)-\log\pi\big)/(4\pi\sqrt\lambda)$ for $\lambda>0$, so that $\mathcal A(t)=e^{t/4}+\int_0^\infty e^{-\lambda t}w(\lambda)\,d\lambda$, let $\lambda_*=r_*^2$ where $r_*=6.28984$ is the unique positive root of $\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac{ir}2)=\log\pi$ (the critical point of the Riemann Siegel theta function), and let $D_n(t)=(-1)^n\mathcal A^{(n)}(t)=(-\frac14)^ne^{t/4}+\int_0^\infty\lambda^ne^{-\lambda t}w(\lambda)\,d\lambda$. For every $n\ge1$, $D_n(t)>0$ for small $t>0$. For odd $n$, $D_n$ has exactly one sign change on $(0,\infty)$, at a point $t_n$, and is negative after it. For even $n$, $D_n$ has at most two sign changes and is positive for large $t$; if it has two, the first is $t_n$ and the second lies where the atom $4^{-n}e^{t/4}$ overtakes the negative part of the density. As $n\to\infty$ a first sign change $t_n$ exists and $t_n=n/\lambda_*+O(1)$. The existence of a first sign change for even $n$ is proved only for $n$ large; it is computed for $n=2,4,6$.

Source: [`ch/wt2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt2.tex), label `wt:prop:window`.

<a id="prime_by_prime_window_law_for_the_order_one_positivity_of_the_truncated_prime_part"></a>

### Prime by prime window law: omitting the prime powers from q on ends the order one window near log q over twice the first ordinate

Result 26.8.2, page 961 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $\gamma_1=14.134725\ldots$ be the ordinate of the first nontrivial zero of $\zeta$, $g_t(u)=(4\pi t)^{-1/2}e^{-u^2/4t}$, $\psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma$, $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, $\mathcal A(t)=e^{t/4}-\frac12g_t(0)\log\pi+\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-tr^2}\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac{ir}2)\,dr$ and $\mathcal P(t)=\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}g_t(\log n)$, so that $\mathcal A-\mathcal P$ is the heat trace of the zeros $W(t)=\sum_je^{-\lambda_jt}$ with $\lambda_j=-(\rho_j-\frac12)^2$ and $\rho_j$ the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane counted with multiplicity, by the Guinand and Weil explicit formula, $\mathcal P_S$ the prime part restricted to all powers of the primes in a finite set $S$, $q$ the smallest prime power not generated by $S$, and $t_n(S)$ the first point where $(-1)^n(\mathcal A-\mathcal P_S)^{(n)}$ fails to be positive. A heuristic balance of the exponents $e^{-(\log q)^2/4t}$ and $e^{-\gamma_1^2t}$ gives $t(S)\approx\log q/2\gamma_1$. Computed (code/wt_window.py, scan to $0.8$): $t_1(S)=0.0253,0.0394,0.0575,0.0696,0.0856,0.1010,0.1289,0.1635$ for $S=\emptyset,\{2\},\{2,3\}$, primes up to $5,7,13,31,97$, against $\log q/2\gamma_1=0.0245,0.0389,0.0569,0.0688,0.0848,0.1002,0.1277,0.1633$ for $q=2,3,5,7,11,17,37,101$. This is an empirical law for this truncation scheme, not a theorem: coefficients, derivative polynomials, the other zeros and the other omitted prime powers contribute corrections for which no uniform bound is given.

Source: [`ch/wt2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt2.tex), label `wt:res:law`.

<a id="rigidity_of_the_prime_point_process_variance_in_short_intervals_follows_the_gue_prediction_computed"></a>

### Computed short interval variance of the prime sum follows the GUE prediction and not the Poisson level

Result 26.8.3, page 963 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $\psi_{\mathrm C}(y)=\sum_{n\le y}\Lambda(n)$ and $V_\delta=\frac1{b-a}\int_a^b[\psi_{\mathrm C}((1+\delta)y)-\psi_{\mathrm C}(y)-\delta y]^2/(\delta y)\,dy$ with $[a,b]=[10^6,10^7]$. The GUE prediction transported to the primes is $\log(1/\delta)+1-\gamma_E-\log2\pi$, with $\gamma_E$ Euler's constant, and a Poisson process of the same intensity such as the Cram\'er model gives about $\log y-1$, averaged over the range $14.37$. Computed (code/wt_rig.py, random points and a sieve to $2.1\times10^7$, standard errors $0.003$ to $0.03$): for $\delta=10^{-5},10^{-4},10^{-3},3\times10^{-3},10^{-2},10^{-1}$ the primes give $10.13,7.71,5.32,4.04,3.22,1.10$ against the GUE values $10.10,7.80,5.49,4.39,3.19,0.89$, while one realisation of the Cram\'er model gives $14.40,14.53,14.60,14.81,14.76,14.55$. This compares finite numerical results with a conjectural variance prediction (Goldston and Montgomery, under RH); it does not establish GUE statistics for the primes.

Source: [`ch/wt2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt2.tex), label `wt:res:rig`.

<a id="window_law_for_the_archimedean_part_with_explicit_constants_beta_and_delta"></a>

### Window law: the first sign change of the derivatives of the archimedean part is n over lambda star plus beta plus delta over n plus O of n to the minus two

Proposition 26.9.1, page 965 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma$ and $w(\lambda)=\big(\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac i2\sqrt\lambda)-\log\pi\big)/(4\pi\sqrt\lambda)$ for $\lambda>0$, so that $\mathcal A(t)=e^{t/4}+\int_0^\infty e^{-\lambda t}w(\lambda)\,d\lambda$, let $\lambda_*=r_*^2$ where $r_*=6.28984$ is the unique positive root of $\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac{ir}2)=\log\pi$ (the critical point of the Riemann Siegel theta function), and let $D_n(t)=(-1)^n\mathcal A^{(n)}(t)=(-\frac14)^ne^{t/4}+\int_0^\infty\lambda^ne^{-\lambda t}w(\lambda)\,d\lambda$. Put $A_1(c)=c\,w'(c)+\frac12c^2w''(c)$, $A_2(c)=c^2w''(c)+\frac56c^3w'''(c)+\frac18c^4w^{(4)}(c)$, $\alpha=-A_1(\lambda_*)/w'(\lambda_*)$ and $\eta=-[\frac12w''(\lambda_*)\alpha^2+A_1'(\lambda_*)\alpha+A_2(\lambda_*)]/w'(\lambda_*)$. The first sign change $t_n$ of $D_n$ satisfies $t_n=n/\lambda_*+\beta+\delta/n+O(n^{-2})$ with $\beta=\lambda_*^{-1}\big(1+\lambda_*w''(\lambda_*)/(2w'(\lambda_*))\big)$ and $\delta=\alpha^2/\lambda_*^3-\eta/\lambda_*^2$. The proof expands $\mathbb E\,w(cT_n)$, with $T_n$ of gamma law of shape $n+1$ and rate $n$, in powers of $1/n$ and shows that the atom term is exponentially small near $\lambda_*$. The numerical value of $\delta$ is not entered here because no script of the book evaluated it.

Source: [`ch/wt3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt3.tex), label `wt:prop:expansion`.

<a id="one_sided_certificates_for_the_heat_trace_from_finitely_many_primes"></a>

### One sided certificates: a first derivative bound with no tail estimate and a second derivative bound with the Rosser and Schoenfeld tail

Proposition 26.9.2, page 966 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $g_t(u)=(4\pi t)^{-1/2}e^{-u^2/4t}$, $\psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma$, $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, $\mathcal A(t)=e^{t/4}-\frac12g_t(0)\log\pi+\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-tr^2}\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac{ir}2)\,dr$, $\mathcal P(t)=\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}g_t(\log n)$ and $W=\mathcal A-\mathcal P$, which by the Guinand and Weil explicit formula is the heat trace $W(t)=\sum_je^{-\lambda_jt}$ with $\lambda_j=-(\rho_j-\frac12)^2$ and $\rho_j$ the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane counted with multiplicity; let $\psi_{\mathrm C}(y)=\sum_{n\le y}\Lambda(n)$, $\mathcal P_S$ the prime part over the prime powers generated by a finite set $S$ of primes, and $q$ the smallest omitted prime power, so that $W=(\mathcal A-\mathcal P_S)-\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rest}}$ with $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{rest}}$ the sum over the omitted prime powers, all at least $q$. (1) For $t<(\log q)^2/2$, $-W'(t)\ge-(\mathcal A-\mathcal P_S)'(t)$; hence if $\mathcal A-\mathcal P_S$ is decreasing on $(0,X]$ with $X<(\log q)^2/2$, so is $W$, with no tail estimate. (2) Let $S$ be all prime powers up to $N_0$, so that $\mathcal P_S=\mathcal P_{\le N_0}=\sum_{2\le n\le N_0}\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}g_t(\log n)$, and let $f(y)=y^{-1/2}\partial_t^2g_t(\log y)$ be nonnegative and decreasing on $(N_0,\infty)$. Then, by the Rosser and Schoenfeld bound $\psi_{\mathrm C}(y)<1.03883y$, $W''(t)\ge(\mathcal A-\mathcal P_{\le N_0})''(t)-1.03883\big(N_0f(N_0)+\int_{\log N_0}^\infty e^{u/2}\partial_t^2g_t(u)\,du\big)$, and the hypotheses on $f$ hold for every $0<t\le X$ as soon as $X\le(\log N_0)^2/[2(5+\sqrt{10})]$.

Source: [`ch/wt3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt3.tex), label `wt:prop:cert`.

<a id="windows_for_positive_second_derivative_of_the_heat_trace_from_the_certificate_bound_computed_on_a_grid"></a>

### Windows for the positivity of the second derivative of the heat trace suggested by the certificate bound (not certified)

Result 26.9.2, page 966 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $W''$ be the second derivative of the heat trace of the zeros and let the lower bound for $W''(t)$ be $(\mathcal A-\mathcal P_{\le N_0})''(t)-1.03883\big(N_0f(N_0)+\int_{\log N_0}^\infty e^{u/2}\partial_t^2g_t(u)\,du\big)$, where $W=\mathcal A-\mathcal P$ is the explicit formula for the heat trace with archimedean part $\mathcal A$, $\mathcal P_{\le N_0}(t)=\sum_{2\le n\le N_0}\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}g_t(\log n)$ is the prime part up to $N_0$, $g_t(u)=(4\pi t)^{-1/2}e^{-u^2/4t}$, $f(y)=y^{-1/2}\partial_t^2g_t(\log y)$, and $1.03883$ is the Rosser and Schoenfeld constant in $\sum_{n\le y}\Lambda(n)<1.03883y$. Computed at 30 digits on the geometric grid $t=0.01\cdot1.08^k$ (code/wt_window.py), the bound stays positive up to $t=0.0740$ for $N_0=10$, $0.1479$ for $N_0=100$ and $0.2346$ for $N_0=1000$, which falls short of the law $\log q/2\gamma_1$, with $\gamma_1=14.134725\ldots$ the ordinate of the first nontrivial zero of $\zeta$ and $q$ the first omitted prime power ($0.0848,0.1633,0.2447$ for $q=11,101,1009$) by $12.8\%$, $9.4\%$ and $4.1\%$. These are not certified windows: floating point positivity at grid points proves neither the signs of the computed quantities nor positivity between the points, and the range $0<t<0.01$ is not covered.

Source: [`ch/wt3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt3.tex), label `wt:res:cert`.

<a id="heat_trace_is_a_gaussian_smoothing_of_the_normalised_prime_error_with_no_hypothesis"></a>

### The heat trace is the sum of an explicit archimedean quantity and a Gaussian derivative smoothing of the normalised prime error

Proposition 26.9.3, page 967 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $g_t(u)=(4\pi t)^{-1/2}e^{-u^2/4t}$, $\psi=\Gamma'/\Gamma$, $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, $\mathcal A(t)=e^{t/4}-\frac12g_t(0)\log\pi+\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-tr^2}\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac{ir}2)\,dr$, $\mathcal P(t)=\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)n^{-1/2}g_t(\log n)$ and $W=\mathcal A-\mathcal P$, which by the Guinand and Weil explicit formula is the heat trace $W(t)=\sum_je^{-\lambda_jt}$ with $\lambda_j=-(\rho_j-\frac12)^2$ and $\rho_j$ the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ in the upper half plane counted with multiplicity; let $\psi_{\mathrm C}(y)=\sum_{n\le y}\Lambda(n)$ and $D(u)=(\psi_{\mathrm C}(e^u)-e^u)e^{-u/2}$, so that $D(0)=-1$. For every $t>0$, without RH, $W(t)=\Sigma_\infty(t)+\int_0^\infty D(u)k_t(u)\,du$ with $k_t=\partial_ug_t-\frac12g_t$ and $\Sigma_\infty(t)=\int_0^\infty g_t(u)e^{-u/2}du-g_t(0)(1+\frac12\log\pi)+\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-tr^2}\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac14+\frac{ir}2)\,dr$. The proof writes $d\psi_{\mathrm C}(e^u)=e^u\,du+d(De^{u/2})$ in the prime part and integrates by parts.

Source: [`ch/wt3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt3.tex), label `wt:prop:smooth`.

<a id="rh_equivalent_to_finite_discounted_energy_of_the_normalised_prime_error"></a>

### Energy form of RH: the normalised prime error has finite discounted energy if and only if RH holds

Proposition 26.9.4, page 968 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\psi_{\mathrm C}(y)=\sum_{n\le y}\Lambda(n)$ and $D(u)=(\psi_{\mathrm C}(e^u)-e^u)e^{-u/2}$, and let $E_\epsilon=\int_0^\infty D(u)^2e^{-2\epsilon u}\,du$. RH holds if and only if $E_\epsilon<\infty$ for every $\epsilon>0$. Under RH, with $m_\gamma$ the multiplicity of the zero $\frac12+i\gamma$ of $\zeta$ and the sum over the distinct positive ordinates $\gamma$ of the nontrivial zeros, $\lim_{U\to\infty}U^{-1}\int_0^UD(u)^2du=2\sum_{\gamma>0}m_\gamma^2/(\frac14+\gamma^2)$. This equals $\sum_\rho|\rho|^{-2}$, the sum over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$ of $\zeta$, $=2+\gamma_E-\log4\pi=0.0461914179$ if all zeros are simple, with $\gamma_E$ Euler's constant, and $2+\gamma_E-\log4\pi+2\sum_{\gamma>0}m_\gamma(m_\gamma-1)/(\frac14+\gamma^2)$ in general. The equivalence is proved from $\int_0^\infty D(u)e^{-zu}du=-\zeta'(s)/(s\zeta(s))-1/(s-1)$ with $s=\frac12+z$ and von Koch's bound; the formula for the limit follows the mean square theorem of Cram\'er, and the multiplicity sensitive form is quoted from the literature.

Source: [`ch/wt3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt3.tex), label `wt:prop:energy`.

<a id="mean_square_of_the_normalised_prime_error_from_primes_up_to_two_times_ten_to_the_seven_computed"></a>

### Computed mean square of the normalised prime error on four windows of the log scale

Result 26.9.4, page 968 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $D(u)=(\psi_{\mathrm C}(e^u)-e^u)e^{-u/2}$ with $\psi_{\mathrm C}(y)=\sum_{n\le y}\Lambda(n)$. Computed from the primes up to $2\times10^7$ by integrating $D^2$ exactly on each interval between integers (code/wt_rig.py): the mean of $D^2$ over $u\in[5,10]$, $[8,12]$, $[10,14]$, $[12,16.8]$ is $0.0509$, $0.0442$, $0.0465$, $0.0468$, against $2+\gamma_E-\log4\pi=0.046191$ ($\gamma_E$ Euler's constant), the limit of the mean that RH with simple zeros gives, where it equals $\sum_\rho|\rho|^{-2}$ over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$. Finite windows can be consistent with this value without proving the limit or the simplicity of the zeros.

Source: [`ch/wt3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt3.tex), label `wt:res:energy`.

<a id="rh_equivalent_to_positive_semidefiniteness_of_two_hankel_families_of_normalised_cumulants"></a>

### Hankel form of RH: all zeros are on the line if and only if two Hankel families of normalised cumulants are positive semidefinite

Proposition 26.9.5, page 970 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\rho_j=\beta_j+i\tau_j$ with $\tau_j>0$ be the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function $\zeta$ in the upper half plane, counted with multiplicity (the zeros are closed under $\rho\mapsto1-\bar\rho$), let $\gamma_j=\tau_j+i(\frac12-\beta_j)$, so that $\rho_j=\frac12+i\gamma_j$ and $\gamma_j$ is real exactly when $\rho_j$ is on the critical line, let $\lambda_j=\gamma_j^2$, and let $W(t)=\sum_je^{-\lambda_jt}$ for $t>0$ be the heat trace of the zeros (absolutely convergent because the number of zeros of height at most $T$ is $O(T\log T)$). Let $s_j=\sum_k\lambda_k^{-j}$ and $m_j=s_{j+1}$ for $j\ge0$ (the normalised cumulants $\kappa_{j+1}/j!$ of the reciprocal Xi law, whose first two values can be read off the primes). RH holds if and only if the Hankel matrices $H_d=(m_{i+j})_{0\le i,j\le d}$ and $H_d^{(1)}=(m_{i+j+1})_{0\le i,j\le d}$ are positive semidefinite for every $d\ge0$. The converse uses Stieltjes' moment theorem to get a positive measure with these moments, supported on $[0,R]$ with $R=\sup|\lambda_k|^{-1}$, and then analytic continuation of $\sum_jm_jz^j=\sum_k1/(\lambda_k-z)$, whose poles have residues minus the positive integer multiplicities, to force every $\lambda_k>0$.

Source: [`ch/wt3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt3.tex), label `wt:prop:hankel`.

<a id="one_heat_time_suffices_rh_iff_sine_squared_functional_is_nonnegative_for_all_shifts"></a>

### One heat time suffices: RH holds if and only if the sine squared functional is nonnegative for every shift at a single heat time

Theorem 26.10.1, page 971 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\rho_j=\beta_j+i\tau_j$ with $\tau_j>0$ be the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function $\zeta$ in the upper half plane, counted with multiplicity (the zeros are closed under $\rho\mapsto1-\bar\rho$), let $\gamma_j=\tau_j+i(\frac12-\beta_j)$, so that $\rho_j=\frac12+i\gamma_j$ and $\gamma_j$ is real exactly when $\rho_j$ is on the critical line, let $\lambda_j=\gamma_j^2$, and let $W(t)=\sum_je^{-\lambda_jt}$ for $t>0$ be the heat trace of the zeros (absolutely convergent because the number of zeros of height at most $T$ is $O(T\log T)$). For $t>0$ and $a\ge0$ let $f_t(a)=\sum_je^{-\lambda_jt}\cos(a\gamma_j)$ and $V(t,a)=W(t)-f_t(a)=\sum_j2\sin^2(a\gamma_j/2)e^{-\lambda_jt}$, the Weil functional of the even part of the test function $FF^*$ with $F(z)=(1-e^{iaz})e^{-tz^2/2}/\sqrt2$. Fix $t>0$. Then the Riemann Hypothesis holds if and only if $V(t,a)\ge0$ for every $a\ge0$. Under RH every term is nonnegative. Conversely, a zero off the line with $\operatorname{Im}\gamma_j=b>0$ gives a genuine pole at $s=-i\gamma_j$ of the Laplace transform $\int_0^\infty e^{-sa}V(t,a)\,da=W(t)/s-\sum_je^{-\gamma_j^2t}s/(s^2+\gamma_j^2)$, so its abscissa of convergence is at least $b>0$, and Landau's theorem for the nonnegative function $V(t,\cdot)$ forces a real singularity there, which no pole of the right side can supply: the poles $\pm i\gamma_j$ are not real because $\operatorname{Re}\gamma_j>0$ (the function $\xi$ has no real zeros), and the possible pole at $s=0$ lies left of $\sigma_c\ge b>0$.

Source: [`ch/wt3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/wt3.tex), label `wt:thm:sin2`.

## Chapter 27. The Comtet Majumdar family and the uniform law

<a id="expected_maximum_of_a_stable_walk_has_the_zeta_constant_of_comtet_and_majumdar"></a>

### A proof by Spitzer's identity and Euler Maclaurin summation that the expected maximum of a symmetric stable walk has the constant of Comtet and Majumdar, zeta of s over a sine factor

Proposition 27.1.2, page 980 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $S_n$ be a random walk whose steps $X$ are symmetric stable with $\mathbb Ee^{ikX}=e^{-|k|^\mu}$, $1<\mu\le2$, let $M_n=\max_{0\le j\le n}S_j$ and $s=1/\mu$. Then $\mathbb EM_n=\frac{\Gamma(1-s)}{\pi s}n^s+\frac{\Gamma(1-s)\zeta(1-s)}{\pi}+O(n^{s-1})$, where $\zeta$ is the Riemann zeta function. Hence the constant term, found by Comtet and Majumdar, is $C_\mu=I(s)=\zeta(s)/\{(2\pi)^s\sin(\pi s/2)\}$, with $I(s)=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty x^{-s}(\frac1{e^x-1}-\frac1x)\,dx$.

Source: [`ch/cg1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cg1.tex), label `cg:prop:spitzer`.

<a id="logarithm_of_the_uniform_transform_as_a_regularised_signed_levy_integral"></a>

### The logarithm of the Laplace transform of the uniform law is a regularised integral against Lebesgue minus counting measure
