Proposition 27.1.3, page 981 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. For $x>0$, $\ln\frac{1-e^{-x}}{x}=-\lim_{R\to\infty}\{\int_0^R(1-e^{-xt})\frac{dt}{t}-\sum_{1\le n\le R}\frac{1-e^{-xn}}{n}\}$, a regularised integral against the signed measure $dt-d\lfloor t\rfloor$ with a common upper cutoff $R$, where $\lfloor t\rfloor$ is the integer part. For $0<\operatorname{Re}z<1$, $\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_0^Rt^{-z}(d\lfloor t\rfloor-dt)=-z\int_0^\infty\{t\}t^{-z-1}\,dt=\zeta(z)$, with $\{t\}$ the fractional part and $\zeta$ the Riemann zeta function. The two parts of the signed measure are mutually singular and $\int_1^\infty|dt-d\lfloor t\rfloor|/t=\infty$, so the representation is regularised and not a signed L\'evy measure.

Source: [`ch/cg1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cg1.tex), label `cg:prop:signed`.

<a id="locally_uniform_limit_of_ggc_reciprocals_implies_real_zeros"></a>

### If locally uniform limits of GGC reciprocals approximate Xi then RH holds

Corollary 27.2.2, page 982 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Xi$ be the Riemann Xi function and let $\Xi_\delta$ be even, real on $\mathbb R$, entire of order less than two with $\Xi_\delta(0)>0$, such that $\Xi_\delta\to\Xi$ locally uniformly as $\delta\to0$ and each $w\mapsto\Xi_\delta(0)/\Xi_\delta(i\sqrt w)$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC). Then all zeros of $\Xi$ are real, that is the Riemann Hypothesis holds. Conversely, under the Riemann Hypothesis the constant family $\Xi_\delta=\Xi$ qualifies.

Source: [`ch/cg1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cg1.tex), label `cg:cor:closure`.

<a id="exact_expansion_of_the_shifted_zeta_in_zeta_at_integer_translates"></a>

### The shifted zeta is an explicit series of zeta at s plus k with a tangent factor

Theorem 27.3.2, page 982 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $g(x)=\frac1{e^x-1}-\frac1x$, $\delta>0$, $I_\delta(s)=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty x^{-s}g(x+\delta)\,dx$ for $0<\operatorname{Re}s<1$, $\zeta_\delta(s)=(2\pi)^s\sin(\pi s/2)I_\delta(s)$ (so $\zeta_0=\zeta$), $\operatorname{Li}_\sigma$ the polylogarithm and $(s)_k$ the rising factorial. For $0<\delta<2\pi$, $\pi I_\delta(s)=\Gamma(1-s)F_\delta(s)$ with $F_\delta(s)=\operatorname{Li}_{1-s}(e^{-\delta})-\Gamma(s)\delta^{-s}=\sum_{k\ge0}\zeta(1-s-k)(-\delta)^k/k!$, and $\zeta_\delta(s)=\sum_{k\ge0}(\delta/2\pi)^k\frac{(s)_k}{k!}\frac{\sin(\pi s/2)}{\sin(\pi(s+k)/2)}\zeta(s+k)=\zeta(s)+\frac{\delta}{2\pi}s\tan\frac{\pi s}2\,\zeta(s+1)-\frac{\delta^2}{8\pi^2}s(s+1)\zeta(s+2)-\cdots$. The ratio of sines is $(-1)^j$ for $k=2j$ and $(-1)^j\tan(\pi s/2)$ for $k=2j+1$.

Source: [`ch/cg1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cg1.tex), label `cg:thm:expansion`.

<a id="shifted_family_has_poles_drifting_zeros_and_no_ggc_reciprocal"></a>

### Obstructions: the shifted xi function has a pole at s equal 3, its zeros drift, and its reciprocal is not a GGC transform

Proposition 27.3.3, page 983 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $0<\delta<2\pi$, $g(x)=\frac1{e^x-1}-\frac1x$, $F_\delta(s)=\operatorname{Li}_{1-s}(e^{-\delta})-\Gamma(s)\delta^{-s}$ with $\operatorname{Li}$ the polylogarithm, $\zeta_\delta(s)=(2\pi)^s\sin(\pi s/2)\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty x^{-s}g(x+\delta)\,dx$ for $0<\operatorname{Re}s<1$, continued meromorphically, and $\xi_\delta(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta_\delta(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{(s-1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{1-s}2)F_\delta(s)$. (a) $\xi_\delta$ is meromorphic and not entire. It has a pole at $s=3$ for every $\delta\in(0,2\pi)$, because $F_\delta(3)=4\sum_{k\ge1}\operatorname{Re}(\delta-2\pi ik)^{-3}<0$, and poles at $s=-1,-2,-3,\dots$ For $m\ge2$ it has a pole at $s=2m+1$ exactly when $F_\delta(2m+1)\ne0$. The values $F_\delta(5)=0$ at $\delta=4.7215$ and $F_\delta(7)=0$ at $\delta=3.0416$ are computed (not proved), so for those $\delta$ there is no pole at $s=5$, respectively $s=7$. (b) Each simple zero $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$ of the Riemann zeta function $\zeta$ moves to $\rho_\delta=\rho-\frac\delta{2\pi}\frac{\rho\tan(\pi\rho/2)\zeta(\rho+1)}{\zeta'(\rho)}+O(\delta^2)$, and $\xi_\delta(s)\ne\xi_\delta(1-s)$. (c) If $\xi_\delta(\frac12)\ne0$, the function $w\mapsto\xi_\delta(\frac12)/\xi_\delta(\frac12+\sqrt w)$ is not the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution, nor of any positive measure.

Source: [`ch/cg1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cg1.tex), label `cg:prop:obstructions`.

<a id="thorin_density_from_a_signed_levy_measure_with_logarithmic_derivative_condition"></a>

### A signed L\'evy measure gives a Thorin density, which is nonnegative if and only if a logarithmic derivative inequality holds

Theorem 27.4.2, page 986 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $f$ be analytic and without zeros on $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha_0$ and positive on $(\alpha_0,\infty)$, and let $M$ be a signed measure on $(0,\infty)$ with $\int(1\wedge x)e^{-\alpha x}|M|(dx)<\infty$ for every $\alpha>\alpha_0$ such that $\frac{f'}f(s)-\frac{f'}f(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty(e^{-\alpha x}-e^{-sx})M(dx)$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha_0$ and $\alpha>\alpha_0$. Then for every $\alpha>\alpha_0$ and $w\ge0$, $\log\frac{f(\alpha+w)}{f(\alpha)}-w\frac{f'}f(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty\log(1+w^2/y^2)\kappa_\alpha(y)\,dy$ with $\kappa_\alpha(y)=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty(1-\cos xy)e^{-\alpha x}M(dx)=\frac1\pi[\operatorname{Re}\frac{f'}f(\alpha+iy)-\frac{f'}f(\alpha)]$. If $\kappa_\alpha\ge0$, then $u\mapsto\frac{f(\alpha)}{f(\alpha+\sqrt{2u})}\exp\{\sqrt{2u}\,\frac{f'}f(\alpha)\}$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) with Thorin density $\tau_\alpha(z)=\kappa_\alpha(\sqrt{2z})/\sqrt{2z}$.

Source: [`ch/cg2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cg2.tex), label `cg:thm:thorinfromlevy`.

<a id="zeros_on_one_vertical_line_give_lorentzian_thorin_densities_tending_to_point_masses"></a>

### Zeros on a vertical line give a Thorin density that is a sum of Lorentzians tending to point masses at the ordinates

Corollary 27.4.3, page 986 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $f$ be analytic and without zeros on $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha_0$ and positive on $(\alpha_0,\infty)$, let $M$ be a signed measure on $(0,\infty)$ with $\int(1\wedge x)e^{-\alpha x}|M|(dx)<\infty$ and $\frac{f'}f(s)-\frac{f'}f(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty(e^{-\alpha x}-e^{-sx})M(dx)$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha_0$ and $\alpha>\alpha_0$, let $\kappa_\alpha(y)=\frac1\pi[\operatorname{Re}\frac{f'}f(\alpha+iy)-\frac{f'}f(\alpha)]$, so that $\log\frac{f(\alpha+w)}{f(\alpha)}-w\frac{f'}f(\alpha)=\int_0^\infty\log(1+w^2/y^2)\kappa_\alpha(y)\,dy$ for $w\ge0$, and let $a$ be real, suppose $f'/f(s)=a+\sum_k(s-\rho_k)^{-1}$ (symmetric summation) with all $\rho_k=\beta_0+it_k$ on one vertical line, the set $\{t_k\}$ symmetric and $0\notin\{t_k\}$, and write $\ell_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon/(\varepsilon^2+x^2)$ for the Cauchy kernel. Then for $\alpha=\beta_0+\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon>0$, $\kappa_\alpha(y)=\frac1\pi\sum_k[\ell_\varepsilon(y-t_k)-\ell_\varepsilon(t_k)]$. If $\sum_kt_k^{-2}<\infty$ then $\kappa_\alpha(y)\,dy\to\sum_{t_k>0}\delta_{t_k}(dy)$ vaguely on $(0,\infty)$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, and $\int_0^\infty\log(1+w^2/y^2)\kappa_\alpha(y)\,dy$ tends to $\sum_{t_k>0}\log(1+w^2/t_k^2)$.

Source: [`ch/cg2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cg2.tex), label `cg:cor:lorentz`.

<a id="thorin_density_of_the_tilted_uniform_law_is_positive_for_every_tilt"></a>

### The tilted uniform law has a strictly positive Thorin density for every positive tilt, a Lorentzian smoothing of the lattice 2 pi m

Theorem 27.4.4, page 987 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\varphi_U(s)=(1-e^{-s})/s$ be the Laplace transform of the uniform law on $(0,1)$, $g=\varphi_U'/\varphi_U$ (so $g(x)=\frac1{e^x-1}-\frac1x$), $\ell_\delta(x)=\delta/(\delta^2+x^2)$ and $\kappa_\delta(y)=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty(1-\cos xy)e^{-\delta x}(dx-d\lfloor x\rfloor)=\frac1\pi[\operatorname{Re}g(\delta+iy)-g(\delta)]$ for $y>0$, with $g(s)=\frac1{e^s-1}-\frac1s$ and $\lfloor x\rfloor$ the integer part. For every $\delta>0$, $\pi\kappa_\delta(y)=\frac{y^2}{\delta(\delta^2+y^2)}-\frac12\coth\frac\delta2\frac{1-\cos y}{\cosh\delta-\cos y}=\sum_{m\ge1}[\ell_\delta(y-2\pi m)+\ell_\delta(y+2\pi m)-2\ell_\delta(2\pi m)]$, and $\kappa_\delta(y)>0$ for all $y>0$. Hence $u\mapsto\frac{\varphi_U(\delta)}{\varphi_U(\delta+\sqrt{2u})}e^{\sqrt{2u}\,g(\delta)}$ is the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) with Thorin density $\tau_\delta(z)=\kappa_\delta(\sqrt{2z})/\sqrt{2z}$. As $\delta\downarrow0$, $\kappa_\delta(y)\,dy\to\sum_{m\ge1}\delta_{2\pi m}$ vaguely, and $\log\frac{\sinh(w/2)}{w/2}=\sum_{m\ge1}\log(1+\frac{w^2}{4\pi^2m^2})$, so $(w/2)/\sinh(w/2)$ is the Laplace transform in $u=w^2/2$ of $\sum_me_m/(2\pi^2m^2)$ with independent standard exponential $e_m$, a GGC with Thorin measure $\sum_m\delta_{2\pi^2m^2}$ (a law of Biane, Pitman and Yor type).

Source: [`ch/cg2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cg2.tex), label `cg:thm:uniform`.

<a id="shifted_zeta_is_the_mellin_transform_of_the_thorin_density_of_the_tilted_uniform_law"></a>

### The shifted zeta equals (2 pi) to the s times the Mellin transform of the positive Thorin density of the tilted uniform law

Theorem 27.4.5, page 988 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $g(s)=\frac1{e^s-1}-\frac1s$, let $\kappa_\delta(y)=\frac1\pi[\operatorname{Re}g(\delta+iy)-g(\delta)]$ for $y>0$, the positive Thorin density of the uniform law on $(0,1)$ tilted by $\delta$, and $\zeta_\delta(s)=(2\pi)^s\sin(\pi s/2)\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty x^{-s}g(x+\delta)\,dx$ (continued analytically in $s$; for $\delta<2\pi$ it equals $\sum_{k\ge0}(\delta/2\pi)^k\frac{(s)_k}{k!}\frac{\sin(\pi s/2)}{\sin(\pi(s+k)/2)}\zeta(s+k)$, with $(s)_k$ the rising factorial). For $1<\operatorname{Re}s<3$ and every $\delta>0$, $\zeta_\delta(s)=(2\pi)^s\int_0^\infty y^{-s}\kappa_\delta(y)\,dy$. At $\delta=0$ the right side is formally $(2\pi)^s\sum_{m\ge1}(2\pi m)^{-s}=\zeta(s)$.

Source: [`ch/cg2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cg2.tex), label `cg:thm:mellinthorin`.

<a id="gauss_damped_theta_kernel_has_finitely_many_real_zeros_and_no_ggc_reciprocal"></a>

### Kink theorem: the Gauss damped Riemann kernel has finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros

Theorem 27.5.1, page 991 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$, $\Phi=2\sum_{n\ge1}\Phi_n$, so that $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(ut)\,du$ for the Riemann Xi function. For $\delta>0$ let $\Phi_\delta=2\sum_{n\ge1}e^{-\pi n^2\delta}\Phi_n$ on $[0,\infty)$ and $\Xi_\delta(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi_\delta(u)\cos(ut)\,du$, an even real entire function of order one with $\Xi_\delta(0)>0$. Then $\Xi_\delta$ has only finitely many real zeros and infinitely many nonreal zeros, because $\Phi_\delta'(0)>0$ (using $\sum_n\Phi_n'(0)=0$, from the evenness of $\Phi$, and $\Phi_n'(0)<0$ for $n\ge2$) and $t^2\Xi_\delta(t)\to-2\Phi_\delta'(0)<0$ as $t\to\infty$ along $\mathbb R$. Consequently $\Xi_\delta(0)/\Xi_\delta(i\sqrt w)$ is not the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution.

Source: [`ch/cg3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cg3.tex), label `cg:thm:kink`.

<a id="modular_constraints_on_the_weights_for_a_laguerre_polya_damped_kernel"></a>

### Modular constraints: a Laguerre P\'olya damped kernel must have vanishing odd derivatives of the damped kernel at the origin

Corollary 27.5.2, page 992 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi_n(u)=(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ for $n\ge1$, the terms of the Riemann kernel $\Phi=2\sum_n\Phi_n$ for which $\Xi(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi(u)\cos(ut)\,du$ is the Riemann Xi function, let $\Phi_w=2\sum_{n\ge1}w_n\Phi_n$ with real weights $w_n$ such that $\sum_n|w_n|n^Ae^{-\pi n^2}<\infty$ for every $A\ge0$, and $\Xi_w(t)=2\int_0^\infty\Phi_w(u)\cos(ut)\,du$. If $\Xi_w$ lies in the Laguerre P\'olya class $\mathcal{LP}$ (locally uniform limits of real polynomials with only real zeros) and is not of the form $e^{-at^2}$ times a polynomial, then $\sum_nw_n\Phi_n^{(2j+1)}(0)=0$ for every $j\ge0$.

Source: [`ch/cg3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cg3.tex), label `cg:cor:modular`.

## Chapter 28. Truncations of the beta lattice and Hermite coefficients

<a id="truncated_mellin_transforms_converge_and_grh_for_chi4_is_a_local_zero_free_statement"></a>

### Truncations converge locally uniformly, and GRH for chi 4 is equivalent to zero free compact subsets of the left half strip for large n

Theorem 28.1.1, page 1000 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Suppose $R_n\to0$ in probability, as for the hard cutoff $R_n=0$ and for every nonnegative remainder with $\mathbb ER_n=\mathbb ET_n$. Then $M_n\to M$ locally uniformly on $0<\Re z<\frac12$, and the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for $\chi_4$ holds if and only if every compact subset of $0<\Re z<\frac14$ is free of zeros of $M_n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

Source: [`ch/tr1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr1.tex), label `tr:thm:local`.

<a id="midpoint_tail_cumulants_of_the_beta_lattice"></a>

### The tail cumulants of the beta lattice have an explicit expansion in the truncation index

Lemma 28.2.1, page 1001 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Then for fixed $j\ge1$, $q_j(n)=\lambda_*^{-j}\{n^{1-2j}/(2j-1)-\frac j{12}n^{-2j-1}+O(n^{-2j-3})\}$. In particular $c_n=\mathbb ET_n=\frac1{\lambda_*n}-\frac1{12\lambda_*n^3}+O(n^{-5})$, $v_n=\operatorname{Var}T_n=q_2(n)=\frac1{3\lambda_*^2n^3}-\frac1{6\lambda_*^2n^5}+O(n^{-7})$ and $\kappa_3(T_n)=\frac2{5\lambda_*^3n^5}+O(n^{-7})$.

Source: [`ch/tr1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr1.tex), label `tr:lem:tail`.

<a id="drift_law_of_the_zeros_of_truncated_beta_mellin_transforms"></a>

### The truncated Mellin transform differs from M by a multiple of M(z+r), and each simple zero is displaced by a multiple of the first unmatched cumulant difference

Theorem 28.2.2, page 1001 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Fix $m\ge0$, $r=m+1$, $p=2r-1$, and let $R_n\ge0$ be independent of $\omega_n$ with $\kappa_j(R_n)=\kappa_j(T_n)$ for $1\le j<r$, such that for a constant $C$ independent of $n$ and $j$, $\log\mathbb Ee^{-tR_n}=\sum_{j\ge1}(-1)^j\kappa_j(R_n)t^j/j!$ for $0\le t<n^2/C$ and $|\kappa_j(R_n)|/j!\le C^jn^{1-2j}$. Put $\Delta_{r,n}=\kappa_r(T_n)-\kappa_r(R_n)$ and $(z)_r=z(z+1)\cdots(z+r-1)$. Then uniformly for $z$ in a compact subset $K$ of $\Re z>0$, $M_n(z)-M(z)=-\frac{(-1)^r\Delta_{r,n}}{r!}(z)_rM(z+r)+O_K(n^{-p-2}+n^{-2p})$. Let $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$ be a simple zero of $\xi_4$ and $z_0=\rho/2$. For all large $n$ a fixed small disc about $z_0$ contains exactly one zero $z_n$ of $M_n$, it is simple, and $z_n-z_0=\frac{(-1)^r\Delta_{r,n}}{r!}(z_0)_r\frac{M(z_0+r)}{M'(z_0)}+O(n^{-p-2}+n^{-2p})$ with $\frac{M(z_0+r)}{M'(z_0)}=\frac{(2\pi)^r\xi_4(\rho+2r)}{2\xi_4'(\rho)}$. If $\Delta_{r,n}=d\,n^{-p}+o(n^{-p})$ with $d\ne0$, then $z_n-z_0=D_rn^{-p}+o(n^{-p})$ with $D_r=\frac{(-1)^rd\,(2\pi)^r(z_0)_r\,\xi_4(\rho+2r)}{2\,r!\,\xi_4'(\rho)}\ne0$.

Source: [`ch/tr1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr1.tex), label `tr:thm:drift`.

<a id="drift_of_the_hard_cutoff_and_of_the_mean_correction_zeros"></a>

### The hard cutoff zeros drift at the rate 1 over n and the mean corrected zeros at 1 over n cubed, with the coefficient delta m

Corollary 28.2.3, page 1002 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Fix $m\ge0$, $r=m+1$, $p=2r-1$, and let $R_n\ge0$ be independent of $\omega_n$ with $\kappa_j(R_n)=\kappa_j(T_n)$ for $1\le j<r$, such that for a constant $C$ independent of $n$ and $j$, $\log\mathbb Ee^{-tR_n}=\sum_{j\ge1}(-1)^j\kappa_j(R_n)t^j/j!$ for $0\le t<n^2/C$ and $|\kappa_j(R_n)|/j!\le C^jn^{1-2j}$. Put $\Delta_{r,n}=\kappa_r(T_n)-\kappa_r(R_n)$ and $(z)_r=z(z+1)\cdots(z+r-1)$. Let $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$ be a simple zero of $\xi_4$, $z_0=\rho/2$, and $\delta_m=\frac{(-1)^{m+1}(z_0)_{m+1}\,\xi_4(\rho+2m+2)}{2(m+1)(2m+1)\,\pi^{m+1}\,\xi_4'(\rho)}$. Let $z_n$ be the zero of $M_n$ in a fixed small disc about $z_0$ (unique and simple for large $n$). For the hard cutoff $R_n=0$, $z_n=z_0+\delta_0/n+O(n^{-2})$. For the mean correction $R_n=\mathbb ET_n$ (a constant), $z_n=z_0+\delta_1/n^3+O(n^{-5})$. For a remainder that satisfies the hypotheses above at order $m$ and has $\kappa_{m+1}(R_n)=o(n^{-(2m+1)})$ the displacement is $\delta_mn^{-(2m+1)}(1+o(1))$.

Source: [`ch/tr1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr1.tex), label `tr:cor:named`.

<a id="gamma_remainders_with_matched_mean_and_variance_give_different_third_order_drifts"></a>

### Remainders matching mean and variance but not the third cumulant give different drifts, so the formula of delta 2 needs the matching hypothesis

Proposition 28.2.4, page 1004 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Let $c_n=\mathbb ET_n$, $v_n=\operatorname{Var}T_n$, $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$ a simple zero of $\xi_4$, $z_0=\rho/2$, $z_n$ the zero of $M_n$ in a fixed small disc about $z_0$ (unique and simple for large $n$), and $\delta_2=-\frac{(z_0)_3\,\xi_4(\rho+6)}{30\,\pi^3\,\xi_4'(\rho)}$ with $(z_0)_3=z_0(z_0+1)(z_0+2)$. Let $R_n$ have the gamma law with shape $c_n^2/v_n$ and scale $v_n/c_n$. Then $R_n$ satisfies, for a constant $C$ independent of $n$ and $j$, $\log\mathbb Ee^{-tR_n}=\sum_{j\ge1}(-1)^j\kappa_j(R_n)t^j/j!$ for $0\le t<n^2/C$ and $|\kappa_j(R_n)|/j!\le C^jn^{1-2j}$, and $z_n=z_0+\frac49\delta_2\,n^{-5}+O(n^{-7})$. A remainder $R_n=G_{1,n}+G_{2,n}$, a sum of two independent gamma variables with the same mean and variance and the same natural scale, gives $z_n=z_0-\frac19\delta_2\,n^{-5}+O(n^{-7})$. A bounded remainder $R_n=b_n+hB_n$ with $B_n$ a Bernoulli variable, $h>0$ small and fixed, matched to the mean and variance, has $z_n-z_0=c\,n^{-3}+O(n^{-5})$ with $c\ne0$.

Source: [`ch/tr1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr1.tex), label `tr:prop:gamma`.

<a id="side_of_approach_of_a_truncated_zero_is_set_by_a_gram_phase"></a>

### The sign of the real part of the drift is the sign of minus sin Theta m times the derivative of the Hardy function of chi 4

Theorem 28.3.1, page 1005 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Put $G(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)$, so that $\xi_4=\frac2{\sqrt\pi}GL$, let $\vartheta_\beta(x)=\arg G(\frac12+ix)$ and $Z_\beta(x)=e^{i\vartheta_\beta(x)}L(\frac12+ix,\chi_4)$ (real), the Riemann Siegel function and the Hardy function of $\chi_4$. Let $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$, $\gamma>0$, be a simple zero of $\xi_4$, $z_0=\rho/2$, $(z)_r=z(z+1)\cdots(z+r-1)$, and for $m\ge0$ let $\delta_m=\frac{(-1)^{m+1}(z_0)_{m+1}\,\xi_4(\rho+2m+2)}{2(m+1)(2m+1)\,\pi^{m+1}\,\xi_4'(\rho)}$. Then $\delta_m=\frac{i\,C_m(\gamma)e^{i\Theta_m(\gamma)}}{Z_\beta'(\gamma)}$ with $C_m(\gamma)>0$ and $\Theta_m(\gamma)=\vartheta_\beta(\gamma)+\arg L(\rho+2m+2,\chi_4)-\sum_{j=0}^m[\arctan\frac{1/2+2j}\gamma+\arctan\frac{3/2+2j}\gamma]$, so that $\operatorname{sgn}\Re\delta_m=\operatorname{sgn}[-\sin\Theta_m(\gamma)Z_\beta'(\gamma)]$, zero included. For a remainder $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$ with $\kappa_j(R_n)=\kappa_j(T_n)$ for $1\le j\le m$ such that, for a constant $C$ independent of $n$ and $j$, $\log\mathbb Ee^{-tR_n}=\sum_{j\ge1}(-1)^j\kappa_j(R_n)t^j/j!$ for $0\le t<n^2/C$ and $|\kappa_j(R_n)|/j!\le C^jn^{1-2j}$, and with $\eta_m=\lim_n[\kappa_{m+1}(T_n)-\kappa_{m+1}(R_n)]/\kappa_{m+1}(T_n)$ the displacement $z_n-z_0$ of the zero $z_n$ of $M_n$ near $z_0$ is $\eta_m\delta_mn^{-(2m+1)}(1+o(1))$ when the limit exists and $\eta_m\ne0$, and the sign of the real part is $\operatorname{sgn}[-\eta_m\sin\Theta_m(\gamma)Z_\beta'(\gamma)]$ when $\eta_m\sin\Theta_m\ne0$.

Source: [`ch/tr1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr1.tex), label `tr:thm:phase`.

<a id="beta_zeros_below_height_500_located_by_sign_changes_of_the_hardy_function"></a>

### L(s,chi 4) has 379 zeros below height 500 by sign changes, all simple and on the line as far as the computation sees, with five anomalous Gram parities

Result 28.3.1, page 1005 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\vartheta_\beta$ and $Z_\beta$ the Riemann Siegel and Hardy functions of $\chi_4$ with $\vartheta_\beta(x)=\arg[(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)]_{s=1/2+ix}$. Put $Z_\beta(x)=e^{i\vartheta_\beta(x)}L(\frac12+ix,\chi_4)$ (real), $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$, and for a zero $\rho$ with $z_0=\rho/2$ and $(z)_r=z(z+1)\cdots(z+r-1)$ let $\delta_m=\frac{(-1)^{m+1}(z_0)_{m+1}\,\xi_4(\rho+2m+2)}{2(m+1)(2m+1)\,\pi^{m+1}\,\xi_4'(\rho)}$, the drift coefficient of the zeros of the truncated Mellin transforms of the beta lattice ($m=0$ for the hard cutoff, $m=1$ for the mean correction). Locating the sign changes of $Z_\beta$ on $0<x<500$ on two independent grids (steps $0.02$ and $0.0137$) and refining at two precisions gives $379$ zeros, all simple and on the critical line as far as the computation sees (the minimal gap is $0.1336$), in agreement with $\vartheta_\beta(500)/\pi=379.15$. The count is not certified, since there is no Turing bound. Measuring the Gram parity by $\lfloor\vartheta_\beta(\gamma)/\pi\rfloor$ minus the zero number, $374$ zeros have offset $-1$ and five do not, at $\gamma=138.7502$, $290.2521$, $364.4197$, $400.8264$ and $422.5104$ (zero numbers $78$, $195$, $258$, $291$, $309$). The mean correction has $\Re\delta_1<0$ exactly at these five zeros and at no other, and the hard cutoff has $\Re\delta_0<0$ at the last four.

Source: [`ch/tr1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr1.tex), label `tr:res:gram`.

<a id="no_one_sided_criterion_for_truncations_of_the_beta_lattice_at_a_fixed_order"></a>

### One sided criterion fails at order m if some critical zero is approached from the left

Corollary 28.3.2, page 1006 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Fix $m\ge0$ and a remainder $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$ with $\kappa_j(R_n)=\kappa_j(T_n)$ for $1\le j\le m$ such that, for a constant $C$ independent of $n$ and $j$, $\log\mathbb Ee^{-tR_n}=\sum_{j\ge1}(-1)^j\kappa_j(R_n)t^j/j!$ for $0\le t<n^2/C$ and $|\kappa_j(R_n)|/j!\le C^jn^{1-2j}$, for which $\eta_m=\lim_n[\kappa_{m+1}(T_n)-\kappa_{m+1}(R_n)]/\kappa_{m+1}(T_n)$ exists, and for a simple zero $\rho$ of $\xi_4$ let $z_0=\rho/2$, $(z)_r=z(z+1)\cdots(z+r-1)$ and $\delta_m=\frac{(-1)^{m+1}(z_0)_{m+1}\,\xi_4(\rho+2m+2)}{2(m+1)(2m+1)\,\pi^{m+1}\,\xi_4'(\rho)}$. If some simple zero $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$ of $\xi_4$ on the critical line has $\Re(\eta_m\delta_m)<0$, then for all large $n$ the function $M_n$ has a zero in $0<\Re z<\frac14$, so no criterion of the form that $M_n$ has no zero in $0<\Re z<\frac14$ for infinitely many $n$ can hold at order $m$ for this remainder.

Source: [`ch/tr1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr1.tex), label `tr:cor:nogo`.

<a id="anomalous_gram_parity_of_the_beta_function_forces_left_approach_with_a_margin"></a>

### Infinitely many Gram anomalies with a margin force infinitely many zeros with negative real drift

Proposition 28.3.3, page 1007 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Put $G(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)$, so that $\xi_4=\frac2{\sqrt\pi}GL$, let $\vartheta_\beta(x)=\arg G(\frac12+ix)$ and $Z_\beta(x)=e^{i\vartheta_\beta(x)}L(\frac12+ix,\chi_4)$ (real), the Riemann Siegel function and the Hardy function of $\chi_4$. For a simple zero $\rho=\frac12+i\gamma$, $\gamma>0$, of $\xi_4$ let $z_0=\rho/2$, $(z)_r=z(z+1)\cdots(z+r-1)$, $\delta_m=\frac{(-1)^{m+1}(z_0)_{m+1}\,\xi_4(\rho+2m+2)}{2(m+1)(2m+1)\,\pi^{m+1}\,\xi_4'(\rho)}$ and $\Theta_m(\gamma)=\vartheta_\beta(\gamma)+\arg L(\rho+2m+2,\chi_4)-\sum_{j=0}^m[\arctan\frac{1/2+2j}\gamma+\arctan\frac{3/2+2j}\gamma]$. Let $\sigma=2m+\frac52$, $\epsilon_\sigma=\sum_{k\ge1}(2k+1)^{-\sigma}<1$ and $B_m(\gamma)=\arcsin\epsilon_\sigma+\sum_{j=0}^m[\arctan\frac{1/2+2j}\gamma+\arctan\frac{3/2+2j}\gamma]$. Then $|\Theta_m(\gamma)-\vartheta_\beta(\gamma)|\le B_m(\gamma)$. If infinitely many simple critical zeros satisfy $-\sin\vartheta_\beta(\gamma)Z_\beta'(\gamma)<0$ and $\operatorname{dist}(\vartheta_\beta(\gamma),\pi\mathbb Z)>B_m(\gamma)$, then infinitely many zeros have $\Re\delta_m<0$.

Source: [`ch/tr1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr1.tex), label `tr:prop:gram`.

<a id="symmetrised_truncations_give_a_hurwitz_criterion_for_grh_of_chi4"></a>

### If the symmetrised truncations have only critical zeros for infinitely many n then GRH holds for chi 4

Theorem 28.5.1, page 1009 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Put $g_n(z)=(2\pi)^{-z}M_n(z)$ and $F_n(z)=g_n(z)+g_n(\frac12-z)$, for remainders with $R_n\to0$ in probability. If for infinitely many $n$ all zeros of $F_n$ in $0<\Re z<\frac12$ lie on $\Re z=\frac14$, then the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis holds for $\chi_4$.

Source: [`ch/tr1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr1.tex), label `tr:thm:symhurwitz`.

<a id="every_simple_critical_zero_of_xi4_is_the_limit_of_one_critical_zero_of_the_symmetrised_truncation"></a>

### Each simple critical zero is the limit of exactly one zero of the symmetrised truncation, and that zero is critical

Proposition 28.5.2, page 1009 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\chi_4$ be the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $L(s,\chi_4)$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\xi_4(s)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)L(s,\chi_4)$ its completion (entire and symmetric about $s=\frac12$), $\lambda_*=2\pi^2$, $\lambda_k=\lambda_*(k-\frac12)^2$, $\omega=\sum_{k\ge1}e_k/\lambda_k$ with independent standard exponential variables $e_k$ (so $\mathbb Ee^{-\lambda\omega}=\operatorname{sech}\sqrt{\lambda/2}$), $\omega_n=\sum_{k\le n}e_k/\lambda_k$ and $T_n=\omega-\omega_n$ the tail with cumulants $\kappa_j(T_n)=(j-1)!\,q_j(n)$, $q_j(n)=\sum_{k>n}\lambda_k^{-j}$. The Mellin transform is $M(z)=\mathbb E\,\omega^{-z}=(2\pi)^z\xi_4(2z)$, and the nontrivial zeros of $L(s,\chi_4)$ are the points $z=\rho/2$ of the strip $0<\Re z<\frac12$ where $M$ vanishes. A truncation is a random variable $R_n\ge0$ independent of $\omega_n$, with $M_n(z)=\mathbb E(\omega_n+R_n)^{-z}$. Put $g_n(z)=(2\pi)^{-z}M_n(z)$ and $F_n(z)=g_n(z)+g_n(\frac12-z)$, for remainders with $R_n\to0$ in probability. Every simple zero of $\xi_4(2z)$ on $\Re z=\frac14$ is, for all large $n$, the limit of exactly one zero of $F_n$ in a small disc about it, and that zero lies on $\Re z=\frac14$.

Source: [`ch/tr1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr1.tex), label `tr:prop:symlocal`.

<a id="hermite_coefficients_of_xi_are_the_taylor_coefficients_of_a_gaussian_smoothing"></a>

### The Hermite coefficients of Xi are generated by the Gaussian smoothing G a, with an explicit moment formula

Theorem 28.7.1, page 1013 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the P\'olya kernel, positive and even, and $\Xi(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ the Riemann Xi function. Let $h_n(x)=\pi^{-1/4}(2^nn!)^{-1/2}H_n(x)e^{-x^2/2}$ be the orthonormal Hermite functions, with $H_n$ the physicists' Hermite polynomials. For a scale $a>0$ put $c_n(a)=\sqrt a\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)h_n(au)\,du$, $t_m=a\sqrt{4m+1}$ and $b_m(a)=\sqrt{2\pi}\,(-1)^mc_{2m}(a)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Xi(t)h_{2m}(t/a)a^{-1/2}\,dt$. Let $G_a(\tau)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)e^{-a^2u^2/2}\cos(\tau u)\,du$ (the Gaussian smoothing of $\Xi$ of variance $a^2$) and $\nu_k(a)=\int\Phi(u)e^{-a^2u^2/2}u^{2k}du>0$. Then for every $a>0$, $\sum_{m\ge0}b_m(a)\frac{z^{2m}}{\sqrt{(2m)!}}=\sqrt{2\pi}\,\pi^{-1/4}\sqrt a\;e^{z^2/2}\,G_a(\sqrt2\,az)$, and $b_m(a)=\sqrt{2\pi}\,\pi^{-1/4}\sqrt a\,\sqrt{(2m)!}\sum_{k=0}^m\frac{(-1)^k2^ka^{2k}\nu_k(a)}{(2k)!\,2^{m-k}(m-k)!}$.

Source: [`ch/tr2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr2.tex), label `tr:thm:heat`.

<a id="additive_asymptotic_of_the_hermite_coefficients_of_xi_at_the_turning_points"></a>

### The normalised Hermite coefficient equals Xi at the turning point up to an explicit error of order a to the fourth

Theorem 28.8.1, page 1014 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the P\'olya kernel, positive and even, and $\Xi(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ the Riemann Xi function. Let $h_n(x)=\pi^{-1/4}(2^nn!)^{-1/2}H_n(x)e^{-x^2/2}$ be the orthonormal Hermite functions, with $H_n$ the physicists' Hermite polynomials. For a scale $a>0$ put $c_n(a)=\sqrt a\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)h_n(au)\,du$, $t_m=a\sqrt{4m+1}$ and $b_m(a)=\sqrt{2\pi}\,(-1)^mc_{2m}(a)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Xi(t)h_{2m}(t/a)a^{-1/2}\,dt$. Let $A_m(a)=\sqrt2\,\pi^{1/4}\sqrt a\sqrt{(2m)!}/(2^mm!)$ and $M_k(a_0)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)|u|^ke^{a_0^2u^2/2}du$. Then for every $a_0>0$, $0<a\le a_0$ and integer $m\ge0$, $|b_m(a)/A_m(a)-\Xi(t_m)|\le\frac{M_4(a_0)}{12}a^4$ and $b_m(a)/A_m(a)=\Xi(t_m)+a^4Q(t_m)+R_m(a)$ with $|R_m(a)|\le\frac{M_8(a_0)}{672}a^8$, where $Q(t)=\frac{\Xi'''(t)}{6t}-\frac{\Xi''(t)}{4t^2}+\frac{\Xi'(t)}{4t^3}$ for $t\ne0$ and $Q(0)=\frac{\Xi^{(4)}(0)}{12}=\frac1{12}\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)u^4du$ is an even entire function.

Source: [`ch/tr2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr2.tex), label `tr:thm:herm`.

<a id="hermite_coefficients_do_not_vanish_at_the_turning_points_over_zeros_of_xi"></a>

### At a real zero of Xi the Hermite coefficient at the matching scale does not vanish for large m

Proposition 28.8.2, page 1016 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the P\'olya kernel, positive and even, and $\Xi(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ the Riemann Xi function. Let $h_n(x)=\pi^{-1/4}(2^nn!)^{-1/2}H_n(x)e^{-x^2/2}$ be the orthonormal Hermite functions, with $H_n$ the physicists' Hermite polynomials. For a scale $a>0$ put $c_n(a)=\sqrt a\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)h_n(au)\,du$, $t_m=a\sqrt{4m+1}$ and $b_m(a)=\sqrt{2\pi}\,(-1)^mc_{2m}(a)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Xi(t)h_{2m}(t/a)a^{-1/2}\,dt$. Let $A_m(a)=\sqrt2\,\pi^{1/4}\sqrt a\sqrt{(2m)!}/(2^mm!)$ and $M_k(a_0)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)|u|^ke^{a_0^2u^2/2}du$. Let $Q(t)=\frac{\Xi'''(t)}{6t}-\frac{\Xi''(t)}{4t^2}+\frac{\Xi'(t)}{4t^3}$ for $t\ne0$. At every positive real zero $\gamma$ of $\Xi$, of any multiplicity, $b_m(a_m)\ne0$ for all large $m$, where $a_m=\gamma/\sqrt{4m+1}$. If $Q(\gamma)\ne0$ then $b_m(a_m)=\frac{2Q(\gamma)}{\sqrt\gamma}a_m^5+O(a_m^9)$. So $b_m(a)=\sqrt{2a}\,m^{-1/4}\,\Xi(a\sqrt{4m+1})(1+O(a^2))$ fails at the zeros of $\Xi$.

Source: [`ch/tr2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr2.tex), label `tr:prop:zeros`.

<a id="first_negative_hermite_coefficient_of_xi_marks_the_first_zero"></a>

### The index of the first negative Hermite coefficient satisfies 4 a squared m star tends to gamma 1 squared

Corollary 28.9.1, page 1016 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the P\'olya kernel, positive and even, and $\Xi(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ the Riemann Xi function. Let $h_n(x)=\pi^{-1/4}(2^nn!)^{-1/2}H_n(x)e^{-x^2/2}$ be the orthonormal Hermite functions, with $H_n$ the physicists' Hermite polynomials. For a scale $a>0$ put $c_n(a)=\sqrt a\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)h_n(au)\,du$, $t_m=a\sqrt{4m+1}$ and $b_m(a)=\sqrt{2\pi}\,(-1)^mc_{2m}(a)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Xi(t)h_{2m}(t/a)a^{-1/2}\,dt$. Let $Q(t)=\frac{\Xi'''(t)}{6t}-\frac{\Xi''(t)}{4t^2}+\frac{\Xi'(t)}{4t^3}$ ($t\ne0$), $\gamma_1=14.134725\ldots$ the first positive zero of $\Xi$ (simple), $m^*(a)=\min\{m\ge0:b_m(a)<0\}$, and $y_{z,t}$ the even solution of $y''+(t^2-zu^2)y=0$ with $y(0)=1$, $y'(0)=0$. Then for every $0<\delta<\gamma_1$ and $a$ small, $b_m(a)>0$ for all $m$ with $t_m\le\gamma_1-\delta$, the index $m^*(a)$ exists, and $\lim_{a\to0}4a^2m^*(a)=\gamma_1^2$. If $\gamma_a$ is the unique zero near $\gamma_1$ of $t\mapsto\int\Phi(u)y_{a^4,t}(u)du$, then $\gamma_a=\gamma_1-a^4Q(\gamma_1)/\Xi'(\gamma_1)+O(a^8)$ and $m^*(a)=\lfloor(\gamma_a^2/a^2-1)/4\rfloor+1$ for small $a$.

Source: [`ch/tr2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr2.tex), label `tr:cor:first`.

<a id="verified_sign_changes_of_hermite_coefficients_with_a_turing_bound_certify_all_zeros"></a>

### A verified sign change count of the Hermite coefficients together with an upper bound on the zero count proves real and simple zeros

Proposition 28.10.2, page 1019 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the P\'olya kernel, positive and even, and $\Xi(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ the Riemann Xi function. Let $h_n(x)=\pi^{-1/4}(2^nn!)^{-1/2}H_n(x)e^{-x^2/2}$ be the orthonormal Hermite functions, with $H_n$ the physicists' Hermite polynomials. For a scale $a>0$ put $c_n(a)=\sqrt a\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)h_n(au)\,du$, $t_m=a\sqrt{4m+1}$ and $b_m(a)=\sqrt{2\pi}\,(-1)^mc_{2m}(a)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Xi(t)h_{2m}(t/a)a^{-1/2}\,dt$. Let $A_m(a)=\sqrt2\,\pi^{1/4}\sqrt a\sqrt{(2m)!}/(2^mm!)$ and $M_k(a_0)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)|u|^ke^{a_0^2u^2/2}du$. Let $\widetilde b_m/A_m$ be computed values of $b_m/A_m$ with rigorous errors $e_m$, and $E_m$ a rigorous bound for $|b_m/A_m-\Xi(t_m)|$ (for example $M_4(a_0)a^4/12$). If $|\widetilde b_m/A_m|>e_m+E_m$ then $\operatorname{sgn}\widetilde b_m=\operatorname{sgn}\Xi(t_m)$. Suppose there are $S$ sign changes at pairs of adjacent sampling points $t_m$ below $T$, all with this property. Then $\Xi$ has $S$ zeros in disjoint intervals, and if an independent rigorous method gives that the number $N(T)$ of zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $0<\Re t<T$ (the zeros $\frac12+it$ of $\zeta$ with ordinate in $(0,T)$), counted with multiplicity, is at most $S$ (Turing's method), then all zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $0<\Re t<T$ are real and simple.

Source: [`ch/tr2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr2.tex), label `tr:prop:verified`.

<a id="average_run_length_of_the_hermite_coefficient_signs_given_one_sign_change_per_zero"></a>

### If each simple zero gives one sign change the mean run of the Hermite coefficient signs is asymptotic to pi T over a squared log of T over 2 pi

Proposition 28.11.1, page 1020 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on the zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $T\le\Re t\le T+H$ are real and simple and the sign changes of $(b_m(a))$ with $t_m\in[T,T+H]$ correspond one to one to them.

Statement. Let $\Phi(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u/2}-3\pi n^2e^{5u/2})\exp(-\pi n^2e^{2u})$ be the P\'olya kernel, positive and even, and $\Xi(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)\cos(tu)\,du$ the Riemann Xi function. Let $h_n(x)=\pi^{-1/4}(2^nn!)^{-1/2}H_n(x)e^{-x^2/2}$ be the orthonormal Hermite functions, with $H_n$ the physicists' Hermite polynomials. For a scale $a>0$ put $c_n(a)=\sqrt a\int_{\mathbb R}\Phi(u)h_n(au)\,du$, $t_m=a\sqrt{4m+1}$ and $b_m(a)=\sqrt{2\pi}\,(-1)^mc_{2m}(a)=\int_{\mathbb R}\Xi(t)h_{2m}(t/a)a^{-1/2}\,dt$. Let $N(T)$ be the number of zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $0<\Re t<T$ (the zeros $\frac12+it$ of $\zeta$ with ordinate in $(0,T)$), counted with multiplicity. Assume the zeros $t$ of $\Xi$ with $T\le\Re t\le T+H$ are real and simple and the sign changes of $(b_m(a))$ with $t_m\in[T,T+H]$ correspond one to one to them. Then the mean number of coefficient steps per sign change is the number $TH/(2a^2)+O(H^2/a^2+1)$ of grid points in the window divided by $N(T+H)-N(T)=\frac H{2\pi}\log\frac T{2\pi}+O(H^2/T+\log T)$, and for fixed $a$, $H\to\infty$ and $H=o(T)$ the ratio is asymptotic to $\pi T/(a^2\log(T/2\pi))$.

Source: [`ch/tr2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/tr2.tex), label `tr:prop:run`.

## Chapter 29. Completeness of the secant dilates and the Moebius problem

<a id="completeness_of_the_secant_dilates_in_l1_with_the_weight_of_lerch"></a>

### The integer dilates of the hyperbolic secant are complete in L1 under an integrability condition at the origin and at infinity

Theorem 29.1.4, page 1025 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$ and let $g$ be a measurable function on $(0,\infty)$ with $\int_0^1|g(x)|x^{-1}dx+\int_1^\infty|g(x)|e^{-x}dx<\infty$. If $\int_0^\infty g(x)\operatorname{sech}(nx)\,dx=0$ for all $n\in\mathbb N$, then $g=0$ almost everywhere. The same holds with $\mathbb N$ replaced by a set $\Lambda\subset(0,\infty)$ containing an interval, provided the integrals $\int g\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\,dx$, $\lambda\in\Lambda$, converge absolutely and vanish. The proof uses $e^{-kx}=\frac12\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)\operatorname{sech}(nkx)$ for $k\in\mathbb N$, with $\mu$ the M\"obius function and $\chi_4$ the nonprincipal character modulo $4$, together with Lerch's theorem that $\int_0^\infty e^{-kx}h(x)\,dx=0$ for all $k\in\mathbb N$ forces $h=0$ when $\int|h|e^{-x}<\infty$.

Source: [`ch/lv1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lv1.tex), label `lv:thm:L1`.

<a id="mobius_secant_series_converges_in_every_weight_with_c_at_least_one"></a>

### The Möbius secant series converges to the exponential in every weight W_c with c at least one

Theorem 29.2.2, page 1027 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$, let $\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots$ be the Dirichlet beta function, with $\chi_4$ the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, let $\mu$ be the M\"obius function, $M_\chi(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)$ and $S_N(x)=\frac12\sum_{n\le N}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)\operatorname{sech}(nx)$. For $c\ge1$, $S_N\to e^{-x}$ in $\mathcal W_c$, that is $\|S_N-e^{-x}\|_c\to0$. For $c>1$ this follows from $|\sum_{n\le N}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)n^{-s}|\le\zeta(c)$ and dominated convergence in the Mellin Plancherel formula; for $c=1$ it follows from the prime number theorem $M_\chi(x)\ll x\exp(-a\sqrt{\log x})$ for some $a>0$ and partial summation.

Source: [`ch/lv1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lv1.tex), label `lv:thm:c1`.

<a id="single_weight_completeness_of_secant_dilates_is_unconditional_by_carleman"></a>

### In one weight the secant dilates over any set of dilations with divergent reciprocal sum are complete, whatever the zeros of the beta function do

Theorem 29.3.2, page 1028 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$. Let $c>0$ and let $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$ satisfy $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty$. Then $\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is complete in $\mathcal W_c$, that is, a function of $\mathcal W_c$ orthogonal to every $\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)$ is zero. In particular the integer dilates $\operatorname{sech}(nx)$ and the prime dilates $\operatorname{sech}(px)$, $p$ prime, are complete in every $\mathcal W_c$, including $c=\frac12$. The proof writes the Mellin transform of the orthogonal function against $\Gamma(c+it)\beta(c+it)$ and applies Carleman's formula to an analytic function on the right half plane that vanishes on $\Lambda$.

Source: [`ch/lv1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lv1.tex), label `lv:thm:single`.

<a id="two_weight_necessity_zero_free_strip_for_the_beta_function"></a>

### Completeness of the exponential in two weights forces a zero free strip for the beta function

Proposition 29.5.1, page 1030 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$, let $\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots$ be the Dirichlet beta function, with $\chi_4$ the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, and let $0<a<b$ with $\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b$ normed by $\|f\|_a+\|f\|_b$. If $e^{-x}$ is a limit in $\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b$ of finite linear combinations of the functions $\operatorname{sech}(nx)$, $n\in\mathbb N$, then $\beta(s)\ne0$ for $a<\Re s<b$.

Source: [`ch/lv1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lv1.tex), label `lv:prop:nec`.

<a id="two_weight_criterion_zero_free_half_plane_for_the_beta_function"></a>

### Two weight completeness of the secant dilates is equivalent to a zero free half plane for L(s,chi_4) and to convergence of the Möbius secant series

Theorem 29.5.2, page 1030 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$, let $\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots$ be the Dirichlet beta function, with $\chi_4$ the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, and let $\mu$ be the M\"obius function, $M_\chi(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)$ and $S_N(x)=\frac12\sum_{n\le N}\mu(n)\chi_4(n)\operatorname{sech}(nx)$. For $\frac12\le\theta<1$ the following are equivalent: (i) $L(s,\chi_4)\ne0$ for $\Re s>\theta$; (ii) $\{\operatorname{sech}(nx)\}_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is complete in $\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b$ (normed by $\|f\|_a+\|f\|_b$) for all $\theta<a<b<1$; (iii) $S_N\to e^{-x}$ in $\mathcal W_c$ for every $c\in(\theta,1)$. With $\theta=\frac12$, (i) is the generalised Riemann hypothesis for $L(s,\chi_4)$. When these hold, $\|S_N-e^{-x}\|_c=O_\varepsilon(N^{\theta-c+\varepsilon})$ for $c\in(\theta,1)$.

Source: [`ch/lv1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lv1.tex), label `lv:thm:two`.

<a id="zeta_version_one_weight_completeness_and_two_weight_criterion_for_the_bose_kernel"></a>

### The zeta analogue: dilates of the Bose kernel with its pole removed are complete in one weight and in two weights exactly when zeta has the corresponding zero free half plane

Theorem 29.6.1, page 1031 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$, let $\varphi(x)=1/(e^x-1)-1/x$ (so $\varphi\in\mathcal W_c$ exactly for $0<c<1$ and $\int_0^\infty x^{s-1}\varphi(x)\,dx=\Gamma(s)\zeta(s)$ for $0<\Re s<1$), let $\mu$ be the M\"obius function, $M(x)=\sum_{n\le x}\mu(n)$ and $T_N(x)=\sum_{n\le N}\mu(n)\varphi(nx)$. (1) For every $c\in(0,1)$ the dilates $\{\varphi(nx)\}_{n\in\mathbb N}$ are complete in $\mathcal W_c$, unconditionally. (2) Let $\frac12\le\theta<1$ and suppose $M(x)=O_\varepsilon(x^{\theta+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. Then $T_N\to e^{-x}$ in $\mathcal W_c$ with $\|T_N-e^{-x}\|_c=O_\varepsilon(N^{\theta-c+\varepsilon})$ for $\theta<c<1$ and $0<\varepsilon<c-\theta$. (3) For $\frac12\le\theta<1$, completeness of $\{\varphi(nx)\}$ in $\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b$ for all $\theta<a<b<1$ is equivalent to $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\Re s>\theta$ (the pole at $1$ being allowed); with $\theta=\frac12$ it is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis.

Source: [`ch/lv1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lv1.tex), label `lv:thm:zeta`.

<a id="necessity_of_the_divergence_condition_for_completeness_in_one_weight"></a>

### Under a polynomial bound for the reciprocal of the beta function on the line, the secant dilates over a set with convergent reciprocal sum are not complete

Theorem 29.10.2, page 1035 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$ and let $\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots$ be the Dirichlet beta function, with $\chi_4$ the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$. Let $c>0$ and assume $(\mathrm N_c)$: $1/\beta(c+it)\ll(1+|t|)^{A}$ for some $A\ge0$ and all real $t$. If $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$ and $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda<\infty$, then $\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is not complete in $\mathcal W_c$. So under $(\mathrm N_c)$ the dilates are complete in $\mathcal W_c$ if and only if $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty$. The hypothesis $(\mathrm N_c)$ holds unconditionally for $c\ge1$ and fails at $c=\frac12$, where $\beta$ has zeros on the line.

Source: [`ch/lv2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lv2.tex), label `lv:thm:nec`.

<a id="necessity_and_sufficiency_of_divergent_reciprocal_sum_for_the_secant_dilates_conditional"></a>

### The secant dilates are complete in W_c if and only if the reciprocal sum of the dilations diverges, for c at least one, for c above 7/8 given a zero free half plane, and for c not one half under GRH

Corollary 29.10.3, page 1036 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on The zero free half plane $\Re s>\frac78$ for $L(s,\chi_4)$, which holds if the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI, announced for Dirichlet $L$ functions, unrefereed and not checked for this book) cover the character modulo $4$; the part for $c\ge1$ is unconditional, and the part for $c\ne\frac12$ needs the generalised Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$.

Statement. For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$ and let $\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots$ be the Dirichlet beta function, with $\chi_4$ the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$. For $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$, $\{\operatorname{sech}(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is complete in $\mathcal W_c$ if and only if $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty$, in each of these cases: for $c\ge1$ (unconditionally); for $c>\frac78$ given that $L(s,\chi_4)\ne0$ for $\Re s>\frac78$; and for every $c>0$ with $c\ne\frac12$ under the generalised Riemann hypothesis for $\beta$.

Source: [`ch/lv2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lv2.tex), label `lv:cor:iff`.

<a id="salem_criterion_for_the_fermi_and_secant_kernels_on_a_divergent_set_of_dilations"></a>

### Salem's criterion in L1: dilates of the Fermi or secant kernel over a divergent set are complete if and only if the Mellin transform has no zero on the line

Theorem 29.11.1, page 1037 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\sigma>0$, let $k$ be $1/(e^x+1)$ or $\operatorname{sech}x$, and let $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$ satisfy $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty$. Then $\{x^{\sigma-1}k(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is complete in $L^1(0,\infty)$ if and only if the Mellin transform of $k$ has no zero on the line $\Re s=\sigma$. In particular, for $\frac12<\sigma<1$ the integer dilates of the Fermi kernel $1/(e^x+1)$ are complete in $L^1$ if and only if the Riemann zeta function has no zero on $\Re s=\sigma$, and the integer dilates of $\operatorname{sech}$ if and only if the Dirichlet beta function $\beta=L(\cdot,\chi_4)$ has none.

Source: [`ch/lv2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lv2.tex), label `lv:thm:salem`.

<a id="residual_identity_for_the_weighted_error_of_arbitrary_secant_combinations"></a>

### The weighted error of an arbitrary combination of secant dilates is an integral over the Mellin line with the factor 2 in 2D_N - 1/beta, split at a segment

Proposition 29.12.1, page 1040 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$, let $\beta(s)=L(s,\chi_4)=1-3^{-s}+5^{-s}-\cdots$ be the Dirichlet beta function, with $\chi_4$ the nonprincipal Dirichlet character modulo $4$, $c>0$, $T\ge1$ and $a_n$ arbitrary complex coefficients, with $D_N(s)=\sum_{n\le N}a_nn^{-s}$, $\|a\|_{N,c}=\sum_{n\le N}|a_n|n^{-c}$ and $K_c(t)=\Gamma(c+it)\beta(c+it)$. Then $\|e^{-x}-\sum_{n\le N}a_n\operatorname{sech}(nx)\|_c^2=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}|\Gamma(c+it)|^2|1-2\beta(c+it)D_N(c+it)|^2dt$, and this is at most $\frac1{2\pi}\int_{|t|\le T}|\Gamma(c+it)|^2|1-2\beta D_N|^2dt+C_ce^{-\pi T}T^{2c}(1+\|a\|_{N,c})^2$ for a constant $C_c$ depending only on $c$. Where $\beta\ne0$ the integrand of the first term is $|K_c(t)|^2|2D_N-1/\beta|^2$. The Mellin transform of $\operatorname{sech}(nx)$ carries the factor $2$, which is why $2D_N-1/\beta$ appears and not $D_N-1/\beta$.

Source: [`ch/lv2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lv2.tex), label `lv:prop:segment`.

<a id="mellin_transform_of_the_meixner_density_in_terms_of_an_entire_dirichlet_type_series"></a>

### The Mellin transform of the symmetric Meixner density of order t is an explicit multiple of an entire Dirichlet type series Z_t

Theorem 29.13.1, page 1041 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. For $t>0$ let $f_t(x)=|\Gamma(\frac t2+\frac{ix}2)|^2$, $x>0$. For $0<\Re s<1$, $M_t(s)=\int_0^\infty x^{s-1}f_t(x)\,dx=2^s\pi\,\Gamma(t)Z_t(1-s)/\sin(\pi s/2)$, where $Z_t$ is the entire function $Z_t(w)=\Gamma(w)^{-1}\int_0^\infty u^{w-1}(2\cosh(u/2))^{-t}\,du=\sum_{k\ge0}(-1)^k\binom{t+k-1}{k}(k+\frac t2)^{-w}$ for $\Re w>t-1$. With $\beta$ the Dirichlet beta function, $\eta(w)=(1-2^{1-w})\zeta(w)$ the Dirichlet eta function and $\zeta$ the Riemann zeta function, $Z_1(w)=2^w\beta(w)$, $Z_2(w)=\eta(w-1)=(1-2^{2-w})\zeta(w-1)$ and $Z_3(w)=2^{w-3}(\beta(w)-\beta(w-2))$. For integer $t$, $Z_t$ is a linear combination of $\eta(w-j)$, $j$ odd, when $t$ is even, and of $2^{w-2i}\beta(w-2i)$ when $t$ is odd.

Source: [`ch/lv2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lv2.tex), label `lv:thm:meixner`.

<a id="one_weight_completeness_throughout_the_meixner_family"></a>

### The dilates of every symmetric Meixner density are complete in every weight over a set of dilations with divergent reciprocal sum

Corollary 29.13.2, page 1042 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$ and $f_t(x)=|\Gamma(\frac t2+\frac{ix}2)|^2$ for $t>0$. For every $t>0$ and every $c>0$, $\{f_t(\lambda x)\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ with $\Lambda\subset[1,\infty)$ is complete in $\mathcal W_c$ whenever $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}1/\lambda=\infty$; in particular the integer dilates are complete. The proof checks that $f_t\in\mathcal W_c$ and that its Mellin transform on $\Re s=c$ is nonzero almost everywhere with the bound $C(1+|\tau|)^Ae^{-\pi|\tau|/2}$, the only properties used in the proof of single weight completeness.

Source: [`ch/lv2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lv2.tex), label `lv:cor:meixner`.

<a id="order_two_meixner_kernel_gives_an_unconditional_mobius_route"></a>

### For the cosecant kernel the Möbius series for x e^{-x} converges in every weight, so completeness holds unconditionally in one and two weights

Theorem 29.13.3, page 1043 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. For $c>0$ let $\mathcal W_c=L^2((0,\infty),x^{2c-1}dx)$ and $\operatorname{sech}=1/\cosh$ and let $\mu$ be the M\"obius function, $c_n=\mu(n)$ for odd $n$ and $c_n=0$ for even $n$, and $\operatorname{csch}=1/\sinh$. Then for every $x>0$, with absolute convergence, $e^{-x}=\frac12\sum_{n\ge1}c_n\operatorname{csch}(nx)$ and $xe^{-x}=\frac12\sum_{n\ge1}(c_n/n)(nx)\operatorname{csch}(nx)$, and $\sum_n(c_n/n)n^{-s}=1/((1-2^{-s-1})\zeta(s+1))$ converges absolutely for $\Re s>0$. Consequently the series for $xe^{-x}$ converges absolutely in every $\mathcal W_c$, $c>0$, and $\{(nx)\operatorname{csch}(nx)\}_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is complete in every $\mathcal W_c$ and in every $\mathcal W_a\cap\mathcal W_b$, $0<a<b$, unconditionally.

Source: [`ch/lv2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lv2.tex), label `lv:thm:t2`.

<a id="thorin_form_of_the_two_weight_criterion_for_the_reciprocal_xi_function"></a>

### A zero free half plane for Xi is equivalent to F_theta being a GGC Laplace transform, with Thorin measure a sum of squared folded Cauchy laws centred at the ordinates

Theorem 29.14.2, page 1045 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Xi$ be either the Riemann function $\xi$ or $\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$ with $\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)\beta(s)$; both are entire of order one, real and positive on the real axis, satisfy $\Xi(s)=\Xi(1-s)$ and have the Hadamard product $\Xi(s)=\Xi(0)\prod_\rho(1-s/\rho)$ over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$, paired with $\bar\rho$. For $\theta\ge\frac12$ let $F_\theta(s)=\Xi(\theta)/\Xi(\theta+\sqrt s)$ for $s$ in the plane cut along $(-\infty,0]$, with the principal square root. A probability law on $[0,\infty)$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if its Laplace transform is $\exp(-as-\int_0^\infty\log(1+s/u)U(du))$ with $a\ge0$ and a locally finite positive Thorin measure $U$ on $(0,\infty)$ with $\int_{(0,1)}|\log u|U(du)<\infty$ and $\int_1^\infty u^{-1}U(du)<\infty$. For $a\ge0$ and $\gamma>0$ let $Q_{0,\gamma}=\delta_{\gamma^2}$ and, for $a>0$, $Q_{a,\gamma}$ be the probability measure on $(0,\infty)$ that is the image under $v\mapsto v^2$ of the law of $|\gamma+aC|$ with $C$ standard Cauchy, with density $\frac1{2\pi\sqrt u}[\frac a{a^2+(\sqrt u-\gamma)^2}+\frac a{a^2+(\sqrt u+\gamma)^2}]$. Let $\theta\ge\frac12$. The following are equivalent: (i) $\Xi$ has no zeros in $\Re s>\theta$; (ii) $F_\theta$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC; (iii) $F_\theta$ is analytic in the cut plane. When they hold, the Thorin measure of $F_\theta$ is $U_\theta=\sum_{\rho,\ \Im\rho>0}m_\rho Q_{\theta-\Re\rho,\ \Im\rho}$ over the distinct zeros $\rho$ in the upper half plane with multiplicity $m_\rho$, and $F_\theta(s)=\exp(-\int_0^\infty\log(1+s/u)U_\theta(du))$ with no linear term. For $\Xi=\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$, (i) is equivalent to two weight completeness of the secant dilates on $(\theta,1)$ (for $\theta<1$, the two weight criterion for $\beta$); for $\Xi=\xi$, to two weight completeness of the dilates of $\varphi(x)=1/(e^x-1)-1/x$ (the zeta version of the two weight criterion).

Source: [`ch/lv2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lv2.tex), label `lv:thm:thorin`.

<a id="thorin_representations_of_reciprocal_xi_above_the_zero_free_abscissa"></a>

### Reciprocal xi and reciprocal xi of chi_4 are GGC Laplace transforms from theta equal to one unconditionally and from 7/8 given the zero free half plane

Corollary 29.14.3, page 1045 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on The zero free half plane $\Re s>\frac78$ for the Riemann zeta function and, for the statement about $\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$, for $L(s,\chi_4)$, from the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI, unrefereed, announced for Dirichlet $L$ functions; that the theorem covers the character modulo $4$ has not been checked); the part for $\theta\ge1$ is unconditional.

Statement. Let $\Xi$ be either the Riemann function $\xi$ or $\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$ with $\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)\beta(s)$; both are entire of order one, real and positive on the real axis, satisfy $\Xi(s)=\Xi(1-s)$ and have the Hadamard product $\Xi(s)=\Xi(0)\prod_\rho(1-s/\rho)$ over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$, paired with $\bar\rho$. For $\theta\ge\frac12$ let $F_\theta(s)=\Xi(\theta)/\Xi(\theta+\sqrt s)$ for $s$ in the plane cut along $(-\infty,0]$, with the principal square root. A probability law on $[0,\infty)$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if its Laplace transform is $\exp(-as-\int_0^\infty\log(1+s/u)U(du))$ with $a\ge0$ and a locally finite positive Thorin measure $U$ on $(0,\infty)$ with $\int_{(0,1)}|\log u|U(du)<\infty$ and $\int_1^\infty u^{-1}U(du)<\infty$. Let $U_\theta=\sum_{\Im\rho>0}m_\rho Q_{\theta-\Re\rho,\Im\rho}$, over the distinct zeros $\rho$ with $\Im\rho>0$ and with $m_\rho$ the multiplicity of $\rho$, be the Thorin measure of $F_\theta$ when $\Xi$ has no zeros in $\Re s>\theta$, where for $a\ge0$ and $\gamma>0$, $Q_{0,\gamma}=\delta_{\gamma^2}$ and, for $a>0$, $Q_{a,\gamma}$ is the image under $v\mapsto v^2$ of the law of $|\gamma+aC|$ with $C$ standard Cauchy. For every $\theta\ge1$, $F_\theta$ for $\xi$ and for $\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC with the absolutely continuous Thorin measure $U_\theta$, since the zeros have $\Re\rho<1$. Conditionally on the zero free half plane $\Re s>\frac78$ the GGC representation holds for every $\theta\ge\frac78$, and the Thorin measure is absolutely continuous for $\theta>\frac78$, and at $\theta=\frac78$ if no zero lies on $\Re s=\frac78$; a zero $\rho$ on that line contributes an atom $m_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho^2}$, $\gamma_\rho=\Im\rho$. For $\theta=\frac12$ the statement for $\xi$ is the Riemann Hypothesis and the Thorin measure is then $\sum_{\gamma>0}m_\gamma\delta_{\gamma^2}$, over the ordinates $\gamma>0$ of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ of $\xi$ with multiplicity $m_\gamma$.

Source: [`ch/lv2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lv2.tex), label `lv:cor:uncond`.

<a id="cauchy_semigroup_of_thorin_measures_of_the_reciprocal_xi_function"></a>

### The symmetrised Thorin measures of F_theta form a Cauchy convolution semigroup in theta

Theorem 29.14.4, page 1046 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Xi$ be either the Riemann function $\xi$ or $\xi(\cdot,\chi_4)$ with $\xi(s,\chi_4)=(4/\pi)^{(s+1)/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)\beta(s)$; both are entire of order one, real and positive on the real axis, satisfy $\Xi(s)=\Xi(1-s)$ and have the Hadamard product $\Xi(s)=\Xi(0)\prod_\rho(1-s/\rho)$ over the nontrivial zeros $\rho$, paired with $\bar\rho$. For $\theta\ge\frac12$ let $F_\theta(s)=\Xi(\theta)/\Xi(\theta+\sqrt s)$ for $s$ in the plane cut along $(-\infty,0]$, with the principal square root. A probability law on $[0,\infty)$ is a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) if its Laplace transform is $\exp(-as-\int_0^\infty\log(1+s/u)U(du))$ with $a\ge0$ and a locally finite positive Thorin measure $U$ on $(0,\infty)$ with $\int_{(0,1)}|\log u|U(du)<\infty$ and $\int_1^\infty u^{-1}U(du)<\infty$. Let $\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,a)$ be the Cauchy law of centre $\gamma$ and scale $a>0$ and $\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,0)=\delta_\gamma$, and let $U_\theta=\sum_{\Im\rho>0}m_\rho Q_{\theta-\Re\rho,\Im\rho}$, over the distinct zeros $\rho$ with $\Im\rho>0$ and with $m_\rho$ the multiplicity of $\rho$, be the Thorin measure of $F_\theta$ when $\Xi$ has no zeros in $\Re s>\theta$, where for $a\ge0$ and $\gamma>0$, $Q_{0,\gamma}=\delta_{\gamma^2}$ and, for $a>0$, $Q_{a,\gamma}$ is the image under $v\mapsto v^2$ of the law of $|\gamma+aC|$ with $C$ standard Cauchy. Suppose $\Xi$ has no zeros in $\Re s>\theta_0$. For $\theta\ge\theta_0$ let $\widetilde U_\theta=\frac12\sum_\rho m_\rho\,\mathrm{Cauchy}(\Im\rho,\theta-\Re\rho)$ be the symmetric measure on $\mathbb R$ in the variable $v$, summed over the distinct zeros $\rho$ of both half planes with multiplicity $m_\rho$ (the factor $\frac12$ is needed: without it the image is $2U_\theta$). Then $U_\theta$ is the image of $\widetilde U_\theta$ under $v\mapsto v^2$, and for $\theta_0\le\theta<\theta'$, $\widetilde U_{\theta'}=\widetilde U_\theta*\mathrm{Cauchy}(0,\theta'-\theta)$. In particular, if all zeros lie on $\Re s=\theta_0$ (which for the completed functions forces $\theta_0=\frac12$), then $\widetilde U_\theta$ is the Poisson smoothing at width $\theta-\theta_0$ of $\frac12\sum_\rho m_\rho\delta_{\Im\rho}$ and converges vaguely to it as $\theta\downarrow\theta_0$. For $\xi$ this is the Cauchy flow of the book's Poisson structure result, credited to Nicholas Polson (Chapter 8 of his monograph On Hilbert's 8th Problem, 2026).

Source: [`ch/lv2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lv2.tex), label `lv:thm:semigroup`.

## Chapter 30. The Thorin measure at level one and the backward Cauchy flow

<a id="level_one_thorin_measure_explicit_density_with_prime_sum"></a>

### The Thorin measure of reciprocal xi is absolutely continuous with the explicit density (1/pi) Re xi'/xi at every level from one

Theorem 30.1.1, page 1051 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$, let $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ run over its zeros with multiplicity, $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, and for $\theta>\sigma_\rho$ for every $\rho$ (in particular for every $\theta>1$, and also for $\theta=1$ because $\zeta(1+it)\ne0$) let $\mathfrak U_\theta=\sum_\rho\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma_\rho,\theta-\sigma_\rho)$ be the positive measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with $\int\mathfrak U_\theta(dv)/(1+v^2)<\infty$, where $\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,c)$ has density $(c/\pi)/(c^2+(v-\gamma)^2)$. Then $\mathfrak U_\theta$ is absolutely continuous with real analytic density $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\theta+iv)=\frac1\pi\partial_\sigma\log|\xi(\sigma+iv)|$ at $\sigma=\theta$, and $\mathfrak U_\theta((0,V])=\frac1\pi\arg\xi(\theta+iV)$ for the branch with $\arg\xi(\theta)=0$. At $\theta=1$, for every real $v$, $u_1(v)=\frac1\pi\bigl[\frac1{1+v^2}-\frac{\log\pi}2+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(\frac{1+iv}2)-\lim_{X\to\infty}\bigl(\sum_{n\le X}\frac{\Lambda(n)}n\cos(v\log n)-\frac{\sin(v\log X)}{v}\bigr)\bigr]$, where $\sin(v\log X)/v$ means $\log X$ at $v=0$; the limit exists locally uniformly, equals $\operatorname{Re}C(1+iv)$ with $C(s)=-\zeta'(s)/\zeta(s)-1/(s-1)$, and $u_1(0)=(2+\gamma_E-\log4\pi)/(2\pi)$ with $\gamma_E$ Euler's constant, while the cosine series itself has no limit. For $\theta>1$, $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\bigl[\frac\theta{\theta^2+v^2}+\frac{\theta-1}{(\theta-1)^2+v^2}-\frac{\log\pi}2+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Gamma'}{\Gamma}(\frac{\theta+iv}2)-\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)n^{-\theta}\cos(v\log n)\bigr]$ with the prime sum absolutely convergent.

Source: [`ch/lo1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lo1.tex), label `lo:thm:density`.

<a id="fourier_transform_of_the_level_one_thorin_measure_is_a_sum_of_prime_atoms"></a>

### The Fourier transform of the level one Thorin measure carries the prime powers as atoms, an explicit formula for one test function

Proposition 30.2.1, page 1053 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. With $\mathfrak U_1=\sum_\rho\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma_\rho,1-\sigma_\rho)$ the level one Thorin measure of $\xi$ (zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$), $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, $P_c(v)=(c/\pi)/(c^2+v^2)$, $\widehat f(\omega)=\int e^{-i\omega v}f(v)\,dv$, and for $\theta\ge1$ $g_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi[\theta/(\theta^2+v^2)-\frac12\log\pi+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\frac{\Gamma'}\Gamma(\frac{\theta+iv}2)]$: as tempered distributions $\widehat{\mathfrak U_1}(\omega)=\widehat{g_1}(\omega)+1-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}n(\delta_{\log n}+\delta_{-\log n})(\omega)$, the constant $1$ being the transform of the atom at $0$ that the pole of $\zeta$ contributes in the limit $\theta\downarrow1$, and on the zero side $\widehat{\mathfrak U_1}(\omega)=\sum_\rho e^{-(1-\sigma_\rho)|\omega|}e^{-i\omega\gamma_\rho}$ as the limit of the sums over $|\gamma_\rho|<T$. Equivalently, for every Schwartz function $\varphi$, $\sum_\rho(P_{1-\sigma_\rho}*\varphi)(\gamma_\rho)=\int g_1\varphi\,dv+\varphi(0)-\frac1{2\pi}\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}n(\widehat\varphi(\log n)+\widehat\varphi(-\log n))$. For $\theta\ge1$, $\mathfrak U_\theta=P_{\theta-1}*\mathfrak U_1$ and $\widehat{\mathfrak U_\theta}(\omega)=e^{-(\theta-1)|\omega|}\widehat{\mathfrak U_1}(\omega)$, which replaces $\Lambda(n)/n$ by $\Lambda(n)n^{-\theta}$ on the prime side.

Source: [`ch/lo1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lo1.tex), label `lo:prop:spectrum`.

<a id="backward_cauchy_flow_converges_exactly_when_zeta_has_the_zero_free_half_plane"></a>

### Dichotomy for the band limited backward Cauchy flow from level one: convergence at level theta' if and only if zeta has no zeros to the right of theta'

Theorem 30.3.1, page 1056 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\frac12\le\theta'<1$, $a=1-\theta'$, $\mathfrak U_\theta=\sum_\rho\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma_\rho,\theta-\sigma_\rho)$ the Thorin measure at level $\theta$ of $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$, over its zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ with multiplicity ($\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,c)$ the Cauchy law of centre $\gamma$ and width $c$, $\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,0)=\delta_\gamma$), $\Phi_\Omega(v)=(1-\cos\Omega v)/(\pi\Omega v^2)$ the Fejér kernel, and $K_{\theta',\Omega}$ the inverse Fourier transform of $(1-|\omega|/\Omega)_+e^{a|\omega|}$. The band limited backward flow is $B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1=\mathfrak U_1*K_{\theta',\Omega}$. (i) If $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$, then $B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1=\mathfrak U_{\theta'}*\Phi_\Omega$, which converges vaguely to $\mathfrak U_{\theta'}$ as $\Omega\to\infty$, with $\int B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1(v)\,dv/(v^2+s)\to\int\mathfrak U_{\theta'}(dv)/(v^2+s)$ for every $s>0$; if moreover $\theta'>\sigma_\rho$ for every zero the convergence is locally uniform as densities. (ii) If $\zeta$ has a zero $\rho$ with $\sigma_\rho>\theta'$, there is no signed measure $\mu$ with $\int|\mu|(dv)/(1+v^2)<\infty$ such that $\int B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1(v)\,dv/(v^2+s)\to\int\mu(dv)/(v^2+s)$ as $\Omega\to\infty$ for all large $s$. Hence the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to convergence of the flow at every $\theta'>\frac12$.

Source: [`ch/lo1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lo1.tex), label `lo:thm:dichotomy`.
