<a id="computed_backward_flow_locates_109_zeros_from_samples_on_the_line_one"></a>

### Computation: the Fourier backward flow from samples of the level one density on Re s = 1 places a peak within 0.035 of each of 109 zeros

Result 30.3.1, page 1057 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. The computation samples the level one Thorin density $u_1(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(1+iv)$, $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$, on $[0,400]$ at spacing $0.05$ from $\zeta$ and $\zeta'$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=1$ only (the Arb library (python flint) balls at $128$ bits, with the analytic value of $u_1(0)$), applies a Hann window and the backward multiplier $e^{(1-\theta')|\omega|}$ with a cutoff at $\Omega$, and inverts. A peak is a local maximum of the output in $100<v<300$ of height at least a quarter of the maximum, and the $109$ zeros of $\zeta$ in that range are those counted by $N(300)-N(100)=138-29$. With a sharp cutoff the output at $\theta'=0.75$, $\Omega=40$ has $109$ peaks, each within $0.035$ of a zero, and is positive; at $\theta'=0.5$, $\Omega=40$ it has $109$ peaks within $0.027$ of the zeros and minimum $-3.2$; at $\theta'=0.5$, $\Omega=60$ it has $213$ peaks, $109$ at the zeros, error $0.042$ and minimum $-16.5$, which is ringing of the cutoff. With the Fejér window at $\theta'=0.5$, $\Omega=60$ it has $109$ peaks, error $0.025$ and minimum $-0.020$. The statement covers only these runs, and the sharp cutoff is not covered by the convergence theorem for the backward flow.

Source: [`ch/lo1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lo1.tex), label `lo:res:flow`.

<a id="positive_deconvolution_of_the_level_one_density_and_the_total_kl_residual"></a>

### A positive solution of the Cauchy deconvolution of the level one density exists exactly when zeta has the zero free half plane, and the total Kullback Leibler residual detects it

Proposition 30.4.1, page 1060 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\theta'\in[\frac12,1)$, $a=1-\theta'$, $P_a(v)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+v^2)$, $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ with zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$, $\mathfrak U_\theta=\sum_\rho\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma_\rho,\theta-\sigma_\rho)$ its Thorin measure at level $\theta$ (defined when no zero has $\sigma_\rho>\theta$; $\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma,0)=\delta_\gamma$), and $u_1(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(1+iv)$ the density of $\mathfrak U_1$. (a) There is a positive measure $x$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with $\int x(dv)/(1+v^2)<\infty$ and $P_a*x=u_1$ if and only if $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$; it is then unique and equals $\mathfrak U_{\theta'}$. (b) Let $h_k\to0$ and $L_k\to\infty$ with $h_k^2L_k\log L_k\to0$, let $v_i\in h_k\mathbb{Z}\cap[-L_k,L_k]$, $y_i=u_1(v_i)$, and $D_k=\inf_xh_k\sum_i\bigl(y_i\log\frac{y_i}{m_i(x)}-y_i+m_i(x)\bigr)$, with the infimum over positive measures $x$ on the grid $h_k\mathbb{Z}$ with $\sum_jx_j/(1+j^2h_k^2)<\infty$ and $m_i(x)=(P_a*x)(v_i)$. Then $D_k\to0$ if $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$, and $\liminf_kD_k>0$ if it has one.

Source: [`ch/lo2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lo2.tex), label `lo:prop:emres`.

<a id="computed_em_injection_test_separates_an_off_line_quartet_from_a_control"></a>

### Computation: the EM inversion of the level one density separates an injected off line quartet of zeros from a control

Result 30.4.4, page 1063 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. The computation runs the EM iteration for the Cauchy deconvolution of the level one Thorin density $u_1(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(1+iv)$ of $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ on the data window $[100,300]$ (unknown on $[80,320]$, spacing $0.05$) and on $[150,250]$, with the total Kullback Leibler residual as the plain sum over the data points. The two zeros nearest the centre of the window ($\gamma=198.0153$ and $201.2648$) are replaced by a quartet $\rho,1-\bar\rho,\bar\rho,1-\rho$ with real part $\sigma$ at their midpoint, total mass kept to $10^{-4}$, and compared with a control of two line zeros at the midpoint. At $\theta'=0.75$, $\sigma=0.85$ the quartet residual after $10^4$ steps is $7.03\times10^{-3}$ on both windows to $0.3$ per cent, a floor, while the control and the real data fall below $10^{-7}$. At $\theta'=0.5$, $\sigma=0.75$ the quartet residual is $1.85\times10^{-2}$ against $1.08\times10^{-3}$ for the control and has not reached a floor. At $\theta'=0.75=\sigma$ the residual keeps decaying, more slowly than the control. The statement covers only these runs: a finite run certifies neither the existence nor the nonexistence of a positive solution.

Source: [`ch/lo2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lo2.tex), label `lo:res:inject`.

<a id="computed_gbc_under_a_gue_prior_counts_zeros_in_unit_bins_from_the_level_one_density"></a>

### Computation: generative Bayesian computation under a GUE prior counts the zeros of zeta in unit bins from the level one Thorin density

Result 30.5.2, page 1064 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ and $u_1(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(1+iv)$ its level one Thorin density. The computation trains, for two seeds, a quantile network (two hidden layers of $256$ rectified units, pinball loss, quantile levels $0.1$, $0.5$, $0.9$) on $24000$ simulated windows in which the ordinates of the zeros are eigenvalues of a GUE matrix of size $400$ unfolded to a density drawn uniformly from $[0.45,0.8]$, all zeros on the critical line; the input is the sum of Cauchy densities of width $\frac12$ at the simulated ordinates on a grid of spacing $0.1$, plus the Cauchy smoothing of the mean density for the zeros beyond, and the targets are the counts of zeros in eight unit bins at the centre of a window of length $16$. On the $25$ windows of the real $u_1$ centred at $v=150,158,\dots,342$ ($200$ bins) the rounded posterior median equals the true count in $196$ and $197$ bins and is within one of it in all $200$; on held out simulations the interval $[q_{0.1},q_{0.9}]$ covers $0.806$ and $0.796$ of the counts (nominal $0.8$), and $0.805$ and $0.775$ on the real windows. The formulation is heuristic and the statement covers only these runs: the prior puts every zero on the critical line, and the network counts zeros in bins and does not locate them.

Source: [`ch/lo2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lo2.tex), label `lo:res:gbc`.

<a id="open_implementation_of_the_data_augmentation_sampler_and_gbc_inversion_for_level_one"></a>

### Open problem: the data augmentation sampler and a generative Bayesian inversion with the EM reconstruction as a feature

Problem 30.1, page 1067 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Let $u_1(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(1+iv)$ be the level one Thorin density of $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$. Implement a data augmentation Gibbs sampler for the Cauchy deconvolution of $u_1$ and compare its posterior spread at $\theta'=0.75$ and $\theta'=0.5$ with the EM point estimate; then build a generative Bayesian computation inversion with the EM reconstruction as an input feature and the positions of the zeros as continuous outputs, and calibrate its quantiles on held out simulations.

Source: [`ch/lo2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lo2.tex), label `lo:prob:sampler`.

<a id="open_characterisation_of_level_one_thorin_densities_in_the_selberg_class"></a>

### Open problem: characterise the level one Thorin densities of functions of the Selberg class without reference to zeros

Problem 30.2, page 1067 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Characterise, without reference to zeros, the functions $\frac1\pi[g(v)-\lim_{X\to\infty}(\sum_{n\le X}a_n\cos(v\log n)-\sin(v\log X)/v)]$ with $a_n\ge0$ supported on prime powers and $g$ a smooth gamma part that are the Thorin densities at level one of a function $\Xi(1)/\Xi(1+\sqrt s)$ with $\Xi$ in the Selberg class. The Thorin conditions constrain the growth and the integrability near $0$ but say nothing about the arithmetic of the $a_n$. The Selberg class needs the completed function, the gamma factors, the conductor, the poles and the sign of the coefficients of $-L'/L$ to be specified.

Source: [`ch/lo2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lo2.tex), label `lo:prob:selberg`.

<a id="open_rate_of_the_backward_cauchy_flow_and_the_lower_bound_off_the_half_plane"></a>

### Open problem: the rate of convergence of the backward flow and the exponential growth lower bound when a zero lies to the right

Problem 30.3, page 1067 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ have zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$, $\theta_0=\sup_\rho\sigma_\rho$, $\mathfrak U_\theta=\sum_\rho\mathrm{Cauchy}(\gamma_\rho,\theta-\sigma_\rho)$ its Thorin measure at level $\theta$, and $B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1=\mathfrak U_1*K_{\theta',\Omega}$ the band limited backward flow, $K_{\theta',\Omega}$ the inverse Fourier transform of $(1-|\omega|/\Omega)_+e^{(1-\theta')|\omega|}$. For $\theta'\in(\theta_0,1)$ give the rate of locally uniform convergence of $B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1$ to $\mathfrak U_{\theta'}$ in terms of $\Omega$ and $\theta'-\theta_0$, and, when $\sigma_{\max}=\sup\sigma_\rho>\theta'$ is attained by a zero, show that $\sup_{|v|\le V}|B_{\theta',\Omega}\mathfrak U_1(v)|$ grows like $e^{(\sigma_{\max}-\theta')\Omega}$ up to polynomial factors. For one zero with $d=\sigma-\theta'>0$ the Fejér inverse at distance $t$ from its ordinate is $(\pi\Omega)^{-1}\operatorname{Re}[(e^{z\Omega}-1-z\Omega)/z^2]$ with $z=d+it$, asymptotic to $e^{d\Omega}/(\pi d^2\Omega)$ at $t=0$; with infinitely many zeros the supremum need not be attained and the cancellations are part of the problem.

Source: [`ch/lo2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lo2.tex), label `lo:prob:rate`.

<a id="open_posterior_of_the_off_line_offset_delta_under_a_prior_allowing_off_line_zeros"></a>

### Open problem: a prior allowing off line zeros and the posterior of the offset delta at the real level one density

Problem 30.4, page 1067 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Replace the GUE prior for the zeros in the generative Bayesian computation inversion of the level one Thorin density $u_1(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(1+iv)$ of $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)$ by a prior that allows a fraction of the zeros off the critical line, for instance pairs at $\frac12\pm\delta+i\gamma$ with $\delta$ drawn from a prior on $[0,\frac12)$, and train the quantile network to report the posterior of $\delta$ for each detected zero. The posterior of $\delta$ at the real $u_1$ is then a window by window numerical diagnostic at the resolution the data allow, conditional on the prior, and not a certificate.

Source: [`ch/lo2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/lo2.tex), label `lo:prob:delta`.

## Chapter 31. Complexity and acceleration of the backward flow

<a id="log_concavity_of_the_poisson_posterior_for_the_backward_cauchy_flow"></a>

### Log concavity of the Poisson likelihood and of the gamma prior posterior in the discretised Cauchy deconvolution

Theorem 31.2.1, page 1076 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $A$ be a matrix with positive entries, $y$ a vector of nonnegative data, and $\ell(x)=\sum_i\bigl(y_i\log(Ax)_i-(Ax)_i\bigr)$ the Poisson log likelihood on the open orthant $x>0$. Then $\ell$ is concave. With independent gamma priors $x_j\sim\mathrm{Gamma}(\alpha_j,\beta_j)$, $\alpha_j\ge1$, the posterior density $\pi(x)\propto e^{\ell(x)}\prod_jx_j^{\alpha_j-1}e^{-\beta_jx_j}$ is log concave on the orthant. In the discretised deconvolution of the book, $A_{ij}=hP_{1-\theta'}(v_i-w_j)$ with $P_a$ the Cauchy density of scale $a$. The sampling clause of the chapter (sampling to total variation accuracy $\varepsilon$ in polynomial time for a log concave density, by a theorem of Applegate, Kannan and Polson) is cited and needs a bound on a ratio of radii that is not proved.

Source: [`ch/cx1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx1.tex), label `cx:thm:logconcave`.

<a id="precision_required_for_the_level_one_data_in_the_backward_cauchy_flow"></a>

### The level one data must be supplied to absolute precision e to the minus (1 minus theta') Omega for the linear inverse

Proposition 31.2.2, page 1077 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function, $u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)$ the level one density, $\theta'\in[\frac12,1)$ and let the Thorin measure at level $\theta'$ be recovered from $u_1$ by inverting the convolution with the Cauchy density of scale $1-\theta'$, whose Fourier transform is $e^{-(1-\theta')|\omega|}$. Let $\Omega$ be the largest frequency to be resolved. Then for the linear inverse the level one data must be supplied to absolute precision $e^{-(1-\theta')\Omega}$ on the scale of $u_1$, that is, to $(1-\theta')\Omega/\log 2$ binary digits, and this is sharp: an error of size $\delta$ at frequency $\omega$ in the Fourier transform of $u_1$ produces an error of size $\delta e^{(1-\theta')|\omega|}$ in the inverted measure.

Source: [`ch/cx1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx1.tex), label `cx:prop:precision`.

<a id="em_limits_converge_to_the_thorin_measure_if_and_only_if_no_zero_right_of_the_level"></a>

### What EM computes for the backward Cauchy flow: the Thorin measure at level theta' when zeta has no zeros to the right of theta'

Proposition 31.3.4, page 1080 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\frac12\le\theta'<1$, $a=1-\theta'$, $\xi$ the Riemann xi function and $u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)$. For a grid of spacing $h$ with data points $v_i=ih$, $|i|\le M$, in the window $[-V,V]$ and unknown points $w_j=jh$, $|j|\le N$, in the window $[-W,W]$, $W>V$, let $A_{ij}=hP_a(v_i-w_j)$ with $P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)$, $y_i=u_1(v_i)$, $R_h(x)=h\sum_{|i|\le M}\bigl(y_i\log\frac{y_i}{(Ax)_i}-y_i+(Ax)_i\bigr)$, $R_h^*=\min_{x\ge0}R_h(x)$, let $x_h$ be any minimiser (for instance the limit of EM from a positive start) and $\mu_h=\sum_jx_{h,j}h\,\delta_{w_j}$. Consider grids with $h\to0$ and $V\to\infty$. (a) If $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$ and $(\log W)^2/(W-V)\to0$, $(W-V)^2\log V/V^2\to0$ and $h^2V\log^2V\to0$, then $R_h^*\to0$ and $\mu_h$ converges vaguely to the Thorin measure $\mathfrak U_{\theta'}$, whose density is $\sum_\rho P_{\theta'-\operatorname{Re}\rho}(v-\operatorname{Im}\rho)$ over the zeros $\rho$ of $\xi$ with multiplicity, with $P_0$ read as the unit point mass. (b) If $\zeta$ has a zero of real part greater than $\theta'$, then $\liminf R_h^*>0$, whatever the choice of $W>V$.

Source: [`ch/cx1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx1.tex), label `cx:prop:what`.

<a id="von_neumann_ulam_estimator_for_the_backward_flow_has_infinite_variance"></a>

### The von Neumann and Ulam Monte Carlo estimator for the backward Cauchy flow has infinite variance for small grid spacing

Proposition 31.5.1, page 1087 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\theta'\in[\frac12,1)$, let $A$ be the square section of order $2N+1$ of the Toeplitz matrix $A_{ij}=hP_{1-\theta'}((i-j)h)$ with $P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)$, and let $t=h/(\pi(1-\theta'))$. Let $t_0=0.52219\ldots$ be the root in $(0,1)$ of $\coth(1/t)=2t$. If $t<t_0$, in particular if $h<\pi(1-\theta')/2$, the bi infinite operator $|I-A|$ has spectral radius $1-2t+\coth(1/t)>1$, and so do its sections for all $N\ge N_0(h,\theta')$. For such a section consider the von Neumann and Ulam estimator of $\sum_{k\ge0}(I-A)^ky$: at state $j$ it stops with probability $q_j\in(0,1)$ and otherwise moves to $k$ with probability $(1-q_j)p_{jk}$, $p_{jk}>0$ wherever $(I-A)_{jk}\ne0$, and it returns the product of the weights $(I-A)_{jk}/((1-q_j)p_{jk})$ along the path times $y_j/q_j$ at the stopping state $j$. Its second moment is infinite from every starting state. If $t_0<t\le1$ the spectral radius of $|I-A|$ is below one for the bi infinite operator and all its sections, and the conclusion fails for the choice $q_j=1-r_j$, $p_{jk}=|(I-A)_{jk}|/r_j$ with $r_j$ the row sums of $|I-A|$.

Source: [`ch/cx1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx1.tex), label `cx:prop:vnvar`.

<a id="thorin_measure_is_a_heat_flow_of_the_zeros_run_to_a_first_passage_time"></a>

### Subordinated heat trace: the Thorin measure at level theta is the heat flow of the zeros run to first passage times of Brownian motion

Proposition 31.6.1, page 1089 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $T_a$ be the first passage time to level $a>0$ of a Brownian motion, with density $\ell_a(t)=a(2\pi)^{-1/2}t^{-3/2}e^{-a^2/(2t)}$. Then $\frac{a/\pi}{a^2+(v-\gamma)^2}=\int_0^\infty\frac{e^{-(v-\gamma)^2/(2t)}}{\sqrt{2\pi t}}\ell_a(t)\,dt$, so $\gamma+B(T_a)$ has the Cauchy law of centre $\gamma$ and scale $a$ for an independent Brownian motion $B$, and $e^{-a|\omega|}=\int_0^\infty e^{-t\omega^2/2}\ell_a(t)\,dt$. Consequently, if $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta_0$ and $\theta>\theta_0$, the Thorin measure $\mathfrak U_\theta$, with density $\sum_\rho P_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}(v-\gamma_\rho)$ over the nontrivial zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ of $\zeta$ with multiplicity and $P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)$, equals $\sum_\rho\int_0^\infty(e^{t\Delta/2}\delta_{\gamma_\rho})\,\ell_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}(t)\,dt$, the sum over the nontrivial zeros of the heat flow of $\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$ run to the random time $T_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}$. Under the Riemann hypothesis it is the heat flow of $\sum_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$ to the single random time $T_{\theta-1/2}$.

Source: [`ch/cx1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx1.tex), label `cx:prop:subord`.

<a id="thorin_positivity_equivalent_to_zero_free_half_plane_and_positivity_of_xi_log_derivative"></a>

### The reciprocal xi transform at level theta is a GGC if and only if zeta has no zeros right of theta, if and only if the real part of xi'/xi is positive there

Theorem 31.9.1, page 1094 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function and, for $\frac12\le\theta<1$, $F_\theta(s)=\xi(\theta)/\xi(\theta+\sqrt s)$ on the plane cut along $(-\infty,0]$ with the principal square root. A generalised gamma convolution (GGC) has Laplace transform $\exp(-as-\int_0^\infty\log(1+s/u)U(du))$ with $a\ge0$ and a positive Thorin measure $U$. For $\frac12\le\theta<1$ the following are equivalent: (i) $F_\theta$ is the Laplace transform of a GGC, that is, the measure $U_\theta$ of the zeros is a positive Thorin measure; (ii) $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$; (iii) $\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(s)>0$ for $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$, that is, $u_\sigma(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\sigma+iv)>0$ for every $\sigma>\theta$ and every real $v$. For $\theta=\frac12$ the equivalence of (ii) and (iii) is the theorem of Lagarias.

Source: [`ch/cx2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx2.tex), label `cx:thm:positivity`.

<a id="mass_deficit_identity_counts_zeros_right_of_the_level"></a>

### Mass deficit identity: twice the number of zeros right of the level equals the drop of the integrated density plus a boundary term

Proposition 31.9.2, page 1095 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function, $u_\sigma(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\sigma+iv)$ and $M_\sigma(T)=\int_0^Tu_\sigma(v)\,dv$. Let $\frac12<\theta<1$ and $T>0$, and suppose no zero of $\xi$ lies on the segment $\operatorname{Re}s=\theta$, $0\le\operatorname{Im}s\le T$, nor on the segment $\operatorname{Im}s=T$, $\theta\le\operatorname{Re}s\le1$. Let $N(\theta,T)$ be the number of zeros with $\operatorname{Re}\rho>\theta$ and $0<\operatorname{Im}\rho<T$. Then $2N(\theta,T)=M_1(T)-M_\theta(T)+\pi^{-1}\Delta_{\mathrm{top}}(\theta,T)$, where $\Delta_{\mathrm{top}}(\theta,T)=-\int_\theta^1\operatorname{Im}(\xi'/\xi)(\sigma+iT)\,d\sigma$ is the change of $\arg\xi$ along the top side.

Source: [`ch/cx2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx2.tex), label `cx:prop:deficit`.

<a id="level_mass_function_jumps_at_real_parts_of_off_line_zeros"></a>

### The level mass function theta to M_theta(T) is continuous if and only if every zero below height T is on the critical line

Corollary 31.9.3, page 1096 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. With $\xi$, $u_\sigma$, $M_\sigma(T)=\int_0^Tu_\sigma(v)\,dv$, $N(\theta,T)$ and $\Delta_{\mathrm{top}}(\theta,T)=-\int_\theta^1\operatorname{Im}(\xi'/\xi)(\sigma+iT)\,d\sigma$ as in the mass deficit identity, let $T>0$ not be the ordinate of a zero. For $\theta\in(\frac12,1]$ not the real part of a zero below height $T$, $M_\theta(T)=M_1(T)+\pi^{-1}\Delta_{\mathrm{top}}(\theta,T)-2N(\theta,T)$. The first two terms form a real analytic function of $\theta$ with derivative $\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Im}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iT)$, and $2N(\theta,T)$ is a step function that drops by $2m$ as $\theta$ decreases through $\operatorname{Re}\rho$, for each zero $\rho$ of multiplicity $m$ with $\operatorname{Re}\rho>\frac12$ and $0<\operatorname{Im}\rho<T$. Hence $\theta\mapsto M_\theta(T)$ extends continuously to $(\frac12,1]$ if and only if every zero below height $T$ lies on the critical line, and its jumps occur exactly at the real parts of the off line zeros, of size twice the total multiplicity of the zeros with that real part and ordinate below $T$.

Source: [`ch/cx2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx2.tex), label `cx:cor:levelmass`.

<a id="certified_positivity_of_the_thorin_densities_at_levels_three_quarters_and_seven_eighths_up_to_1420"></a>

### Certified positivity of u_{3/4} and u_{7/8} on [0,1420] and 1000 zeros on the critical line below 1419.9, in ball arithmetic

Theorem 31.9.6, page 1102 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function, $u_\theta(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)$, $\Xi(v)=\xi(\frac12+iv)$, $T^*=1419.9$, $N(T)$ the number of zeros $\rho$ of $\zeta$ with $0<\operatorname{Im}\rho<T$ and $N(\theta,T)$ the number of those with $\operatorname{Re}\rho>\theta$. A computation in ball arithmetic (run at $96$ and at $160$ bits, with Taylor bounds for $u_\theta$ on cells and the argument change of $\xi$ along a path and a rectangle) establishes: (i) $u_{3/4}(v)>0$ and $u_{7/8}(v)>0$ for $0\le v\le1420$; (ii) $N(T^*)=1000$; (iii) $N(\frac34,T^*)=0$, with $\int_0^{T^*}u_{3/4}(v)\,dv=1000.01952570266\ldots$ to within $10^{-20}$; (iv) $\Xi$ has $1000$ certified sign changes in $(0,T^*)$. Consequently every zero of $\zeta$ with $0<\operatorname{Im}\rho<T^*$ lies on the critical line and is simple. The statement covers only this range of heights.

Source: [`ch/cx2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx2.tex), label `cx:thm:certified`.

<a id="global_minimum_of_the_thorin_density_at_level_seven_eighths_conditional"></a>

### Global minimum of the Thorin density u_{7/8} at the origin, given the announced zero free half plane

Theorem 31.10.2, page 1105 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on The zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ for the Riemann zeta function, announced in the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI 2026, Liu 2026), unrefereed and not checked for this book.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function and $u_\theta(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)$. If $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$, then, as measures, $\mathfrak U_{7/8}\ge u_{7/8}(0)\,dv$, where $\mathfrak U_{7/8}$ is the Thorin measure with density $u_{7/8}$ (with atoms at the ordinates of zeros on $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac78$ if there are any) and $u_{7/8}(0)=\pi^{-1}(\xi'/\xi)(\frac78)=0.0055146635278\ldots$, and $u_{7/8}(v)>u_{7/8}(0)$ wherever $v\ne0$ is not the ordinate of a zero on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac78$. The proof is a computation, with least certified bound on $[13.5,1420]$ equal to $0.0272$ at $v=17.49$ for $\theta=\frac78$.

Source: [`ch/cx2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx2.tex), label `cx:thm:globalmin`.

<a id="global_minimum_of_the_thorin_density_uniform_in_the_level_conditional"></a>

### Global minimum of u_theta at the origin for every level between 7/8 and 1, given the announced zero free half plane

Theorem 31.11.1, page 1110 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on The zero free half plane $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$ for the Riemann zeta function, announced in the quasi Riemann hypothesis preprints (OpenAI 2026, Liu 2026), unrefereed and not checked for this book. The monotonicity of $\theta\mapsto u_\theta(0)$ is unconditional.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function, $u_\theta(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)$ and $\mathfrak U_\theta$ the Thorin measure at level $\theta$, with density $u_\theta$ for $\theta>\frac78$. Suppose $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\frac78$. Then for every $\theta\in[\frac78,1]$ and every real $v\ne0$ that is not the height of a zero on $\operatorname{Re}s=\theta$, $u_\theta(v)>u_\theta(0)=\pi^{-1}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta)$, and the singular part of $\mathfrak U_\theta$ consists of positive atoms, which occur only if $\theta=\frac78$ and a zero lies on $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac78$; so $\mathfrak U_\theta-u_\theta(0)\,dv$ is a positive measure. Unconditionally, $\theta\mapsto u_\theta(0)$ is increasing on $[\frac12,\infty)$. The values of $u_\theta(0)$ run from $0.0055147$ at $\theta=\frac78$ to $0.0073516$ at $\theta=1$.

Source: [`ch/cx3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx3.tex), label `cx:thm:uniform`.

<a id="level_by_level_global_minimum_equivalent_to_zero_free_half_plane_with_explicit_excess"></a>

### Level by level theorem: a zero free half plane right of theta is equivalent to the global minimum of u_theta' at the origin for all theta' in [theta,1], with an explicit excess bound

Theorem 31.11.3, page 1112 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function, $u_\theta(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)$ and $\frac12<\theta\le1$. The following are equivalent: (i) $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$; (ii) for every $\theta'\in[\theta,1]$, $u_{\theta'}(v)\ge u_{\theta'}(0)$ for all real $v$ that are not heights of zeros on $\operatorname{Re}s=\theta'$. When they hold, $\mathfrak U_{\theta'}\ge u_{\theta'}(0)\,dv$ as measures for $\theta'\in[\theta,1]$, and for every $\theta'\in[\theta,1]$, with $c=2\theta'-1$ and the sum over all nontrivial zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ of $\zeta$ with multiplicity, $u_{\theta'}(v)-u_{\theta'}(0)\ge\frac c{2\pi}\bigl(\sum_\rho\frac1{c^2+(v-\gamma_\rho)^2}-\pi w^*\bigr)$ with $w^*=0.0294450$, where the bracket $\sum_\rho\frac1{c^2+(v-\gamma_\rho)^2}-\pi w^*$ is at least $\pi(0.06174-w^*)>0.1014$ for $13.5\le|v|\le1418.9$ and at least $7/65-\pi w^*>0.0151$ for $|v|\ge1418.9$. The numerical constants and brackets are computed, not proved by hand.

Source: [`ch/cx3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx3.tex), label `cx:thm:lbl`.

<a id="slope_of_the_excess_of_the_thorin_density_and_its_minimum_in_the_first_gap"></a>

### The slope of the excess of the Thorin density: certified infima near 0.1758 to 0.1793, and under RH the minimum 0.183899 in the first gap at v equal to 17.4979

Proposition 31.11.4, page 1114 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on The Riemann hypothesis, for the clause on the limiting bracket $X$ (its minimiser and value in the first gap). The lower bounds for $\inf B_c$ are a computation in ball arithmetic that needs only the hypothesis stated, no zeros of $\zeta$ in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$, which holds for $\theta=1$.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the Riemann xi function, $\theta\in(\frac12,1]$ be such that $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta$, $\theta'\in[\theta,1]$, $c=2\theta'-1$, $\gamma$ run over the ordinates of the zeros with multiplicity (both signs), $V_c(v)=\sum_{|\gamma|<1419.9}\bigl(\frac{c^2}4+(v-\gamma)^2\bigr)^{-1}$ and $B_c(v)=V_c(v)-V_c(0)-2\sum_{|\gamma|\ge1419.9}\gamma^{-2}$, the lower bound for $\frac{2\pi}c(u_{\theta'}(v)-u_{\theta'}(0))$ in which the zeros below height $1419.9$ are on the critical line by the certified computation of the book. A computation shows $\inf_{13.5\le|v|\le1418.9}B_c(v)\ge0.17575$ for $c=1$, $0.17838$ for $c=\frac12$, $0.17904$ for $c=\frac14$ and $0.17927$ as $c\downarrow0$, each infimum approached at $v=17.49$ to $17.50$, between the first two zeros. Under the Riemann hypothesis the limiting bracket $X(v)=\lim_{c\downarrow0}\frac{2\pi}c(u_{\theta'}(v)-u_{\theta'}(0))=\sum_\rho\bigl(\frac1{(v-\gamma_\rho)^2}-\frac1{\gamma_\rho^2}\bigr)$ has in the first gap between the zeros $14.1347$ and $21.0220$ a unique minimiser $v^*\in[17.4978,17.4980]$, and $0.1838985448\le X(v^*)\le0.1838987563$. The statement that $17.4979$ minimises $X$ over all of $13.5\le|v|\le1418.9$ is the author's computation, not rerun, and is not claimed here.

Source: [`ch/cx3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx3.tex), label `cx:prop:slope`.

<a id="a_posteriori_bound_for_window_masses_of_the_backward_flow_from_its_residual"></a>

### A posteriori bound: the error of a window mass of a positive measure against the Thorin measure is bounded by the residual against a weight

Proposition 31.11.5, page 1116 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\theta'\in[\frac12,1)$, $a=1-\theta'$, $P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)$, and suppose $\zeta$ has no zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>\theta'$, so that the Thorin measure $\mathfrak U_{\theta'}$ exists and $P_a*\mathfrak U_{\theta'}=u_1\,dv$ with $u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)$. Let $\mu$ be a finite positive measure and $r=P_a*\mu-u_1$ on $\mathbb{R}$. For a test function $\varphi$ with $\int e^{a|\omega|}|\widehat\varphi(\omega)|\,d\omega<\infty$ put $\psi=\mathcal F^{-1}[e^{a|\omega|}\widehat\varphi]$, and assume that $\psi\cdot(P_a*\mu+u_1)$ is integrable. Then $\bigl|\int\varphi\,d\mu-\int\varphi\,d\mathfrak U_{\theta'}\bigr|\le\int_{\mathbb{R}}|r(v)||\psi(v)|\,dv$.

Source: [`ch/cx3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx3.tex), label `cx:prop:apost`.

<a id="centroid_of_a_gaussian_window_locates_a_single_zero_under_rh"></a>

### From certified Gaussian window mass and centroid to the location of a zero, under the Riemann hypothesis

Corollary 31.11.9, page 1122 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on The Riemann hypothesis, so that $\mathfrak U_{1/2}=\sum_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$.

Statement. Assume the Riemann hypothesis, so that the Thorin measure at level $\frac12$ is $\mathfrak U_{1/2}=\sum_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$ over the ordinates with multiplicity. Let $\varphi(v)=e^{-(v-c)^2/(2\sigma^2)}$, let $\int\varphi\,d\mathfrak U_{1/2}\in[\widehat M-B_0,\widehat M+B_0]$ with $\widehat M>B_0$ and $\int(v-c)\varphi\,d\mathfrak U_{1/2}\in[\widehat m-B_1,\widehat m+B_1]$ be given bounds, let $\gamma_*$ be an ordinate with $|\gamma_*-c|\le R$, and let $\Theta\ge\sum_{\gamma\ne\gamma_*}(|\gamma-c|+R)\varphi(\gamma)$, the sum over the other ordinates with multiplicity. Then $|\gamma_*-c|\le\frac{|\widehat m|+B_1+\Theta}{\widehat M-B_0}$.

Source: [`ch/cx3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx3.tex), label `cx:cor:zeroloc`.

<a id="smoothed_prime_sum_evaluates_the_level_one_density_with_explicit_error"></a>

### Smoothed prime sum for u_1: exact identity and error bound under a local hypothesis on the zeros

Theorem 31.11.10, page 1124 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $v\ge2$, $X\ge2$, $s=1+iv$, $L=\zeta'/\zeta$, $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function and $u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)$, and let $u_1^X(v)=\frac1\pi\bigl[\frac1{1+v^2}-\frac{\log\pi}2+\frac12\operatorname{Re}\psi(\frac{1+iv}2)-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}n e^{-n/X}\cos(v\log n)\bigr]$ with $\psi$ the digamma function. Then $\pi(u_1(v)-u_1^X(v))=-\operatorname{Re}\sum_\rho\Gamma(\rho-s)X^{\rho-s}+\operatorname{Re}\Gamma(1-s)X^{1-s}+\operatorname{Re}[X^{-1}L(s-1)]+\operatorname{Re}R_X(s)$, with $R_X(s)=(2\pi i)^{-1}\int_{\operatorname{Re}w=-3/2}(-L(s+w))\Gamma(w)X^w\,dw$ and $|R_X(s)|\le2.5X^{-3/2}\log(v+2)$. If every zero with $|\gamma-v|\le Y$, $Y\ge1$, lies on the critical line, then $|u_1(v)-u_1^X(v)|\le\frac1\pi\bigl[c_\Gamma n(v)X^{-1/2}+2.6c_\Gamma'n(v+Y+1)e^{-\pi Y/2}+\sqrt{\pi/(v\sinh\pi v)}+\frac{27\log v}X+\frac{2.5\log(v+2)}{X^{3/2}}\bigr]$, where $n(t)=0.39\log t+7$ bounds the number of ordinates in any interval of length one below height $t$, $c_\Gamma\le8.34$ and $c_\Gamma'\le2.51$ are the explicit gamma function constants of the chapter.

Source: [`ch/cx3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx3.tex), label `cx:thm:fastu1`.

<a id="rate_at_the_boundary_two_phase_convergence_of_em_for_the_cauchy_deconvolution"></a>

### Open problem: the two phase rate of EM for the continuous Cauchy deconvolution at an atomic target

Problem 31.1, page 1129 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. For EM applied to the continuous Cauchy deconvolution $P_a*\mu=u_1$ at an atomic target, with $R_k$ the residual after $k$ steps and $R^*$ its limit, prove the two phase picture of the chapter: a sublinear phase with $k(R_k-R^*)$ near a constant of order $50$ (observed $54.7$, $51.9$, $49.5$, $48.1$ at $k=500$, $1000$, $2000$, $3000$), lasting of the order of $10^4$ steps on the data of the chapter, followed by faster convergence on the support of the atoms with a grid independent rate, and compute that rate from the curvature of the divergence at the atoms. For the accelerated scheme with restart, explain the observed three point exponents, which oscillate between $0.6$ and $2.8$ with a running value near $1.3$. The problem is open, and the numbers are observations.

Source: [`ch/cx3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx3.tex), label `cx:prob:twophase`.

<a id="closed_form_of_the_limiting_slope_of_the_thorin_density_excess"></a>

### Open problem: a closed form for the limiting slope 0.183899 of the excess of the Thorin density under RH

Problem 31.2, page 1129 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Under the Riemann hypothesis, with $\gamma$ running over the positive ordinates of the zeros, $\log|\xi(\frac12+iv)|=\log\xi(\frac12)+\sum_{\gamma>0}\log|1-v^2/\gamma^2|$. Put $\mathcal C(v)=\partial_v^2\log|\xi(\frac12+iv)|$, so that the limiting bracket of the excess of the Thorin density is $X(v)=\mathcal C(0)-\mathcal C(v)$, and let $v^*=17.4979$ be the zero of $\mathcal C'$ between the first two zeros, where $X(v^*)=0.183899$ to six digits. Does $\mathcal C(v^*)$, equivalently $X(v^*)$, have an expression in known constants? This is not known.

Source: [`ch/cx3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cx3.tex), label `cx:prob:closedform`.

<a id="algorithm_polynomial_in_log_height_and_log_accuracy_for_the_level_one_density"></a>

### Open problem: evaluate the level one Thorin density to accuracy epsilon in time polynomial in log v and log(1/epsilon)

Problem 31.3, page 1129 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Let $u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)$. The smoothed prime sum evaluates $u_1(v)$ to accuracy $\varepsilon$ in time polynomial in $\log v$ and in $1/\varepsilon$. Is there an algorithm polynomial in $\log v$ and $\log(1/\varepsilon)$? Such an algorithm for $\zeta$ and $\zeta'$ on $\operatorname{Re}s=1$ would give one; the converse is not known, and the question is open.

<a id="best_residual_of_a_first_order_method_for_a_single_blurred_atom"></a>

### Open problem: the best residual after k steps of a first order method for a single Cauchy blurred atom

Problem 31.4, page 1129 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. For a single atom at $\gamma$ blurred by the Cauchy density $P_a$ and observed exactly on a grid of spacing $h$, with $r_i$ the residuals at the grid points $v_i$ and $\psi_\gamma$ the weight of the a posteriori window bound for a window centred at $\gamma$, what is the best achievable value of $h\sum_i|\psi_\gamma(v_i)||r_i|$ after $k$ steps of any first order method on the cone of nonnegative measures, as a function of $k$, $h$ and $a$? The question is open.

## Chapter 32. The explicit formula as a deconvolution

<a id="explicit_formula_for_all_compactly_supported_test_functions_as_deconvolution"></a>

### The explicit formula for every smooth compactly supported test function, read as the deconvolution at level one half

Theorem 32.1.1, page 1135 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, let $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ run over its zeros (the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$, with multiplicity), let $\Lambda$ be the von Mangoldt function and $\gamma_E$ Euler's constant. For every $g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R})$, with the sum over $\rho$ absolutely convergent, $$\sum_\rho\int_{\mathbb{R}}g(\omega)\,e^{(\sigma_\rho-\frac12)|\omega|}\,e^{-i\omega\gamma_\rho}\,d\omega=\int_{\mathbb{R}}g(\omega)\,e^{|\omega|/2}\,d\omega-\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}\bigl(g(\log n)+g(-\log n)\bigr)+(1-\log\pi-\gamma_E)\,g(0)+\sum_{k\ge1}\Bigl[\frac{g(0)}{k+1}-\int_{\mathbb{R}}g(\omega)\,e^{-(2k+\frac12)|\omega|}\,d\omega\Bigr].$$ For even $g$ this is the explicit formula of Guinand and Weil; for odd $g$ both sides vanish. Under the Riemann hypothesis the left side is $\sum_\rho\widehat g(\gamma_\rho)$, $\widehat g(x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}g(\omega)e^{-i\omega x}\,d\omega$. Under the Riemann hypothesis the theorem is the Fourier form of the deconvolution $P_{1/2}*\mu=u_1$, $\mu=\sum_\rho\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$, of the level one density $u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)$, with $P_a$ the Cauchy density of width $a$: the multiplier $e^{|\omega|/2}$ that undoes the Cauchy kernel is the factor $\sqrt n$ that turns the weights $\Lambda(n)/n$ of the level one spectrum into the weights $\Lambda(n)/\sqrt n$ of the formula.

Source: [`ch/es1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/es1.tex), label `es:thm:explicit`.

<a id="unresolvable_perturbation_of_the_cauchy_deconvolution"></a>

### An unresolvable perturbation of the Cauchy deconvolution at width one half

Proposition 32.1.2, page 1137 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\Omega>0$, $L\ge1$, $\chi_L(v)=(2\pi L^2)^{-1/2}e^{-v^2/2L^2}$, $N=\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\cos(\Omega v)|\,\chi_L(v)\,dv$ and $\nu=N^{-1}\cos(\Omega v)\,\chi_L(v)\,dv$, and let $P_{1/2}(x)=(1/2\pi)/(1/4+x^2)$ be the Cauchy density of width $\frac12$. Then the total variation norm of $\nu$ is $1$, the Fourier transform $\widehat\nu$ is concentrated within $O(1/L)$ of $\pm\Omega$, and $\|P_{1/2}*\nu\|_\infty\le\sqrt{\pi/8}\,L^{-1}e^{1/8L^2}e^{-\Omega/2}\le0.72\,e^{-\Omega/2}$. Consequently, if $0.72\,e^{-\Omega/2}\le2\varepsilon$ and $\mu$ is a positive measure with $\mu\ge N^{-1}\chi_L\,dv$, then $\mu$ and $\mu+\nu$ are positive measures at total variation distance $1$ whose data $P_{1/2}*\mu$ and $P_{1/2}*(\mu+\nu)$ lie within $\varepsilon$ in the supremum norm of one function, so data of accuracy $\varepsilon$ do not distinguish them. The heuristic reading of this at scale $\delta=\pi/\Omega$ (primes to $e^{\pi/\delta}$) is not a theorem.

Source: [`ch/es1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/es1.tex), label `es:prop:resolution`.

<a id="tapered_transform_of_the_level_one_density_is_a_sum_of_damped_exponentials"></a>

### The Gaussian tapered Fourier transform of the level one density is a sum of damped exponentials, one per zero

Theorem 32.2.1, page 1138 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$, $a_\rho=1-\sigma_\rho\in(0,1)$, $P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)$, and $u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)=\sum_\rho P_{a_\rho}(v-\gamma_\rho)$. Let $w(v)=e^{-(v-c)^2/2\ell^2}$ with $\ell>0$ and $F(\omega)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}u_1(v)\,w(v)\,e^{i\omega(v-c)}\,dv$. Then for $\omega\ell^2>1$, $$F(\omega)=\sum_\rho w(\gamma_\rho+ia_\rho)\,e^{-a_\rho\omega}e^{i\omega(\gamma_\rho-c)}+R(\omega),$$ where $w(x+iy)=w(x)e^{y^2/2\ell^2}e^{-iy(x-c)/\ell^2}$ is the entire extension of the taper, the series converges absolutely, and with $Y=\omega\ell^2$ $$|R(\omega)|\le\frac1\pi\,e^{-\ell^2\omega^2/2}\sum_\rho a_\rho\int_{\mathbb{R}}\frac{e^{-(x-c)^2/2\ell^2}\,dx}{(x-\gamma_\rho)^2+(Y-a_\rho)^2},\qquad\int_{\mathbb{R}}\frac{e^{-(x-c)^2/2\ell^2}\,dx}{(x-\gamma)^2+B^2}\le\min\Bigl(\frac\pi B,\frac{\sqrt{2\pi}\,\ell}{B^2}\Bigr).$$ In particular for $\omega_j=\omega_0+j\Delta$ with $\omega_0\ell^2>1$, $F(\omega_j)=\sum_\rho A_\rho z_\rho^{\,j}+R(\omega_j)$ with $|R(\omega_j)|\le C_0e^{-\ell^2\omega_j^2/2}$, $C_0$ the above bound on $|R(\omega_0)|$ divided by $e^{-\ell^2\omega_0^2/2}$, $A_\rho=w(\gamma_\rho+ia_\rho)e^{-a_\rho\omega_0}e^{i\omega_0(\gamma_\rho-c)}$ and $z_\rho=e^{\Delta(-a_\rho+i(\gamma_\rho-c))}$: the pole $z_\rho$ has modulus giving $a_\rho$ and argument giving $\gamma_\rho-c$ modulo $2\pi/\Delta$. Nothing is assumed about the real parts $\sigma_\rho$.

Source: [`ch/es1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/es1.tex), label `es:thm:taper`.

<a id="posterior_concentration_for_zeros_in_a_window_under_the_tapered_model"></a>

### Posterior concentration for the atoms of the tapered transform model on a window

Theorem 32.4.1, page 1142 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Fix a window centre $c$, a taper width $\ell$, a step $\Delta$, samples $\omega_j=\omega_0+j\Delta$, $0\le j<J$, with $\omega_0\ell^2>1$, and a radius $R$ with $2R\Delta<2\pi$. The data are $F=\Phi(\vartheta^0)+b$ with $\Phi(\vartheta)_j=\sum_{m=1}^MA_mz_m^{\,j}$, $z_m=e^{\Delta(-a_m+i(\gamma_m-c))}$, where $\vartheta^0$ collects the zeros $(\gamma_m,a_m,A_m)$ with $|\gamma_m-c|\le R$ (ordinate, width $a_m=1-\sigma_m$, amplitude) and $b$ is the deterministic bias from the zeros beyond $R$ and the remainder of the tapered transform; the observation is $Y=F+\tau\xi$ with $\xi\in\mathbb{C}^J$ having independent standard normal real and imaginary parts. Fix $s>0$, $0<a_-<a_+<1$, $0<\alpha_-<A_+$ and an integer $M_{\max}$ with $J\ge2M_{\max}$. For $0\le M\le M_{\max}$ let $K_M$ be the compact set of $\vartheta=(\gamma_m,a_m,A_m)_{m\le M}$ with $c-R\le\gamma_1<\dots<\gamma_M\le c+R$, $\gamma_{m+1}-\gamma_m\ge s$, $a_m\in[a_-,a_+]$, $\alpha_-\le|A_m|\le A_+$. Let the prior be $\Pi=\sum_Mp_M\Pi_M$ with $\Pi_M$ having a density on $K_M$ between $\pi_->0$ and $\pi_+$. Let $\vartheta^0$ be an interior point of $K_{M^0}$ with $p_{M^0}>0$, $\|b\|_2\le B\tau$, and $d(\vartheta,\vartheta^0)=\max_m(|\gamma_m-\gamma^0_m|+|a_m-a^0_m|+|A_m-A^0_m|)$ if $M=M^0$, $d=\infty$ otherwise. Then there are $\tau_0,r_0,K,\kappa_0>0$, depending on $\vartheta^0$, the sets $K_M$, the prior, $J$, $\Delta$ and $B$, such that for $\tau\le\tau_0$ and $K\tau\le\varepsilon\le r_0$, with probability at least $1-e^{-\kappa_0\varepsilon^2/\tau^2}$, $\Pi(d(\vartheta,\vartheta^0)\le\varepsilon\mid Y)\ge1-e^{-\kappa_0\varepsilon^2/\tau^2}$. In particular, for fixed $\varepsilon_1>0$ and $\|b\|_2\le B\tau$, as $\tau\to0$ the posterior probability that every component has $|\sigma_m-\frac12|\le\varepsilon_1$ tends to $1$ in probability if every zero of $\vartheta^0$ has $|\sigma^0_m-\frac12|<\varepsilon_1$, and to $0$ if one has $|\sigma^0_m-\frac12|>\varepsilon_1$. The hypotheses (bias below the noise, no aliasing) are incompatible at the settings of the chapter's computations, and the theorem is indifferent between the Riemann hypothesis and its negation.

Source: [`ch/es1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/es1.tex), label `es:thm:concentration`.

<a id="rate_tau_to_the_one_half_for_the_real_part_of_a_pair_of_zeros"></a>

### The real part of an off line pair of zeros is resolved only at the rate tau to the one half

Theorem 32.5.2, page 1146 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Work in the window model of the tapered transform at a level $\theta>\frac12$ with $a_0=\theta-\frac12$, samples $\omega_j=\omega_0+j\Delta$, $0\le j<J$, and $f(a)_j=\exp(-q^2/2\ell^2+i\omega_jq)$, $q=(\gamma-c)+ia$. One ordinate $\gamma$ carries either a zero on the line or a pair at real parts $\frac12\pm\delta$, $0\le\delta\le\delta_+<a_0$, entering the samples as $A\,g(\eta;\gamma)$ with $g(\eta;\gamma)=f(a_0-\sqrt\eta)+f(a_0+\sqrt\eta)$, $\eta=\delta^2$, and one complex amplitude $A$ common to the two members (the functional equation puts zeros off the line in such pairs); the other $M$ zeros enter as $\sum_{m\le M}A_mz_m^{\,j}$ with $z_m=e^{\Delta(-a_m+i(\gamma_m-c))}$. Write $\vartheta'=(\gamma,A,(\gamma_m,a_m,A_m)_{m\le M})$, of real dimension $D'=3+4M$, and $\Phi(\eta,\vartheta')\in\mathbb{C}^J=\mathbb{R}^{2J}$ for the noiseless samples. Assume (H1) $Y=\Phi(\eta^0,\vartheta'^0)+b+\tau\xi$ with $\xi$ having independent standard normal real and imaginary parts and $\|b\|_2\le B\tau$; (H2) the parameter set is $[0,\eta_+]\times K'$ with $\eta_+=\delta_+^2$, $K'$ compact, $\eta^0\in[0,\eta_+)$, $\vartheta'^0$ interior to $K'$ and $\Phi$ injective on it; (H3) the Jacobian $T'$ of $\vartheta'\mapsto\Phi(\eta^0,\vartheta')$ at $\vartheta'^0$ has rank $D'$ and, with $t=\partial_\eta\Phi(\eta^0,\vartheta'^0)$ and $t_\perp=(I-P')t$ for the orthogonal projection $P'$ onto the range of $T'$, $\|t_\perp\|>0$; (H4) the prior puts mass $1-p<1$ at $\eta=0$ and density $p\,\pi(\sqrt\eta)/2\sqrt\eta$ on $(0,\eta_+]$ with $\pi$ continuous and positive on $[0,\delta_+]$, and independently $\vartheta'$ has a density bounded on $K'$, continuous and positive at $\vartheta'^0$. Let $r_\tau=\tau/\|t_\perp\|$ and $\tau\to0$ with $B$ and $\vartheta'^0$ fixed, and with $\eta^0$ fixed in (i) and (ii). Then (i) for every $M_\tau\to\infty$, $\Pi(|\eta-\eta^0|>M_\tau r_\tau\mid Y)\to0$ in probability, so $\delta$ is located within $(M_\tau r_\tau)^{1/2}$ if $\delta^0=0$; (ii) for $\eta^0=0$ and $\delta_1=c\,r_\tau^{1/2}$ the two error probabilities of any test of $\delta=0$ against $\delta=\delta_1$, whatever the method, sum to at least $1-c^2/2-O(\tau)$; (iii) for $\eta^0=v\,r_\tau$, $v\ge0$ fixed, with $\|b\|_2=o(\tau)$, the matched filter statistic $Z=\langle t_\perp,r\rangle/(\tau\|t_\perp\|)$, with $t_\perp$ taken at $\eta=0$ and $r$ the residual of the least squares fit of $\Phi(0,\cdot)$ over $K'$, satisfies $Z=v+\zeta_\perp+o_P(1)$ with $\zeta_\perp$ standard Gaussian, the one sided test $Z>z_\alpha$ has asymptotic level $\alpha$ and power $1-N(z_\alpha-v)$, $N$ the standard normal distribution function and $z_\alpha=N^{-1}(1-\alpha)$, which is $\frac12$ at $\delta^*=(z_\alpha r_\tau)^{1/2}$, and twice the log generalised likelihood ratio of $\eta\ge0$ against $\eta=0$ is $\max(Z,0)^2+o_P(1)$. The theorem needs the bias below the noise and no aliasing, so it does not cover the chapter's runs on the zeros of $\zeta$.

Source: [`ch/es2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/es2.tex), label `es:thm:singular`.

<a id="bayes_factors_for_the_line_against_a_pair_of_zeros"></a>

### Bayes factors for a zero on the line against a pair at one half plus and minus delta

Theorem 32.5.4, page 1150 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. In the setting of the rate theorem for the real part of a pair (hypotheses H1 to H4, noise level $\tau$, scale $s=\|t_\perp\|/\tau$), put the spike and slab prior on the pair: $\delta=0$ with probability $1-p$, and otherwise $\delta$ with a density $\pi$ continuous and positive on $[0,\delta_+]$. Let $G(Z)=\int_0^\infty u^{-1/2}e^{Zu-u^2/2}\,du$ and $Z$ the matched filter statistic of that theorem. (a) If $\eta^0=0$, or $\eta^0=v\,r_\tau$ with $v$ fixed, $\|b\|_2=o(\tau)$, and $\vartheta'$ has the same prior under the line and the pair, the Bayes factor for the line against the pair is $\mathrm{BF}_{01}=\dfrac{2\,s^{1/2}}{\pi(0)\,G(Z)}(1+o_P(1))$; under the null $Z$ is asymptotically standard Gaussian and $\mathrm{BF}_{01}\asymp\tau^{-1/2}$ in probability. (b) Under a pair with fixed $\delta\in(0,\delta_+)$, if the prior density of $\vartheta'$ is bounded below on $K'$ and every point of $K'$ has prior mass at least $c\tau^{D'}$ within distance $\tau$, then $\log\mathrm{BF}_{01}=-D(\delta)^2(1+o_P(1))/2\tau^2$ with $D(\delta)=\delta^2\|t_\perp\|+O(\delta^4)$. (c) Against the alternative of a single zero of width $a_0+\varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon$ having a density positive and continuous at $0$ and $\|(I-P')\partial_\varepsilon\Phi\|>0$, the same data give $\mathrm{BF}_{01}\asymp\tau^{-1}$ in probability under the null. All of this is in the free amplitude model with a common amplitude for the pair.

Source: [`ch/es2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/es2.tex), label `es:thm:bf`.

<a id="levels_below_the_zeros_signed_lorentzians_and_poles"></a>

### The density at a level between one half and one is a signed sum of Lorentzians, and the Riemann hypothesis fixes every damping rate

Proposition 32.8.1, page 1157 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\frac12<\theta\le1$ with $\theta\ne\sigma_\rho$ for every zero $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ of the completed zeta function $\xi$, let $P_b(x)=(b/\pi)/(b^2+x^2)$ and $u_\theta(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(\theta+iv)$. Then $u_\theta(v)=\sum_\rho\operatorname{sgn}(\theta-\sigma_\rho)P_{|\theta-\sigma_\rho|}(v-\gamma_\rho)$ and $\widehat{u_\theta}(\omega)=\sum_\rho\operatorname{sgn}(\theta-\sigma_\rho)e^{-|\theta-\sigma_\rho||\omega|}e^{-i\omega\gamma_\rho}$. For $\omega\ell^2>1$ the tapered transform $F_\theta(\omega)=\int u_\theta(v)w(v)e^{i\omega(v-c)}dv$ with the Gaussian taper $w(v)=e^{-(v-c)^2/2\ell^2}$ equals $\sum_\rho\operatorname{sgn}(\theta-\sigma_\rho)\,w(\gamma_\rho+i|\theta-\sigma_\rho|)\,e^{-|\theta-\sigma_\rho|\omega}e^{i\omega(\gamma_\rho-c)}+R_\theta(\omega)$, with $R_\theta$ bounded as in the tapered transform theorem with $a_\rho$ replaced by $|\theta-\sigma_\rho|$. For samples $\omega_j=\omega_0+j\Delta$, a zero with $\sigma_\rho>\theta$ gives the pole $e^{\Delta(-(\sigma_\rho-\theta)+i(\gamma_\rho-c))}$, of modulus $e^{-\Delta(\sigma_\rho-\theta)}$, with an amplitude of sign opposite to the taper profile, while its partner $1-\sigma_\rho<\theta$ gives a pole at the same ordinate with the profile's sign. The Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if every damping rate $|\theta-\sigma_\rho|$ equals $\theta-\frac12$.

Source: [`ch/es2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/es2.tex), label `es:prop:level`.

<a id="pencil_at_height_3e12_inside_the_verified_range_demonstration"></a>

### Matrix pencil on a window at height 3e12, a demonstration inside the verified range

Result 32.8.6, page 1159 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. A demonstration, computed and not a finding about the zeros: the window centred at $c=3\times10^{12}+100$ lies inside the range $0<\gamma\le3\,000\,175\,332\,800$ in which Platt and Trudgian verified the Riemann hypothesis. From $1001$ values of $u_{0.6}(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(0.6+iv)$ at spacing $0.02$ (level $0.6$, taper $\ell=2$, ball arithmetic at $160$ bits), the matrix pencil returned $52$ components with amplitudes on the taper profile within $6$ of the centre, the smooth count being $51.36$, each with real part $0.5000000\pm1.4\times10^{-8}$ read from the modulus of its pole; this is a floating point estimate, not a certificate, and the selection of components presumes the real part $\frac12$. The authors' certificate (not rerun) is a sign change of Hardy's function $Z$ in ball arithmetic on $[\gamma-10^{-7},\gamma+10^{-7}]$ for all $52$ of the $52$ ordinates, which places a zero on the line within $10^{-7}$ of each; an independent scan in ball arithmetic at $160$ bits finds exactly $52$ certified sign changes in $[c-6,c+6]$, but the comparison with the pencil's ordinates one by one was not made. Not certified: that these are all the zeros of the window (a sign scan cannot see two zeros inside one step, and no winding number or Turing method was completed) and the real parts.

Source: [`ch/es2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/es2.tex), label `es:res:window3e12`.

<a id="pencil_components_above_the_verified_range_at_height_1e13"></a>

### Matrix pencil on a window at height 1e13 plus 100, above the verified range, computed

Result 32.8.7, page 1161 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. A computation with scripts written for the book: the window centred at $c=10^{13}+100$, above the verified range of Platt and Trudgian ($\gamma\le3\,000\,175\,332\,800$), level $0.6$, taper $\ell=2$, $1001$ values $u_{0.6}(v_k)$, $v_k=c-10+0.02k$, each a ball at $160$ bits, $\omega\in[5,85]$ at spacing $0.2$, a Hankel matrix of order $200$ in double precision and model order $132$. The pencil returns $53$ components with amplitude on the taper profile within $6$ of the centre, at ordinates from $c-5.7$ to $c+5.8$ (the smooth count is $53.66$), the ratio of amplitude to profile being $1$ to within $1.6\times10^{-7}$; the selection compares the amplitude with the profile at the pole's own width, so no real part is assumed. The largest $|\sigma_\rho-\frac12|$ over the $53$ poles is $4.7\times10^{-9}$ (median $7.1\times10^{-11}$), an estimate from a double precision pencil and not a certificate, and it is not a proof of the Riemann hypothesis in the window.

Source: [`ch/es2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/es2.tex), label `es:res:pencil1e13`.

<a id="certified_zeros_on_the_critical_line_at_height_1e13_plus_100"></a>

### Fifty three certified zeros on the critical line in a window at height 1e13 plus 100, above the verified range

Result 32.8.7, page 1161 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. In ball arithmetic at $160$ bits, with each step of $0.02$ having opposite signs of Hardy's function $Z(t)=e^{i\vartheta(t)}\zeta(\frac12+it)$ at its ends, the interval $[c-6,c+6]$ with $c=10^{13}+100$, above the height $3\,000\,175\,332\,800$ verified by Platt and Trudgian, contains $53$ certified sign changes, with bisection brackets of width $10^{-10}$ certified at both ends again at $192$ bits; hence $\zeta$ has at least $53$ zeros on the critical line in that interval, each located to $10^{-10}$. The pencil of the same chapter returns the same $53$ ordinates (the largest difference is $3.9\times10^{-9}$). Not certified: the number of zeros in the window (a sign scan cannot see two zeros inside one step of $0.02$, the smallest gap found is $0.0326$, and no Turing method or winding number was run) and the real parts; nothing is certified off the line. The certified statement is only that these $53$ zeros lie on the line, and it is not a proof of the Riemann hypothesis in the window.

Source: [`ch/es2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/es2.tex), label `es:res:zeros1e13`.

<a id="open_rigorous_matrix_pencil_perturbation_bound"></a>

### Open problem, a rigorous matrix pencil with a perturbation bound under the model error

Problem 32.1, page 1162 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. The matrix pencil applied to the tapered transform $F(\omega_j)=\sum_\rho A_\rho z_\rho^{\,j}+R(\omega_j)$ of the level one density $u_1$ of the completed zeta function makes the Hankel matrix of exact finite rank only in the limit, because of the far zeros and the remainder $R$. The problem: state and prove a perturbation bound for the pencil under this model error, which together with verified linear algebra on ball data (in the sense of Rump) would give rigorous enclosures of the zeros from level one data, and compare the width of the resulting enclosures with the winding number route of the argument principle. Status: open.

Source: [`ch/es2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/es2.tex), label `es:prob:rigorous_pencil`.

<a id="open_spurious_components_at_window_edges"></a>

### Open problem, characterise and remove the spurious pencil components at the edges of windows

Problem 32.2, page 1162 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. In the many window use of the matrix pencil on the tapered transform of $u_1$, a few components at the edges of overlapping windows pass the amplitude filter without being zeros. The problem: characterise them (the expectation is that they are the pencil's representation of the taper's tail of the next zeros outside the window, with poles close to the genuine ones and amplitudes off the profile), and prove under explicit hypotheses on the separation and the amplitudes that a rule based on the agreement of two windows, or on the phase $e^{i(\omega_0-a/\ell^2)(\gamma-c)}$ of the amplitude predicted by the tapered transform theorem, removes all of them. Status: open.

Source: [`ch/es2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/es2.tex), label `es:prob:spurious`.

<a id="open_pencil_at_greater_height_with_rigorous_argument_principle"></a>

### Open problem, windows at greater height with a rigorous argument principle and the cost of a full certificate

Problem 32.3, page 1163 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. The matrix pencil runs on one window of fifty two or fifty three zeros at heights $3\times10^{12}$ and $10^{13}$ at the cost of the Riemann and Siegel sum, $t^{1/2}$ terms per value, which Hiary's method would bring to $t^{1/3+o(1)}$. The problem: make the argument principle rigorous at large height, with an explicit bound for $|\zeta'|$ on a small disc from the explicit convexity bounds, so that the count of zeros in the window is certified and not only their existence on the line; estimate the height at which a window of the pencil with its full certificate is feasible on a laptop in a day, and run it; and determine whether the many window scheme at a fixed height, for example $10^3$ zeros above $3\,000\,175\,332\,800$, is competitive with Turing's method for that range when the real parts are wanted as output and not only tested. Status: open.

Source: [`ch/es2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/es2.tex), label `es:prob:higher_wider`.

<a id="open_adaptive_prior_for_the_zeros_in_a_window"></a>

### Open problem, the adaptive prior in full: sine kernel process with marked ordinates and a spike and slab on the pairs

Problem 32.4, page 1163 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. The problem: place the sine kernel determinantal process on marked distinct ordinates, a pair of zeros at real parts $\frac12\pm\delta$ counting as one point marked by its displacement, and implement the posterior on the number, the positions and the marks of the zeros in a window, with the spike and slab prior on the marks, by reversible jump or by a determinantal birth and death sampler started at the pencil; measure on the many window run whether it removes the spurious components; state the count with its multiplicity (a double zero counts twice), and report the posterior probability of each count, conditional on the model, separately from the argument principle certificate, which it does not replace. Status: open.

Source: [`ch/es2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/es2.tex), label `es:prob:adaptive_prior`.

<a id="open_design_maximising_the_information_for_the_real_part"></a>

### Open problem, the constant in the tau to the one half rate and the design that maximises the information

Problem 32.5, page 1163 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. The detectable displacement of an off line pair of zeros is $\delta^*=(z_\alpha\tau/\|t_\perp\|)^{1/2}$, with $\tau$ the standard deviation per real coordinate and $t_\perp$ the part of the tangent of the pair orthogonal to the tangent space of the other zeros, depending on the taper, the bandwidth and the level. The problem: find the design that maximises the information $\|t_\perp\|/\tau$, and not $\|t_\perp\|$ alone, for a given cost, and determine how it scales with the height, through the gaps to the neighbouring zeros, which enter $t_\perp$ through the projection, and not through the mean density alone. Status: open.

Source: [`ch/es2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/es2.tex), label `es:prob:constant_rate`.

## Chapter 33. Cauchy deconvolution

<a id="cauchy_deconvolution_is_unique_for_admissible_measures"></a>

### Uniqueness of Cauchy deconvolution for admissible measures

Proposition 33.1.1, page 1167 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)$ be the Cauchy density of width $a>0$. Call a signed measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ admissible when $\int(1+x^2)^{-1}d|\mu|(x)<\infty$. If $\mu_1,\mu_2$ are admissible and $P_a*\mu_1=P_a*\mu_2$ then $\mu_1=\mu_2$. The proof applies the semigroup property $P_a*P_b=P_{a+b}$ to the difference, shows its Poisson extension vanishes for heights above $a$ and hence on the whole upper half plane, and uses that an admissible measure is the vague boundary value of its Poisson integral.

Source: [`ch/cd1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cd1.tex), label `cd:prop:unique`.

<a id="range_of_cauchy_convolution_on_l2_and_the_failure_of_the_naive_description"></a>

### The range of convolution with a Cauchy density on L2, unboundedness of the inverse, and a positive bounded datum outside the range

Proposition 33.1.2, page 1168 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)$, $a>0$, with Fourier transform $\widehat f(\omega)=\int f(x)e^{-i\omega x}dx$, so $\widehat{P_a}=e^{-a|\omega|}$, and let $H^s$ be the Sobolev space of order $s$. (a) For $f\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, $\int e^{2a|\omega|}|\widehat{P_a*f}|^2d\omega=\int|\widehat f|^2d\omega$, and every $u$ with $\int e^{2a|\omega|}|\widehat u|^2d\omega<\infty$ equals $P_a*f$ for some $f\in L^2$. (b) For all real $s,t$, $\sup_f\|f\|_{H^t}/\|P_a*f\|_{H^s}=\infty$. (c) The function $u(x)=2+\cos(x^2)$ is positive and bounded, its Poisson extension continues to an entire harmonic function, and yet $u\ne P_a*\mu$ for every $a>0$ and every measure $\mu$ with $\int(1+t^2)^{-1}d|\mu|(t)<\infty$.

Source: [`ch/cd1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cd1.tex), label `cd:prop:range`.

<a id="positive_data_with_a_signed_source_and_the_closed_form_of_the_critical_width"></a>

### A positive datum with a signed source: the two atom example and its critical width

Example 33.2.1, page 1169 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $P_a(x)=(a/\pi)/(a^2+x^2)$, $d>0$, $0<q<1$, $a>0$ and $\mu=\delta_0-q\delta_d$. Then $P_a*\mu=P_a-qP_a(\cdot-d)\ge0$ on $\mathbb{R}$ if and only if $q\le(r-d)/(r+d)$ with $r=\sqrt{d^2+4a^2}$. By uniqueness of the deconvolution, the signed measure $\mu$ is then the only source of this datum at width $a$. The partial deconvolution $P_{a-c}*\mu$, $0\le c<a$, is nonnegative if and only if $q\le(r_c-d)/(r_c+d)$ with $r_c=\sqrt{d^2+4(a-c)^2}$, that is, if and only if $c\le c^*=a-\frac12\sqrt{m^2-d^2}$ with $m=\frac{1+q}{1-q}d$. For $q=9-4\sqrt5$, $a=\frac12$ and $d=1$ this gives $c^*=\frac14$ exactly.

Source: [`ch/cd1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cd1.tex), label `cd:ex:signed`.

<a id="critical_width_of_a_positive_datum_is_attained"></a>

### The critical width of a positive datum for Cauchy deconvolution is attained when finite

Proposition 33.2.2, page 1169 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $P_c(x)=(c/\pi)/(c^2+x^2)$ with $P_0*\nu=\nu$, and let $u\ge0$ satisfy $\int u(x)(1+x^2)^{-1}dx<\infty$. Put $c^*(u)=\sup\{c\ge0:\ u=P_c*\nu\text{ for some measure }\nu\ge0\}\in[0,\infty]$, so that $c=0$ always qualifies. Then a positive source at width $c$ exists for every finite $c\le c^*(u)$ and for no $c>c^*(u)$; in particular the supremum is attained when it is finite. The proof uses that the admissible widths form an interval and the Herglotz and Riesz characterisation of nonnegative harmonic functions on a half plane.

Source: [`ch/cd1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cd1.tex), label `cd:prop:critical`.

<a id="existence_of_a_positive_source_iff_nonnegative_harmonic_extension_below_the_line"></a>

### A positive source exists at width c if and only if the harmonic extension continues as a nonnegative harmonic function to the half plane y > -c

Theorem 33.2.3, page 1170 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $u\ge0$ be continuous with $\int u(x)(1+x^2)^{-1}dx<\infty$ and let $h(x,y)=(P_y*u)(x)$, $y>0$, be its Poisson (harmonic) extension to the upper half plane, with $P_y$ the Cauchy density of width $y$. For $c>0$ the following are equivalent: (i) $u=P_c*\nu$ for a measure $\nu\ge0$; (ii) $h$ extends to a nonnegative harmonic function on the half plane $y>-c$. The proof of (ii) implies (i) uses the Herglotz and Riesz representation of nonnegative harmonic functions on a half plane and shows that its linear coefficient vanishes.

Source: [`ch/cd1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cd1.tex), label `cd:thm:herglotz`.

<a id="three_lines_holder_stability_of_cauchy_deconvolution_between_levels"></a>

### Hölder stability of Cauchy deconvolution between levels by the three lines theorem, with sharp exponent

Theorem 33.3.1, page 1171 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $P_y$ be the Cauchy density of width $y>0$, with $P_0*\mu=\mu$, let $b_0<b<a$ and let $\mu$ be a signed measure with $P_{b_0}*\mu\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, where for $b_0<0$ this means $\mu=P_{|b_0|}*\lambda$ with $\lambda\in L^2$ and $P_{b_0}*\mu$ stands for $\lambda$; for $y>b_0$, $P_y*\mu$ means $P_{y-b_0}*(P_{b_0}*\mu)$. Then $\|P_b*\mu\|_2\le\|P_a*\mu\|_2^{\kappa}\,\|P_{b_0}*\mu\|_2^{1-\kappa}$ with $\kappa=(b-b_0)/(a-b_0)$. In particular, if two sources have data at width $a$ within $\varepsilon$ in $L^2$ and both are bounded by $M$ at width $b_0$, they agree at width $b$ to within $\varepsilon^\kappa(2M)^{1-\kappa}$. The exponent $\kappa$ is attained in rate. The proof is Hölder's inequality on the Fourier side, equivalently convexity of $y\mapsto\log\|P_y*\mu\|_2$.

Source: [`ch/cd1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cd1.tex), label `cd:thm:holder`.

<a id="sharp_holder_exponent_for_finite_signed_sources"></a>

### Sharp Hölder exponent (b+w)/(a+w) for Cauchy deconvolution of finite signed sources

Proposition 33.3.2, page 1172 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $P_y$ be the Cauchy density of width $y>0$ with $P_0*\nu=\nu$. Let $\nu$ be a finite signed measure of total variation at most $B$, let $w\ge0$, $h=P_w*\nu$ (with $P_b*h$ meaning $P_{b+w}*\nu$ when $b<0$) and let $-w<b<a$. Then $\|P_b*h\|_2\le\sqrt2\,D^{1-\kappa}\|P_a*h\|_2^{\kappa}$ with $\kappa=(b+w)/(a+w)$ and $D=B/\sqrt{2\pi(b+w)}$, and no larger exponent holds uniformly over this class. The upper bound is a split of the frequencies at a cutoff chosen as a function of the data error, and the sharpness is shown by the sources $B\phi(x)\cos(\Omega x)dx$ with $\Omega\to\infty$ for a fixed nonnegative kernel $\phi$ with transform $(1-|\omega|)_+$.

Source: [`ch/cd1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cd1.tex), label `cd:prop:finite`.

<a id="two_level_bound_for_positive_sources_of_cauchy_deconvolution"></a>

### Two level Hölder bound for positive sources of Cauchy deconvolution with data in L2 on the line

Corollary 33.3.3, page 1172 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $P_y$ be the Cauchy density of width $y>0$. If $\mu_1,\mu_2\ge0$ are measures, $u_j=P_a*\mu_j\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and $\|u_1-u_2\|_2\le\varepsilon$, then for $0<d<b<a$, $\|P_b*(\mu_1-\mu_2)\|_2\le\varepsilon^\kappa\bigl((a/d)(\|u_1\|_2+\|u_2\|_2)\bigr)^{1-\kappa}$ with $\kappa=(b-d)/(a-d)$. The proof uses the pointwise bound $P_d\le(a/d)P_a$ and the three lines bound. The statement is for data in $L^2$ on the whole line; the case of data on a window is a problem of the chapter.

Source: [`ch/cd1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cd1.tex), label `cd:cor:positive`.

<a id="logarithmic_stability_of_cauchy_deconvolution_at_the_boundary_is_sharp"></a>

### Logarithmic stability of Cauchy deconvolution for sources in a Sobolev ball, sharp in order and in the constant

Theorem 33.3.4, page 1173 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $P_a$ be the Cauchy density of width $a>0$, $s>0$, and $H^s$ the Sobolev space of order $s$; $C_s$ denotes a constant depending only on $s$. Suppose $\|\mu\|_{H^s}\le M$ and $\|P_a*\mu\|_2\le\varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon/M$ small enough depending on $a$ and $s$. Then $\|\mu\|_2\le C_sM\bigl(2a/\log(M/\varepsilon)\bigr)^s$, and no bound of smaller order holds uniformly over the class: the modulus of continuity of the inverse is of this order. The sharp modulus $\sup\{\|\mu\|_2:\|\mu\|_{H^s}\le M,\|P_a*\mu\|_2\le\varepsilon\}$ is $(1+o(1))M(a/\log(M/\varepsilon))^s$ as $\varepsilon/M\to0$.

Source: [`ch/cd1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cd1.tex), label `cd:thm:log`.

<a id="spectral_cutoff_deconvolution_of_cauchy_noise_with_a_target_analytic_in_a_strip"></a>

### Polynomial upper rate for density deconvolution with Cauchy noise and a target analytic in a strip

Proposition 33.4.1, page 1174 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $Y_1,\dots,Y_n$ be i.i.d. observations $Y_j=X_j+E_j$, with $X_j$ of density $f$ independent of $E_j$, Cauchy noise of width $a>0$, with $\int e^{2w|\omega|}|\widehat f(\omega)|^2d\omega\le2\pi M^2$ for some $w>0$, where $\widehat f(\omega)=\int f(x)e^{-i\omega x}dx$. The spectral cutoff estimator $\widehat f_n(x)=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{|\omega|\le\Omega}e^{a|\omega|}\widehat\phi_n(\omega)e^{i\omega x}d\omega$, with $\widehat\phi_n(\omega)=n^{-1}\sum_{j\le n}e^{-i\omega Y_j}$ and $\Omega=\log n/(2(a+w))$, has root mean integrated squared error $O(n^{-w/(2(a+w))})$. This is an upper bound only; no lower bound is claimed.

Source: [`ch/cd1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cd1.tex), label `cd:prop:strip`.

<a id="open_problem_estimating_the_critical_width_of_a_positive_datum"></a>

### Problem: estimating the critical width of noisy positive data

Problem 33.1, page 1177 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Let $u\ge0$ with $\int u(x)(1+x^2)^{-1}dx<\infty$ and $c^*(u)=\sup\{c\ge0:u=P_c*\nu\text{ for some measure }\nu\ge0\}$, with $P_c$ the Cauchy density of width $c$. Given noisy data $u+\text{noise}$, estimate $c^*(u)$. For atomic sources with positive weights $c^*$ is the smallest width among the poles, estimable by a matrix pencil on a class with bounded order, weights bounded below, separation and no aliasing; without weights bounded below there is no uniform rate, since $c^*$ is discontinuous ($(1-\delta)P_A+\delta P_r$ has $c^*=r<A$ for every $\delta>0$). For general sources $c^*$ is a boundary of a convex cone in an infinite dimensional space. Status: open.

Source: [`ch/cd1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cd1.tex), label `cd:prob:width`.

<a id="open_problem_does_positivity_alone_give_a_polynomial_rate_for_the_thorin_family"></a>

### Problem: positivity and rates for the Thorin family

Problem 33.2, page 1177 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Let $P_a$ be the Cauchy density of width $a>0$. Positive sources of the form $P_w*\nu$ with $\nu\ge0$ of mass at most $B$ have the polynomial exponent $w/(a+w)$ for deconvolution at $b=0$, but this comes from the smoothing and the mass bound, not from positivity, and the zero counting measure of the Riemann zeta function has infinite mass. Positivity does not improve the logarithmic minimax rate over smoothness classes of densities in the worst case, and prescribing a number of sign changes of the Fourier transform does not help.
