Open: is the Thorin family, the family of the solutions $\mu\ge0$ of $P_{1-\theta}*\mu=u_1$, $\frac12\le\theta<1$, with $u_1(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(\xi'/\xi)(1+iv)$ and $\xi$ the completed zeta function, in a class on which positivity alone gives a polynomial rate?

Source: [`ch/cd1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cd1.tex), label `cd:prob:rates`.

<a id="open_problem_three_lines_with_positivity_on_a_window"></a>

### Problem: Hölder bound between levels from data on a window for positive sources

Problem 33.3, page 1178 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Let $P_y$ be the Cauchy density of width $y>0$. The three lines bound needs an a priori bound at a level below the target, and for nonnegative sources with data in $L^2$ on the whole line this bound is removed. For data known only on a window, the mass in a window of a positive source is controlled by the data alone. Open: does positivity give a Hölder bound between levels from data on a window, without any a priori bound below the target, with an exponent determined by the data?

Source: [`ch/cd1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cd1.tex), label `cd:prob:three`.

## Chapter 34. Cauchy deconvolution from U_1 to U_1/2

<a id="cauchy_transport_identity_for_the_density_at_every_level"></a>

### Cauchy transport: the density at level theta is the Cauchy smoothing of the critical zeros plus a signed defect from zeros off the line

Proposition 34.1.2, page 1182 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ counted with multiplicity, $P_a(x)=\frac{a}{\pi(a^2+x^2)}$ for $a>0$, $Q_a(x)=\frac{a}{\pi(a^2+x^2)}$ for real $a\ne0$, $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\theta+iv)$ and $\mathfrak U_{1/2}=\sum_{\sigma_\rho=1/2}\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$. For $\theta>\frac12$ and $\theta+iv$ not a zero, $u_\theta=P_{\theta-1/2}*\mathfrak U_{1/2}+R_\theta$ with $R_\theta(v)=\sum_{\sigma_\rho>1/2}\bigl[Q_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}+Q_{\theta-1+\sigma_\rho}\bigr](v-\gamma_\rho)$, the sum over the zeros off the critical line each taken together with its reflection $1-\bar\rho$. In particular $u_1=P_{1/2}*\mathfrak U_{1/2}+R_1$, the pair of a zero off the line being positive at $\theta=1$ and signed only for $\theta<\sigma_\rho$. Under the Riemann hypothesis $R_\theta=0$.

Source: [`ch/c34.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/c34.tex), label `cf:prop:transport`.

<a id="local_positivity_of_the_density_from_a_narrowing_zero_free_region"></a>

### Local positivity of the Thorin density from any zero free region that narrows with the height

Corollary 34.1.3, page 1182 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ and $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\theta+iv)$. Let $\eta:[0,\infty)\to(0,\frac12]$ be nonincreasing and suppose every zero satisfies $\sigma_\rho\le1-\eta(\lvert\gamma_\rho\rvert)$. Then $u_\theta(v)>0$ whenever $\theta>\frac12$, $\theta\ge1-\eta(\lvert v\rvert+\frac12)$ and $\xi(\theta+iv)\ne0$. The proof groups the zeros of the Hadamard sum into orbits of $\rho\mapsto1-\bar\rho$; an orbit with $\sigma_\rho>\theta$ is negative only within distance $\frac12$ of its ordinate.

Source: [`ch/c34.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/c34.tex), label `cf:cor:localpos`.

<a id="zeros_off_the_line_are_invisible_in_the_limit_of_the_density_at_one_half"></a>

### The density tends to the critical zero counting measure as the level tends to one half, zeros off the line being invisible

Proposition 34.2.1, page 1183 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function with zeros $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ and $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\theta+iv)=\sum_\rho Q_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}(v-\gamma_\rho)$ with $Q_a(x)=\frac{a}{\pi(a^2+x^2)}$. As $\theta\downarrow\frac12$, in the sense of distributions, $u_\theta\to\mathfrak U_{1/2}=\sum_{\sigma_\rho=1/2}\delta_{\gamma_\rho}$. A zero $\rho$ off the line and its reflection $1-\bar\rho$ contribute $Q_{\theta-\sigma_\rho}+Q_{\theta-1+\sigma_\rho}\to Q_{1/2-\sigma_\rho}+Q_{\sigma_\rho-1/2}=0$, because $a\mapsto Q_a$ is continuous from $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$ to $L^1(\mathbb{R})$ and the far terms are bounded by $\lvert\gamma_\rho\rvert^{-2}$ uniformly in $\theta\in[\frac12,1]$.

Source: [`ch/cf1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf1.tex), label `cf:prop:ends`.

<a id="zeros_of_the_davenport_heilbronn_function_off_the_line_below_height_200"></a>

### The four zeros of the Davenport and Heilbronn function off the critical line below height 200 and their enclosures

Result 34.2, page 1184 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $\kappa=(\sqrt{10-2\sqrt5}-2)/(\sqrt5-1)$ and $f(s)=5^{-s}\bigl[\zeta(s,\frac15)+\kappa\zeta(s,\frac25)-\kappa\zeta(s,\frac35)-\zeta(s,\frac45)\bigr]$ the Davenport and Heilbronn function, with $\zeta(s,a)$ the Hurwitz zeta function, and $\Lambda(s)=(5/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)f(s)$, which is entire with $\Lambda(s)=\Lambda(1-s)$. Computed in ball arithmetic: the zeros of $f$ off the critical line with $0<\gamma<200$ are $0.8085171825+85.6993484854i$, $0.6508300806+114.1633427308i$, $0.5743560505+166.4793059132i$, $0.7242576946+176.7024612429i$ together with their reflections in the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\frac12$, each the only zero in a square of half width $10^{-16}$ about its centre, so the printed decimals are correct. The count rests on $130$ zeros of $\Lambda$ with $0<\gamma<200$ by the argument principle against $122$ sign changes of $\Lambda(\frac12+it)$ on a grid of step $\frac1{50}$, the difference $8=2\cdot4$ being the off line zeros and their reflections. This is a computation and not a statement for all heights. The zeros were found by Spira (1994); the ball arithmetic enclosures and the count are the book's.

Source: [`ch/cf1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf1.tex), label `cf:res:dhzeros`.

<a id="detectability_of_a_symmetric_pair_of_zeros_off_the_line_from_one_level"></a>

### A symmetric pair of zeros off the line exceeds a double zero on the line by a second order term in the deviation, growing like the fifth inverse power of the level

Proposition 34.3.1, page 1187 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $P_a(x)=\frac{a}{\pi(a^2+x^2)}$, $a=\theta-\frac12>\delta>0$. At the centre $v=\gamma$ the density at level $\theta$ of a pair of zeros at $\frac12\pm\delta+i\gamma$ exceeds that of a double zero at $\frac12+i\gamma$ by $\Delta(a,\delta)=\frac1\pi\bigl(\frac1{a-\delta}+\frac1{a+\delta}\bigr)-\frac2{\pi a}=\frac{2\delta^2}{\pi a(a^2-\delta^2)}$. In the parameter $\eta=\delta^2$ the pair differs from the double zero by $\eta\,\partial_a^2P_a+O(\eta^2)$, and $\int_{\mathbb{R}}(\partial_a^2P_a(x))^2dx=\frac3{4\pi a^5}$.

Source: [`ch/cf1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf1.tex), label `cf:prop:detect`.

<a id="open_best_resolution_of_the_pair_parameter_from_levels_above_a_threshold"></a>

### Open: the best resolution of the symmetric pair parameter from data at levels above a threshold

Problem 34.1, page 1188 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Consider a symmetric pair of zeros of the completed Riemann zeta function at $\frac12\pm\delta+i\gamma$, with parameter $\eta=\delta^2$, and data given by the density $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\theta+iv)$ at levels $\theta\ge\theta_{\min}$ with observation error. What is the best possible resolution of $\eta$, and does the particle filter with the pair parametrisation reach it? This is posed as an open problem.

Source: [`ch/cf1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf1.tex), label `cf:op:pairres`.

<a id="non_asymptotic_concentration_of_the_particle_approximation_with_multinomial_resampling_under_a_ratio_minorisation_of_the_mutation_kernels"></a>

### Non asymptotic concentration inequality for a Feynman Kac particle system with multinomial resampling and fixed potentials under a ratio minorisation of the mutation kernels

Theorem 34.5.1, page 1195 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\eta_0$ be a probability measure on a space $E$, $G_0,\dots,G_{n-1}$ positive bounded potentials with $\sup G_k/\inf G_k<\infty$, $M_1,\dots,M_n$ Markov kernels, $\eta_{k+1}=\Psi_{G_k}(\eta_k)M_{k+1}$ with $\Psi_G(\mu)(dx)=G(x)\mu(dx)/\mu(G)$, and let $\eta_k^N$ be the empirical measure of the particle system that draws $N$ independent particles from $\eta_0$ and then, given generation $k$, $N$ independent particles from $\Psi_{G_k}(\eta_k^N)M_{k+1}$ (multinomial resampling followed by mutation). With $\mathcal Q_{k+1}(x,dy)=G_k(x)M_{k+1}(x,dy)$, $G_{k,n}=\mathcal Q_{k+1}\cdots\mathcal Q_n(1)$, $\mathcal P_{k,n}f=\mathcal Q_{k+1}\cdots\mathcal Q_n(f)/G_{k,n}$, $g_{k,n}=\sup_{x,y}G_{k,n}(x)/G_{k,n}(y)$, $\varkappa_{k,n}$ the Dobrushin coefficient of $\mathcal P_{k,n}$ and $S_n=\sum_{k=0}^ng_{k,n}\varkappa_{k,n}$, for every measurable $f$ with oscillation at most $1$, every $N$ and every $x>0$, $\mathbb P(\lvert\eta_n^N(f)-\eta_n(f)\rvert\ge x)\le2(n+1)\exp(-Nx^2/(2S_n^2))$ and $\mathbb E[(\eta_n^N(f)-\eta_n(f))^2]^{1/2}\le S_n/\sqrt N$. The theorem covers a fixed schedule and fixed kernels, not samplers with adaptive tempering or random walk Metropolis moves. The proof is given (in the style of Del Moral 2004).

Source: [`ch/cf2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf2.tex), label `cf:thm:conc`.

<a id="concentration_of_the_particle_filter_along_the_cauchy_flow"></a>

### Concentration bound uniform in the number of tempering steps for the Cauchy flow when the parameters stay away from the levels

Corollary 34.5.4, page 1197 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Consider the Gaussian tolerance posterior of the chapter, in which zeros $\sigma_j+i\gamma_j$, $j\le K$, in a window of heights are fitted to the values $y_l(v_i)$ of the density at levels $\theta_l$ and heights $v_i$ with tolerance $\varepsilon$, and the parameter space is restricted to $\Theta_\varsigma=\{z:\lvert\theta_l-\sigma_j\rvert\ge\varsigma\text{ for all levels }\theta_l\text{ and zeros }j\}$. Then the total log likelihood $\ell$ has $\operatorname{osc}(\ell)\le\Omega_\varsigma=\frac1{2\varepsilon^2}\sum_{l,i}\bigl(\lvert y_l(v_i)\rvert+\frac K{\pi\varsigma}\bigr)^2$, and a tempering schedule with $n=\max(1,\lceil\Omega_\varsigma/c\rceil)$ equal increments has potentials with $\sup G/\inf G\le e^c$. If the mutation kernels satisfy the ratio minorisation $M(x,\cdot)\ge\epsilon M(y,\cdot)$ for all $x,y$, then for every posterior functional $f$ of oscillation at most one, for the idealised particle system of the concentration theorem of the chapter, $\mathbb P(\lvert\eta_n^N(f)-\eta_n(f)\rvert\ge x)\le2\exp(-\frac12Nx^2\epsilon^6e^{-2c})$ for every $N$ and every $x>0$. Without the minorisation the concentration theorem holds with its finite constant $S_n$, which is not uniform in $n$. Random walk Metropolis kernels do not satisfy the minorisation.

Source: [`ch/cf2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf2.tex), label `cf:cor:cauchyconc`.

<a id="one_level_determines_the_density_only_with_an_order_condition_and_inversion_is_unstable"></a>

### What the density at level one determines: unique continuation for entire functions of order one, a counterexample without the order condition, and the Poisson inversion

Proposition 34.6.1, page 1202 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $F_1,F_2$ be real entire functions of order at most one with all zeros in $0<\operatorname{Re}s<1$ and $u^{(j)}_\theta(v)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(F_j'/F_j)(\theta+iv)$. (a) If $u^{(1)}_1=u^{(2)}_1$ on an interval then $F_1'/F_1=F_2'/F_2$, so $u^{(1)}_\theta=u^{(2)}_\theta$ for every $\theta$. (b) The order hypothesis cannot be dropped: $F=\xi e^{G}$ with $\xi$ the completed Riemann zeta function and $G(s)=-(10\pi)^{-1}\cos(10\pi(s-1))$ is real entire with the zeros of $\xi$, its densities at the levels $1$ and $0.9$ equal those of $\xi$ on the whole line, and its density at $\frac34$ is $u_{3/4}(v)-\pi^{-1}\cosh(10\pi v)$. (c) If no zero of $\xi$ has real part at least $\frac34$ (in particular under the Riemann hypothesis) then $u_1=P_{1/4}*u_{3/4}$ with $P_a$ the Cauchy density of scale $a$, whose Fourier multiplier is $e^{-\lvert\omega\rvert/4}$, so an error at frequency $\omega$ in $u_1$ is magnified by $e^{\lvert\omega\rvert/4}$ in the recovery of $u_{3/4}$.

Source: [`ch/cf2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf2.tex), label `cf:prop:determine`.

<a id="zero_density_controls_the_negative_part_of_the_thorin_measure"></a>

### The negative part of the Thorin density at level theta is bounded by the number of zeros to the right of theta, and is a fraction T to the minus (theta minus one half) over four of its mass unconditionally

Theorem 34.7.1, page 1203 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\theta+iv)$ the density of $\mathfrak U_\theta$, $u_\theta^-=\max(-u_\theta,0)$ and $N(\theta,T)$ the number of zeros with $\operatorname{Re}\rho>\theta$ and $0<\operatorname{Im}\rho\le T$, with multiplicity. Let $\frac12<\theta<1$ and $T\ge2$. (a) $\int_0^Tu_\theta^-(v)\,dv\le N(\theta,T+\frac12)$. (b) If $T$ is not an ordinate and no zero with $0<\gamma_\rho<T$ has real part $\theta$ then $\mathfrak U_\theta((0,T])=\int_0^Tu_\theta=\frac T{2\pi}\log\frac T{2\pi e}-2N(\theta,T)+O(\log T)$. (c) By Selberg's density theorem $N(\theta,T)\ll T^{1-(\theta-1/2)/4}\log T$, for $T$ as in (b) the negative part of $\mathfrak U_\theta$ on $(0,T]$ is a fraction $O(N(\theta,T+\frac12)/(T\log T))=O(T^{-(\theta-1/2)/4})$ of its mass. The Riemann hypothesis is not assumed.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:thm:negmass`.

<a id="open_how_negative_can_the_thorin_density_be_without_the_riemann_hypothesis"></a>

### Open: how negative can the Thorin measure be at a level between one half and one without assuming RH

Problem 34.2, page 1203 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Let $\mathfrak U_\theta$ be the measure on the line with density $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\theta+iv)$, $\xi$ the completed Riemann zeta function. How negative can $\mathfrak U_\theta$ be for $\frac12<\theta<1$ without assuming the Riemann hypothesis? The book proves a bound through the zero density function (negative part on $(0,T]$ at most $N(\theta,T+\frac12)$) and leaves the question open.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:op:negdepth`.

<a id="open_converse_of_the_negative_mass_bound_for_zero_density"></a>

### Open: does a linear bound on the negative Thorin mass defect imply a zero density bound

Problem 34.3, page 1204 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Let $N(\theta,T)$ be the number of zeros of the Riemann zeta function with real part above $\theta$ and ordinate in $(0,T]$, and $\mathrm{def}(\theta)$ the defect of the negative Thorin mass at level $\theta$ as defined in the chapter. Does $\mathrm{def}(\theta)\le A(1-\theta)$ for all $\theta$ imply $N(\theta,T)\ll T^{A(1-\theta)+\epsilon}$ for every $\epsilon>0$? The book proves the converse for separated zeros and a weighted bound for all zeros, and leaves the general question open.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:op:converse`.

<a id="a_separated_zero_off_the_line_forces_negative_thorin_mass"></a>

### A separated zero off the line forces negative Thorin mass in a half disc to its left

Proposition 34.7.2, page 1205 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function, $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\theta+iv)$, $u_\theta^-=\max(-u_\theta,0)$, $k(\rho)$ the multiplicity of a zero $\rho$, $d(\rho)$ the distance from $\rho$ to the nearest other zero and $\mathrm{cr}(\rho)=\sum k(\rho')/\lvert\rho'-\rho\rvert$ over distinct zeros $\rho'\ne\rho$ with $\lvert\gamma_{\rho'}-\gamma_\rho\rvert\le2$, the reflected zero included. Let $\rho_0=\sigma_0+i\gamma_0$ be a zero of multiplicity $k$ with $\sigma_0>\frac12$ and $\gamma_0\ge3$. There is an absolute constant $C_1\ge1$ such that if $r\le\min\bigl(1,\sigma_0-\frac12,\frac12d(\rho_0),k/(\pi(\mathrm{cr}(\rho_0)+C_1\log\gamma_0))\bigr)$ then $\int_{\sigma_0-r}^{\sigma_0}\int_{\gamma_0-r}^{\gamma_0+r}u_\theta^-(v)\,dv\,d\theta\ge kr/\pi$.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:prop:converse`.

<a id="two_sided_control_of_negative_thorin_mass_and_zero_count_for_separated_zeros"></a>

### Two sided bound between the negative Thorin mass and the number of separated zeros to the right of a level

Corollary 34.7.3, page 1206 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. With the notation of the converse proposition for a separated zero (the density $u_\theta$, $u_\theta^-=\max(-u_\theta,0)$, $\mathrm{cr}$ and the constant $C_1$), let $\frac12<\theta_0<1$, $T\ge3$ and $E(\theta_0,T)=\int_{\theta_0}^1\int_0^{T+1}u_\theta^-(v)\,dv\,d\theta$. Let $N_{\mathrm{sep}}(\theta_0,T;c,\delta)$ count the zeros with $\operatorname{Re}\rho>\theta_0$, $3\le\operatorname{Im}\rho\le T$, $\mathrm{cr}(\rho)\le c$ and distance at least $2\delta$ from every other zero, and $r=\min(\delta,1/(\pi(c+C_1\log T)))$. Then $\frac r\pi N_{\mathrm{sep}}(\theta_0+r,T;c,\delta)\le E(\theta_0,T)\le\int_{\theta_0}^1N(\theta,T+\frac32)\,d\theta=\sum_{\operatorname{Re}\rho>\theta_0,\,0<\operatorname{Im}\rho\le T+3/2}(\operatorname{Re}\rho-\theta_0)$, where $N(\theta,T)$ counts zeros with real part above $\theta$ and imaginary part in $(0,T]$.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:cor:twosided`.

<a id="every_zero_off_the_line_forces_negative_thorin_mass_in_proportion_to_its_isolation"></a>

### Every zero off the line forces negative Thorin mass at least its isolation distance over the logarithm of the height

Theorem 34.7.4, page 1206 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. With $u_\theta$, $k(\rho)$, $d(\rho)$, $\mathrm{cr}(\rho)$, $C_1$ and $E(\theta_0,T)=\int_{\theta_0}^1\int_0^{T+1}u_\theta^-\,dv\,d\theta$ as in the converse proposition and its corollary, let $\theta_0>\frac12$ and for a zero $\rho$ with $\operatorname{Re}\rho>\theta_0$ put $r(\rho)=\min\bigl(1,\operatorname{Re}\rho-\theta_0,\frac12d(\rho),k(\rho)/(\pi(\mathrm{cr}(\rho)+C_1\log\gamma_\rho))\bigr)$. Then for $T\ge3$, $E(\theta_0,T)\ge\frac1\pi\sum k(\rho)r(\rho)$, the sum over distinct zeros with $\operatorname{Re}\rho>\theta_0$ and $3\le\gamma_\rho\le T$. For an absolute $c>0$, $r(\rho)\ge c\min(\operatorname{Re}\rho-\theta_0,\min(d(\rho),1)/\log\gamma_\rho)$, and so $E(\theta_0,T)\gg\frac1{\log T}\sum\min((\operatorname{Re}\rho-\theta_0)\log T,d(\rho),1)$ over the same zeros.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:thm:converse`.

<a id="open_consequences_of_a_zero_free_half_plane_at_7_8_for_the_thorin_framework"></a>

### Open: what a zero free half plane at theta_0, for instance 7/8, gives in the Cauchy flow framework

Problem 34.4, page 1207 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. Let QRH($\theta_0$) be the statement that the Riemann zeta function has no zero with real part greater than $\theta_0$, equivalent to positivity of the Thorin measure $\mathfrak U_\tau$ for every $\tau>\theta_0$. What does QRH($\theta_0$) give in the framework of the particle filter and the Cauchy flow, for instance at $\theta_0=\frac78$? This is posed as an open problem; QRH(7/8) is announced in unrefereed preprints and is not used as a theorem.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:op:qrh78`.

<a id="positivity_margin_of_the_thorin_density_under_the_quasi_riemann_hypothesis"></a>

### Under a zero free half plane the Thorin density has a positive margin proportional to the distance from the abscissa and to the logarithm of the height

Proposition 34.7.5, page 1208 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on The quasi Riemann hypothesis QRH(theta_0), that is, that the Riemann zeta function has no zero with real part greater than theta_0, for the stated theta_0 with 1/2 <= theta_0 < 1.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the completed Riemann zeta function and $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\theta+iv)$. Assume $\xi$ has no zero with real part greater than $\theta_0$, where $\frac12\le\theta_0<1$. Then there are constants $c>0$ and $v_0$ such that $u_\theta(v)\ge c(\theta-\theta_0)\log v$ for all $\theta_0<\theta\le1$ and $v\ge v_0$. The proof combines the positivity of every term of the Hadamard sum, the Riemann and von Mangoldt formula and an explicit bound for the argument of the zeta function on the critical line.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:prop:margin`.

<a id="de_la_vallee_poussin_inequality_for_the_thorin_density_in_general_cosine_form"></a>

### De la Vallée Poussin inequality for the Thorin density with every nonnegative cosine polynomial (general version)

Theorem 34.8.1, page 1209 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi(s)=\frac12s(s-1)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(\frac s2)\zeta(s)$, $u_\theta(v)=\frac1\pi\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\theta+iv)$ and $g_\theta(v)=\operatorname{Re}\bigl[\frac1s+\frac1{s-1}-\frac12\log\pi+\frac12\psi(\frac s2)\bigr]$ with $s=\theta+iv$ and $\psi$ the digamma function. For $\theta>1$ and every real $v$, $3u_\theta(0)+4u_\theta(v)+u_\theta(2v)\le\frac1\pi[3g_\theta(0)+4g_\theta(v)+g_\theta(2v)]$. More generally, for every cosine polynomial $p(\omega)=\sum_{k=0}^Ka_k\cos k\omega$ with $p\ge0$ and $a_k\ge0$, $\sum_ka_ku_\theta(kv)\le\pi^{-1}\sum_ka_kg_\theta(kv)$. The proof uses $\pi u_\theta=g_\theta+\operatorname{Re}\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(\theta+iv)$ and that $-\operatorname{Re}\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(\theta+iv)=\sum_{n\ge2}\Lambda(n)n^{-\theta}\cos(v\log n)$, with $\Lambda$ the von Mangoldt function, is a cosine series with nonnegative coefficients.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:thm:dvp`.

<a id="open_certificate_for_the_screen_in_each_window"></a>

### Open: turn the calibrated GBC screen into a proof of the zero count in each window

Problem 34.5, page 1209 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: open.

Statement. The GBC screen of the chapter returns a posterior for the real parts of the zeros of $\xi$ in a window of heights, calibrated on simulations, which is evidence and not proof. Can it be turned into a proof in each window, for instance through the contour moment $M_0$ computed in interval arithmetic and shown to be less than $\frac12$ (the argument principle)? This is posed as an open problem.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:op:certificate`.

<a id="crude_zero_free_region_constant_from_the_thorin_form_of_de_la_vallee_poussin"></a>

### Zero free region of width c over log gamma with every c below 14 minus 8 root 3 over 5 from the Thorin form

Corollary 34.8.2, page 1210 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $c_\ast=(14-8\sqrt3)/5=0.028719\ldots$. For every $c<c_\ast$ there is $\gamma_c$ such that every zero $\rho=\sigma_\rho+i\gamma_\rho$ of the Riemann zeta function with $\gamma_\rho\ge\gamma_c$ has $1-\sigma_\rho\ge c/\log\gamma_\rho$. The proof takes $v=\gamma_0$ and $\theta=1+a/\log\gamma_0$ in the inequality of the cosine polynomial $3+4\cos\omega+\cos2\omega$, with optimum $a=(4\sqrt3-6)/5$. Sharper constants are known from other methods.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:cor:zfr`.

<a id="the_davenport_heilbronn_function_has_the_hadamard_density_but_violates_qrh_for_every_level"></a>

### The Davenport and Heilbronn function satisfies the Cauchy flow identities and violates the quasi Riemann hypothesis at every level below one

Proposition 34.8.3, page 1210 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\kappa=(\sqrt{10-2\sqrt5}-2)/(\sqrt5-1)$ and $f(s)=5^{-s}\bigl[\zeta(s,\frac15)+\kappa\zeta(s,\frac25)-\kappa\zeta(s,\frac35)-\zeta(s,\frac45)\bigr]$ the Davenport and Heilbronn function, with $\zeta(s,a)$ the Hurwitz zeta function, and $\Lambda_{\mathrm{DH}}(s)=(5/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)f(s)$, entire of order one, real on the real axis with $\Lambda_{\mathrm{DH}}(s)=\Lambda_{\mathrm{DH}}(1-s)$. The Hadamard sum, the Cauchy transport identity, the equivalence of positivity of the density at every level above $\theta$ with the absence of zeros to the right of $\theta$, and the detectability proposition hold for $\Lambda_{\mathrm{DH}}$ with the same proofs; so does the formula of Balazard, Saias and Yor with $h=f$ and the sum over all zeros of $f$ to the right of the level, and the deconvolution theorem with the line $\operatorname{Re}s=1$ replaced by $\operatorname{Re}s=2$, to the right of all zeros since $\lvert f(s)-1\rvert\le\zeta(2)-1<1$ there. The function $f$ has infinitely many zeros with real part above $1$ (Davenport and Heilbronn), so $\Lambda_{\mathrm{DH}}$ violates the absence of zeros to the right of $\theta$ for every $\theta<1$, and its lowest zeros off the line, $0.8085\ldots+85.6993\ldots i$ and $0.6508\ldots+114.1633\ldots i$, already violate it for $\theta=\frac34$ and $\theta=\frac58$.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:prop:barrier`.

<a id="multilevel_inequality_for_the_thorin_density_with_level_kernels"></a>

### Multilevel inequality for the Thorin density with a cosine polynomial and a level kernel of nonnegative Laplace transform

Theorem 34.8.4, page 1211 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Fix $v\ge2$, $L=\log v$, and let $u_\theta$ and $g_\theta$ be the density of the Thorin measure of the Riemann zeta function and its explicit gamma part. A level kernel is a finite signed measure $w$ with compact support in $(0,\infty)$ acting by $w[u](y)=\int u_{1+x/L}(y)\,w(dx)$, and likewise on $g$, with Laplace transform $\phi_w(\lambda)=\int e^{-x\lambda}w(dx)$. Let $p(\omega)=\sum_{k=0}^Ka_k\cos k\omega\ge0$ with $a_k\ge0$ and let $\phi_w(\lambda)\ge0$ for $\lambda>0$. Then $\sum_{k=0}^Ka_k\,w[u](kv)\le\frac1\pi\sum_{k=0}^Ka_k\,w[g](kv)$.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:thm:multilevel`.

<a id="zero_free_constant_of_an_admissible_cosine_polynomial_and_level_kernel_pair"></a>

### Zero free constant y star of an admissible pair of a cosine polynomial and a level kernel

Corollary 34.8.6, page 1212 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $p(\omega)=\sum_{k=0}^Ka_k\cos k\omega\ge0$ with $a_k\ge0$ and let $w$ be a level kernel with compact support in $(0,\infty)$ and Laplace transform $\phi_w\ge0$, such that $\int w(dx)P_{x+y}(\tau)\ge0$ for all $y\ge0$ and real $\tau$, with $P_a$ the Cauchy density of scale $a$ (the pair is called admissible, which is equivalent to positive definiteness of the even extension of $\phi_w$). Assume $\phi_w(0)>0$ and put $I=\int_0^\infty\phi_w$, $J(y)=\int_0^\infty e^{-y\lambda}\phi_w(\lambda)\,d\lambda$ and $A=a_1+\dots+a_K$. If $(a_1-a_0)I>\frac A2\phi_w(0)$ the equation $a_1J(y)=a_0I+\frac A2\phi_w(0)$ has a unique root $y^\ast>0$ and every zero $\rho$ of the Riemann zeta function with large ordinate has $(1-\operatorname{Re}\rho)\log\gamma_\rho\ge y^\ast-o(1)$. Otherwise the scheme gives no positive constant.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:cor:ystar`.

<a id="no_admissible_pair_gives_a_zero_free_constant_above_one_over_log_gamma"></a>

### No admissible pair of a cosine polynomial and a level kernel gives a zero free region wider than a constant below one over log gamma

Proposition 34.8.7, page 1213 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $p(\omega)=\sum_{k=0}^Ka_k\cos k\omega\ge0$ with $a_k\ge0$ and $a_1>a_0$, $A=a_1+\dots+a_K$, and let $w$ be a level kernel with Laplace transform $\phi_w$, admissible, that is $\phi_w(\lambda)\ge0$ for $\lambda>0$ and the even extension of $\phi_w$ is positive definite, and normalised by $\phi_w(0)=1$. If $y>0$ satisfies $a_1\int_0^\infty e^{-y\lambda}\phi_w(\lambda)\,d\lambda\ge a_0\int_0^\infty\phi_w(\lambda)\,d\lambda+\frac A2$ then $y\le\frac2A\bigl(a_1-a_0-a_0\log\frac{a_1}{a_0}\bigr)<\frac{2(a_1-a_0)}A\le1$. In particular the zero free constant of the corresponding scheme for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, $(1-\sigma_\rho)\log\gamma_\rho\ge y^\ast$, obeys these bounds, which are $0.0548$ for $3+4\cos\omega+\cos2\omega$ and $0.1051$ for the cosine polynomial of degree $4$ with coefficients $\approx(1,1.705,1.044,0.425,0.089)$.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:prop:barrier2`.

<a id="zero_free_constants_of_admissible_pairs_computed_by_optimisation"></a>

### Computed zero free constants of admissible pairs: about 1 over 11.8 log gamma with a level kernel with derivatives

Table 34.12, page 1214 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Computed (code cf_arith.py, not certified): in the scheme of the zero free constant of an admissible pair, with $(1-\sigma_\rho)\ge c/\log\gamma_\rho$ for the zeros of the Riemann zeta function, the optimised constants $c=y^\ast$ over cosine polynomials $p=\lvert\sum_jb_je^{ij\omega}\rvert^2$ with $b_j\ge0$ are $0.0287$ for one level with $3+4\cos\omega+\cos2\omega$, $0.0376$, $0.0542$ and $0.0573$ for the best single level polynomials of degree $2$, $3$ and $4$ to $8$, $0.0377$, $0.0704$ and $0.0742$ for two levels in the curvature limit with $3+4\cos\omega+\cos2\omega$ and the best polynomials of degree $3$ and $4$, and $0.0800$, $0.0826$, $0.0841$ and $0.0849$ for a level with derivatives and a polynomial factor of degree $2$, $3$, $4$ and $5$ (best level $0.89$ at degree $4$). The rows with derivatives are optima on finite constraint grids and at degree $4$ and $5$ the kernels are not certified admissible. All values lie below the proved cap $0.1051$. The curvature and derivative kernels are limits of level kernels and are not covered by the multilevel inequality itself.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:tab:arith`.

<a id="computed_ceiling_of_the_admissible_scheme_by_linear_programming"></a>

### Computed ceiling of about 1 over 11.3 log gamma for smoothings of nonnegative positive definite type, by linear programming

Table 34.13, page 1216 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Computed by discretised linear programming (code cf_lp.py, not certified: positive definiteness is imposed at finitely many frequencies, the support is truncated at $\lambda_{\max}$ and the polynomial and the smoothing are optimised alternately, so the rows with an optimised polynomial are lower estimates): the best zero free constant $c$ in $(1-\sigma_\rho)\log\gamma_\rho\ge c$ of the scheme of the zero free constant of an admissible pair, over every smoothing $\phi$ with $0\le\phi\le1$, $\phi(0)=1$ and positive definite even extension, is $0.0460$ and $0.0450$ for $p=3+4\cos\omega+\cos2\omega$ on a uniform and a low frequency grid, $0.0874$ for the degree $4$ polynomial of the chapter and for degree at most $4$ with both optimised, and $0.0881$ for degree at most $8$, that is about $1/(11.3\log\gamma)$, against $0.0849$ for the best level kernel and the proved cap $0.1051$.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:tab:lp`.

<a id="one_far_level_paired_with_its_reflection_gives_a_zero_free_constant_without_smoothing"></a>

### Stechkin pairing with one far level gives a zero free constant outside the admissible class

Proposition 34.8.10, page 1217 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $p(\omega)=\sum_{k=0}^Ka_k\cos k\omega\ge0$ with $a_k\ge0$ and $a_1>a_0$, $A=a_1+\dots+a_K$ and $\kappa_\ast=1/\sqrt5$. Every zero $\rho_0=\sigma_0+i\gamma_0$ of the Riemann zeta function with $\gamma_0$ large has $(1-\sigma_0)\log\gamma_0\ge\frac{2(\sqrt{a_1}-\sqrt{a_0})^2}{(1-\kappa_\ast)A}-o(1)$. For $p=3+4\cos\omega+\cos2\omega$ the constant is $0.05195$ and for the degree $4$ polynomial with coefficients $\approx(1,1.705,1.044,0.425,0.089)$ it is $0.10367=1/9.646$ (computed values; the inequality is proved). The scheme pairs each zero with its reflection through a two level kernel $\delta_x-\kappa\delta_{x_1}$ with $x_1$ of order $\log\gamma_0$, which is outside the admissible class of the barrier proposition. The pairing is the device of Stechkin (1970), and the degree $4$ constant $9.646$ is the constant of Rosser and Schoenfeld (1975), an attribution the book recalls without verifying it; the book adds a proof of the pair inequality by direct algebra and the form for every nonnegative cosine polynomial with $a_1>a_0$.

Source: [`ch/cf3.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf3.tex), label `cf:prop:stechkin`.

<a id="nested_sampling_finds_the_two_davenport_heilbronn_zeros_in_1000_to_1020"></a>

### Nested sampling of the normalised Thorin density finds both zeros of the Davenport and Heilbronn function off the line in heights 1000 to 1020

Result 34.9.2, page 1219 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Computed in ball arithmetic (code cf_dhzeros.py): for the Davenport and Heilbronn function $f$, nested sampling over heights $t\in[1000,1100]$ of the score $s(t)=u_{0.6}(t)/\varrho(t)$, with $u_{0.6}$ the density of the Thorin measure at level $0.6$ of $\Lambda'/\Lambda$ and $\varrho(t)=\frac1{2\pi}\log\frac{5t}{2\pi}$, found negative values in two clusters near $1012.0$ and $1018.8$. Newton's method gives the zeros $0.691404808984+1012.019981489088i$ and $0.698097971267+1018.795762313197i$ of $f$ with their reflections, each the only zero in a square of half width $10^{-18}$. Both zeros are in the table of Balanzario and Sánchez-Ortiz (2007). The run parameters of the nested sampler are those of Polson's note; the heights, scores, enclosures and counts were recomputed for the book. The argument principle in interval arithmetic gives $0$ zeros with real part at least $0.6$ in $[0.6,2]\times[1000,1010]$ and $2$ in $[0.6,2]\times[1010,1020]$. The rest of $[1020,1100]$ was not counted. This is a computation for one function and one band of heights, and none of it is a statement about the Riemann zeta function.

Source: [`ch/cf4.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/cf4.tex), label `cf:res:nsdh`.

## Chapter 35. Balazard, Saias and Yor meet Thorin

<a id="balazard_saias_yor_criterion_at_every_level_and_height_by_a_cauchy_average"></a>

### The Balazard, Saias and Yor criterion at every level theta and every height: the Cauchy average of log of zeta minus log of h equals the sum of Green potentials of the zeros right of the level

Theorem 35.2.1, page 1228 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ its nontrivial zeros counted with multiplicity, $P_a(x)=\frac{a}{\pi(a^2+x^2)}$ for $a>0$, $\frac12\le\theta<1$, $H=\{\operatorname{Re}s>\theta\}$ and $h_\theta(s)=\zeta(s)\frac{s-1}{s-2\theta+1}$, which is analytic in $H$ and has $|h_\theta|=|\zeta|$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\theta$. For a zero $\rho$ with $\beta>\theta$ let $G_\theta(s,\rho)=\log\bigl|\frac{s-2\theta+\bar\rho}{s-\rho}\bigr|\ge0$ be the Green function of $H$ with pole $\rho$. For every $s=\sigma+it\in H$ with $h_\theta(s)\ne0$, $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\log|\zeta(\theta+i\tau)|\,P_{\sigma-\theta}(t-\tau)\,d\tau-\log|h_\theta(s)|=\sum_{\beta>\theta}G_\theta(s,\rho)\ge0$, the integral absolutely convergent and the sum convergent. In particular the defect $D_\theta(t_0)=\int_{-\infty}^\infty\log|\zeta(\theta+i\tau)|\,P_{1-\theta}(t_0-\tau)\,d\tau-\log|h_\theta(1+it_0)|$ equals $\sum_{\beta>\theta}G_\theta(1+it_0,\rho)$, and $\zeta$ has no zero with $\beta>\theta$ (the quasi Riemann hypothesis $\mathrm{QRH}(\theta)$) if and only if $D_\theta(t_0)=0$ for one, equivalently every, real $t_0$. At $\theta=\frac12$, $t_0=0$ this is the theorem of Balazard, Saias and Yor (1999): $\frac1{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^\infty\frac{\log|\zeta(\frac12+it)|}{\frac14+t^2}\,dt=\sum_{\beta>1/2}\log\bigl|\frac{\rho}{1-\rho}\bigr|$.

Source: [`ch/bsy1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy1.tex), label `bsy:thm:bsy`.

<a id="computed_bound_on_the_defect_from_all_possible_zeros_above_the_verified_height"></a>

### Computed bound: zeros above height 3 times 10 to the 12 can change the global defect D_theta(0) by at most about 10 to the minus 12

Remark 35.2.2, page 1229 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. A zero $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ with $\beta>\theta$ contributes about $2(\beta-\theta)(1-\theta)/\gamma^2$ to the defect $D_\theta(0)$, the Cauchy average of $\log|\zeta(\theta+i\tau)|$ with centre $0$ and scale $1-\theta$ minus $\log\frac1{2-2\theta}$, which is zero exactly when no zero has real part above $\theta$. Using the verification of the Riemann hypothesis to height $3\times10^{12}$ (Platt and Trudgian 2021) and the explicit zero counting bound of Hasanalizade, Shen and Wong (2022), the computation in floating point of the book gives that the sum over all possible zeros above that height is below $7.4\times10^{-13}$ at $\theta=\frac12$, $1.85\times10^{-13}$ at $\theta=\frac34$ and $4.7\times10^{-14}$ at $\theta=\frac78$. So the global criterion at $t_0=0$ cannot detect a zero above the verified range, and the criterion is useful only locally, centred where the zeros are. This is a computation from the cited bounds and not a certified interval bound.

Source: [`ch/bsy1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy1.tex), label `bsy:rem:local`.

<a id="equivalent_forms_of_the_riemann_hypothesis_by_defect_and_positivity_of_thorin_measures"></a>

### Equivalent forms of the Riemann hypothesis and of QRH(theta): zero defect, positivity of the Thorin measures, and Cauchy deconvolution from level one

Corollary 35.3.3, page 1231 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function, $\xi$ the completed zeta function, $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ its zeros, $P_a(x)=\frac{a}{\pi(a^2+x^2)}$ and $\mathfrak U_\sigma$ the measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with density $m_\sigma(t)=\pi^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}(\sigma+it)$ for $\sigma>\frac12$ not the real part of a zero. Let $D_\theta(t_0)$ be the Cauchy defect at level $\theta$ and height $t_0$ (the Cauchy average of $\log|\zeta(\theta+i\tau)|$ against $P_{1-\theta}(t_0-\tau)$ minus $\log|h_\theta(1+it_0)|$, $h_\theta(s)=\zeta(s)\frac{s-1}{s-2\theta+1}$). The following are equivalent: (i) the Riemann hypothesis; (ii) $D_{1/2}(t_0)=0$ for some $t_0$; (iii) $\mathfrak U_\sigma$ is a positive measure for every $\sigma\in(\frac12,1)$; (iv) $\mathfrak U_1=P_{1/2}*\nu$ for a positive measure $\nu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with $\int(1+t^2)^{-1}\nu(dt)<\infty$, and then $\nu=\sum_{\beta=1/2}\delta_\gamma$. More generally, for $\theta\in[\frac12,1)$, $\mathrm{QRH}(\theta)$ (no zero with $\beta>\theta$) holds if and only if $D_\theta\equiv0$, if and only if $\mathfrak U_\sigma\ge0$ for all $\sigma>\theta$. The equivalence of (i) and (ii) is the criterion of Balazard, Saias and Yor and the equivalence with (iii) is the argument of Lagarias; the book gives the proofs and the form for $\mathrm{QRH}(\theta)$.

Source: [`ch/bsy1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy1.tex), label `bsy:cor:equiv`.

<a id="levy_density_of_the_reciprocal_xi_function_is_positive_without_hypothesis"></a>

### The Levy density of the reciprocal Xi function is positive with no hypothesis, and is an extended generalised gamma convolution under the Riemann hypothesis

Proposition 35.4.1, page 1232 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the completed zeta function with zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ counted with multiplicity, and $K(u)=\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{-\gamma|u|}\cos\bigl((\beta-\tfrac12)u\bigr)$. Then $K(u)>0$ for every $u\ne0$, with no hypothesis. Hence $x\mapsto\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+x)$ is the characteristic function of an infinitely divisible law with Levy density $K(u)/|u|$, since $\log\frac{\xi(1/2+x)}{\xi(1/2)}=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}2\sin^2(\frac{xu}2)\frac{K(u)}{|u|}du$. Under the Riemann hypothesis it is moreover an extended generalised gamma convolution (EGGC) $\exp\bigl(-\int_{(0,\infty)}\log(1+x^2/y^2)\,U(dy)\bigr)$ with $U=\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_\gamma$. The proof uses that the zeros with $0<\gamma<100$ lie on the line, the lowest at $\gamma_1=14.1347\ldots$, and the bound $\sum_\rho(1+\gamma^2)^{-1}\le2+\gamma_E-\log4\pi<0.05$ ($\gamma_E$ Euler's constant).

Source: [`ch/bsy1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy1.tex), label `bsy:prop:kpos`.

<a id="riemann_hypothesis_equivalent_to_reciprocal_xi_being_an_eggc"></a>

### The Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if the reciprocal of xi is the characteristic function of an extended generalised gamma convolution

Proposition 35.4.2, page 1232 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\xi$ be the completed zeta function. The Riemann hypothesis holds if and only if $x\mapsto\xi(\frac12)/\xi(\frac12+x)$ is the characteristic function of an extended generalised gamma convolution, that is of the form $\exp\bigl(-\int\log(1+x^2/y^2)\,U(dy)\bigr)$ for a measure $U$ on $(0,\infty)$ (a drift or a Gaussian part changes the exponent by an entire function and does not affect the argument). When it is, $U=\sum_{\gamma>0}\delta_\gamma$, the sum over the ordinates of the zeros $\frac12+i\gamma$ with $\gamma>0$ counted with multiplicity. The proof uses that a zero $\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ with $\delta\ne0$ produces a pole of $1/\xi(\frac12+x)$ off the imaginary axis, where an extended generalised gamma convolution is analytic.

Source: [`ch/bsy1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy1.tex), label `bsy:prop:eggc`.

<a id="infinite_divisibility_of_the_reciprocal_davenport_heilbronn_function_without_the_eggc_property"></a>

### The reciprocal of the completed Davenport and Heilbronn function is infinitely divisible with positive Levy density but is not an extended generalised gamma convolution

Theorem 35.4.3, page 1233 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\kappa=(\sqrt{10-2\sqrt5}-2)/(\sqrt5-1)$, $f(s)=5^{-s}\bigl[\zeta(s,\frac15)+\kappa\zeta(s,\frac25)-\kappa\zeta(s,\frac35)-\zeta(s,\frac45)\bigr]$ the Davenport and Heilbronn function ($\zeta(s,a)$ the Hurwitz zeta function) and $\Lambda(s)=(5/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)f(s)$, so that $\Lambda(s)=\Lambda(1-s)$. Let $K_{\mathrm{DH}}(u)=\sum e^{-\gamma|u|}\cos(\delta u)$, the sum over the zeros $\frac12+\delta+i\gamma$ of $\Lambda$ with $\gamma>0$ counted with multiplicity. Then $K_{\mathrm{DH}}(u)>0$ for every $u\ne0$, and $\Lambda(\frac12)/\Lambda(\frac12+x)$ is the characteristic function of an infinitely divisible law. That law is not an extended generalised gamma convolution, because $\Lambda$ has a zero off the line near $0.8085+85.6993\,i$ (known to Spira 1994 and Balanzario and Sanchez-Ortiz 2007). The proof rests on three finite computations certified in ball arithmetic at two precisions: (a) $\Lambda$ has a zero $\frac12+ig$ with $5.09<g<5.10$; (b) $\Lambda$ has no zero $\beta+i\gamma$ with $\beta\ne\frac12$ and $0<\gamma<85.69$ (the argument principle gives $86$ zeros in $[-2,3]\times[-85.69,85.69]$ against $43$ certified sign changes of $\Lambda(\frac12+it)$ on $(0,85.69)$); (c) $\Lambda$ has exactly one zero in a square of half width $10^{-16}$ about $0.8085171824566374+85.6993484853775922\,i$. The floating point zero list to height $300$ is evidence only and is not used in the proof.

Source: [`ch/bsy1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy1.tex), label `bsy:thm:dhid`.

<a id="negative_trace_for_a_combination_of_dirichlet_l_functions_of_imprimitive_characters"></a>

### A combination of L functions of characters modulo 4, 4p, 4q and 4pq with a functional equation whose reciprocal is not infinitely divisible

Remark 35.4.5, page 1236 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $B(s)=L(s,\chi_4)$ with $\chi_4$ the character modulo $4$, $\Lambda_B(s)=(4/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)B(s)$, $p<q<2p$ odd primes, $a=\frac12\log(pq)$, $b=\frac12\log(p/q)$, $P(s)=1+2\sqrt p\,p^{-s}+2\sqrt q\,q^{-s}+\sqrt{pq}\,(pq)^{-s}$. Then $F(s)=(4pq/\pi)^{s/2}\Gamma(\frac{s+1}2)P(s)B(s)=2(pq)^{1/4}\Lambda_B(s)\bigl[\cosh(a(s-\frac12))+2\cosh(b(s-\frac12))\bigr]$ is entire of order one, real and positive on $\mathbb{R}$ and invariant under $s\mapsto1-s$, and $P B$ is a real linear combination of Dirichlet $L$ functions of characters modulo $4$, $4p$, $4q$ and $4pq$ (those induced by $\chi_4$). For $p$ large, $F$ has a lowest pair of zeros above the real axis of the form $\frac12\pm\delta_0+i\gamma_0$ with $\delta_0>0$ and $\gamma_0$ below the first zero of $\Lambda_B$, the trace $K(u)=\sum_{\gamma>0}e^{-\gamma|u|}\cos((\beta-\frac12)u)$ over the zeros $\beta+i\gamma$ of $F$ satisfies $K(u)=2e^{-\gamma_0u}\cos(\delta_0u)+O(e^{-(\gamma_0+\eta)u})$ for some $\eta>0$, and $K((2k+1)\pi/\delta_0)<0$ for all large $k$. So $F(\frac12)/F(\frac12+x)$ is not the characteristic function of an infinitely divisible law. For $p=101$, $q=103$ the computation in floating point gives $\delta_0=0.28475$, $\gamma_0=0.67928$ and $K(\pi/\delta_0)=-1.11\times10^{-3}$.

Source: [`ch/bsy1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy1.tex), label `bsy:rem:negW`.

<a id="criterion_as_optional_stopping_of_planar_brownian_motion_on_log_h_theta"></a>

### The criterion as optional stopping: log of h at the hitting point of the line for planar Brownian motion, a submartingale that is a martingale exactly when QRH(theta) holds

Proposition 35.5.1, page 1236 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $B$ be planar Brownian motion started at $s_0=1+it_0$, $\tau$ its hitting time of the line $\{\operatorname{Re}s=\theta\}$, $\frac12\le\theta<1$, $H=\{\operatorname{Re}s>\theta\}$, $h_\theta(s)=\zeta(s)\frac{s-1}{s-2\theta+1}$ and $G_\theta(s,\rho)=\log\bigl|\frac{s-2\theta+\bar\rho}{s-\rho}\bigr|$. Then $\log|h_\theta(B_\tau)|$ is integrable and $\mathbb{E}\log|h_\theta(B_\tau)|=\log|h_\theta(s_0)|+\sum_{\beta>\theta}G_\theta(s_0,\rho)$, the sum over the zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ of $\zeta$ with $\beta>\theta$ with multiplicity. The process $\log|h_\theta(B_{t\wedge\tau})|$ is a local martingale and a submartingale, and a uniformly integrable martingale if and only if $\zeta$ has no zero with $\beta>\theta$. Each zero contributes its Riesz mass $2\pi$, times $\frac12$, times the value at $\rho$ of $\pi^{-1}G_\theta(s_0,\cdot)$, the density of the expected occupation measure of $B$ killed at $\tau$.

Source: [`ch/bsy1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy1.tex), label `bsy:prop:yor`.

<a id="moments_of_the_complex_logarithm_of_h_theta_under_harmonic_measure_given_qrh"></a>

### Under QRH(theta) the complex logarithm of h at the line has all moments equal to powers of its value at the starting point, equal variances of log of zeta and its argument, zero covariance, and a Littlewood Paley variance formula

Theorem 35.5.2, page 1237 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on QRH(theta): the Riemann zeta function has no zero with real part greater than theta, for the stated theta in [1/2, 1) (for theta = 1/2 this is the Riemann hypothesis).

Statement. Assume $\mathrm{QRH}(\theta)$, $\frac12\le\theta<1$: $\zeta$ has no zero with real part greater than $\theta$. Let $h_\theta(s)=\zeta(s)\frac{s-1}{s-2\theta+1}$, $H=\{\operatorname{Re}s>\theta\}$, $L$ the analytic logarithm of $h_\theta$ on $H$ with $L(\sigma+it)\to0$ as $\sigma\to+\infty$, and $G_\theta(1+it_0,w)=\log\bigl|\frac{w-2\theta+1-it_0}{w-1-it_0}\bigr|$ the Green function of $H$ with pole $1+it_0$. For almost every $\tau$ the limit $Z(\tau)=X(\tau)+iY(\tau)=\lim_{\sigma\downarrow\theta}L(\sigma+i\tau)$ exists, $X(\tau)=\log|\zeta(\theta+i\tau)|$ and $Y(\tau)=\arg h_\theta(\theta+i\tau)$ continued along the horizontal path from $+\infty$. Let $\tau$ have the Cauchy law with density $\frac{1-\theta}{\pi((1-\theta)^2+(t_0-\tau)^2)}$ and $z_0=x_0+iy_0=L(1+it_0)$. Then $\mathbb{E}|Z|^p<\infty$ for every $p<\infty$, $\mathbb{E}[Z^k]=z_0^k$ for every $k\ge1$, and in particular $\mathbb{E}X=x_0$, $\mathbb{E}Y=y_0$, $\operatorname{Var}X=\operatorname{Var}Y$, $\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=0$, with $\operatorname{Var}X=\operatorname{Var}Y=\frac1\pi\iint_HG_\theta(1+it_0,w)\bigl|\frac{h_\theta'}{h_\theta}(w)\bigr|^2dA(w)$. The raw argument of $\zeta$ does not satisfy these identities: at $\theta=\frac12$, $t_0=0$ under the Riemann hypothesis the variance of $\arg\zeta$ exceeds that of $\log|\zeta|$ by more than $\pi^2/3$.

Source: [`ch/bsy1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy1.tex), label `bsy:thm:cmart`.

<a id="computed_moments_of_log_h_theta_for_zeta_and_the_davenport_heilbronn_function"></a>

### Computed moments of the complex logarithm of h at the line for zeta and the Davenport and Heilbronn function: the identities hold for zeta and fail for Davenport and Heilbronn

Table 35.2, page 1239 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $h_\theta(s)=\zeta(s)\frac{s-1}{s-2\theta+1}$ for $\zeta$, $Z=X+iY=\log h_\theta(\theta+i\tau)$ (continued horizontally from $+\infty$) with $\tau$ Cauchy distributed with centre $t_0$ and scale $1-\theta$, $h=f$ for the Davenport and Heilbronn function, and $x_0+iy_0=\log h(1+it_0)$. Computed in floating point (Poisson weighted panels between the zeros, with a window $|\tau-t_0|\le13000$ and a tail correction; the larger of the difference between two meshes and half the tail correction is at most $2.1\times10^{-5}$ in each entry): for $\zeta$, $\mathbb{E}X-x_0=\mathbb{E}Y-y_0=\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=0$ and $\operatorname{Var}X=\operatorname{Var}Y$ equal to $0.1415$ at $(\theta,t_0)=(\frac12,0)$, $0.7056$ at $(\frac12,85.7)$, $1.0539$ at $(\frac12,1000)$, $1.1298$ at $(\frac12,5000)$ and $0.1341$ at $(\frac34,85.7)$ to that accuracy; for the Davenport and Heilbronn function at $(\frac12,85.7)$, $\mathbb{E}X-x_0=1.4407$, $\mathbb{E}Y-y_0=-0.0016$, $\operatorname{Var}X=0.6410$, $\operatorname{Var}Y=4.4414$, $\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=-0.0727$, and at $(\frac34,85.7)$, $\mathbb{E}X-x_0=0.4770$, $\mathbb{E}Y-y_0=-0.0003$, $\operatorname{Var}X=1.0124$, $\operatorname{Var}Y=3.2682$, $\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=-0.0162$, so the identities fail there. The agreement for $\zeta$ is a computation and not a proof for any $\theta$.

Source: [`ch/bsy1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy1.tex), label `bsy:tab:cm`.

<a id="complex_moments_of_log_h_theta_through_horizontal_cuts_from_the_zeros_without_qrh"></a>

### Without the hypothesis that no zero lies right of the line Re s = theta: the defects of the complex moments of log h as integrals along horizontal cuts from the zeros to the line

Proposition 35.5.4, page 1239 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\frac12\le\theta<1$, $z=1+it_0$, $z^*=2\theta-1+it_0$, $K(s)=\frac1{s-z^*}-\frac1{s-z}$ and $h_\theta(s)=\zeta(s)\frac{s-1}{s-2\theta+1}$. For each ordinate $\gamma$ of a zero with $\beta>\theta$ let $b_\gamma$ be the largest real part of the zeros with that ordinate, $C_\gamma=[\theta+i\gamma,b_\gamma+i\gamma]$, and for $x+i\gamma\in C_\gamma$ let $M_\gamma(x)$ be the number of zeros $\beta'+i\gamma$ with $\beta'>x$, with multiplicity. Let $L$ be the logarithm of $h_\theta$ on $\{\operatorname{Re}s>\theta\}$ minus the cuts, continued along horizontal paths from $+\infty$ where it tends to $0$, $z_0=L(z)$, $L_-$ its boundary value from below on $C_\gamma$ (the value above minus the value below is $2\pi iM_\gamma$), $Z(\tau)=\lim_{\sigma\downarrow\theta}L(\sigma+i\tau)$ and $\tau$ Cauchy distributed with centre $t_0$ and scale $1-\theta$. Then for every polynomial $F$, $\mathbb{E}F(Z)-F(z_0)=\sum_\gamma\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{C_\gamma}[F(L_-+2\pi iM_\gamma)-F(L_-)]K(s)\,ds$, each integral taken from left to right and the sum absolutely convergent. In particular $D:=\mathbb{E}Z-z_0=\sum_{\beta>\theta}[\log\frac{\rho-z^*}{\rho-z}-\log\frac{\theta+i\gamma-z^*}{\theta+i\gamma-z}]$ over the zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ with multiplicity, with the logarithms continued along the cut, and $\mathbb{E}Z^2-z_0^2=2\sum_\gamma\int_{C_\gamma}M_\gamma(L_-+\pi iM_\gamma)K\,ds$. The real part of the formula for $D$ is the Balazard, Saias and Yor identity at $1+it_0$. The second order balance $\operatorname{Var}X=\operatorname{Var}Y$, $\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=0$ for $Z=X+iY$ holds exactly when $2\sum_\gamma\int_{C_\gamma}M_\gamma(L_-+\pi iM_\gamma-z_0)K\,ds=D^2$. The same holds for the Davenport and Heilbronn function with $h=f$ when no zero has $\gamma=t_0$ and $\beta\ge1$. A floating point check on the Davenport and Heilbronn function at $t_0=85.7$ with the zeros below height $700$ gives at $\theta=\frac12$ the defect $\mathbb{E}Z-z_0=1.4407-0.0016\,i$ and the balance defect $\operatorname{Var}X-\operatorname{Var}Y+2i\operatorname{Cov}(X,Y)=-3.8003-0.1455\,i$, against $1.4407-0.0016\,i$ and $-3.8004-0.1455\,i$ from the computed moments, and at $\theta=\frac34$ $0.4770-0.0003\,i$ and $-2.2558-0.0323\,i$ for both; the jump across every cut is $2\pi i$ to $7$ digits (computed). Heuristic and not claimed: that the balance fails for most $t_0$ when a zero lies right of the line.

Source: [`ch/bsy1.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy1.tex), label `bsy:prop:cuts`.

<a id="log_of_zeta_has_every_moment_under_the_cauchy_law_on_a_vertical_line"></a>

### Finite moments of log of zeta under the Cauchy law on a line at every level and height

Lemma 35.6.1, page 1241 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\frac12\le\theta<1$, $t_0\in\mathbb{R}$, $f(\tau)=\log|\zeta(\theta+i\tau)|$ and $P$ the Cauchy law with density $\frac{1-\theta}{\pi((1-\theta)^2+(t_0-\tau)^2)}$. Then $\mathbb{E}_P|f|^p<\infty$ for every $p<\infty$. Hence the plain Monte Carlo estimator of $\mathbb{E}_Pf$ that averages $f$ at $n$ independent exact Cauchy draws is unbiased and has root mean square error $(\operatorname{Var}_Pf/n)^{1/2}$ with no truncation of the heavy tail. The proof bounds $\int_T^{T+1}|f|^p\,dt\ll_p\log^pT$ using the convexity bound and the local formula of Titchmarsh for $\log|\zeta|$.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:lem:var`.

<a id="computed_gain_factor_of_the_optimal_weight_over_plain_monte_carlo_for_the_defect_integrands"></a>

### Computed bound on the gain of any weight over plain Monte Carlo for independent draws: the factor Var f over the squared mean absolute deviation is between 1.35 and 2.46

Remark 35.6.2, page 1242 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $\mu=\mathbb{E}_Pf$, $w>0$, $Z=\mathbb{E}_Pw$ and $q=Pw/Z$. For independent draws from $q$ the self normalised estimator $\hat\mu=\sum_if(\tau_i)/w(\tau_i)\big/\sum_i1/w(\tau_i)$ has $n\operatorname{Var}\hat\mu\to Z\,\mathbb{E}_P[(f-\mu)^2/w]$, at least $(\mathbb{E}_P|f-\mu|)^2$ with equality exactly for $w\propto|f-\mu|$, and $(\mathbb{E}_P|f-\mu|)^2\le\operatorname{Var}_Pf$. For the nine integrands $f=\log|h|$ of the book's table of local defects (zeta and Davenport and Heilbronn at several levels and heights), the factor $\operatorname{Var}_Pf/(\mathbb{E}_P|f-\mu|)^2$ ranges from $1.35$ to $2.46$ with an error up to $0.03$ (computed by quadrature), so for independent draws no weight gains more than that over plain Monte Carlo. For a Markov chain negative autocorrelation can bring the limit below the value for independent draws, so the factor does not bound Markov samplers. The optimal weight itself is the standard one of self normalised importance sampling.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:rem:weight`.

<a id="computed_local_defects_of_the_cauchy_average_for_zeta_and_davenport_heilbronn"></a>

### Computed local defects D_theta(t_0) for zeta and the Davenport and Heilbronn function by quadrature, plain Monte Carlo and vertical Monte Carlo

Table 35.3, page 1244 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Let $D_\theta(t_0)$ be the defect of the Cauchy average of $\log|h|$ on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\theta$ against the Cauchy law of centre $t_0$ and scale $1-\theta$, minus $\log|h(1+it_0)|$, with $h=h_\theta$, $h_\theta(s)=\zeta(s)\frac{s-1}{s-2\theta+1}$, for $\zeta$ and $h=f$ for the Davenport and Heilbronn function, whose zero $0.808517182457+85.699348485378\,i$ lies off the critical line. Computed in floating point (adaptive quadrature with the zeros as breakpoints on $|\tau-t_0|\le W$, plain Monte Carlo with $20{,}000$ exact Cauchy draws for $\zeta$ and $4{,}000$ for the Davenport and Heilbronn function, and a vertical likelihood Metropolis sampler): for $\zeta$ at $(\theta,t_0)=(\frac12,0),(\frac78,0),(\frac12,85.7),(\frac34,85.7),(\frac78,85.7)$ the quadrature at $W=200$ gives values of absolute value at most $5.0\times10^{-6}$, and both Monte Carlo columns agree with $0$ within $2.4$ standard errors; for the Davenport and Heilbronn function the quadrature at $W=200$ gives $1.4406$ at $(\frac12,85.7)$, $0.47698$ at $(\frac34,85.7)$, $1.47\times10^{-4}$ at $(\frac34,100)$ and $-3.6\times10^{-7}$ at $(\frac78,85.7)$, against the predictions $1.4407$, $0.4770$, $1.49\times10^{-4}$ and $0$ (the sum of the Green potentials of the zeros found below height $700$; the exact defect at $\theta=\frac78$ is positive, since $f$ has zeros with real part above $1$). The neglected Cauchy mass outside the window makes the realised truncation errors larger than the printed digits suggest. This is a computation at these points and not a statement for all heights.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:tab:defects`.

<a id="computed_root_mean_square_error_of_the_weighted_trapezoid_rule_for_the_cauchy_average"></a>

### Computed errors of plain Monte Carlo, the Yakowitz, Krimmel and Szidarovszky trapezoid rule and its Dirichlet polynomial control for the Cauchy average of log of zeta

Table 35.4, page 1246 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Computed in floating point over $400$ replications at $t_0=0$ for the Cauchy average of $\log|\zeta(\theta+i\tau)|$, with $N$ between $500$ and $16{,}000$ nodes: at $\theta=\frac12$ the root mean square error of plain Monte Carlo, of the sorted trapezoid rule (weights of Yakowitz, Krimmel and Szidarovszky, 1978) and of the trapezoid rule with the exact control by the Selberg smoothed truncation of $\log\zeta$ ($M=100$) is $1.7\times10^{-2}$, $9.6\times10^{-3}$ and $5.3\times10^{-3}$ at $N=500$ and $3.1\times10^{-3}$, $9.7\times10^{-4}$ and $7.2\times10^{-4}$ at $N=16{,}000$, a gain of $3.2$ to $4.3$; at $\theta=\frac78$ ($M=1000$) it is $3.0\times10^{-2}$, $2.3\times10^{-3}$ and $4.0\times10^{-4}$ at $N=500$ and $5.1\times10^{-3}$, $2.9\times10^{-4}$ and $6.9\times10^{-5}$ at $N=16{,}000$, a gain of $65$ to $75$. The fitted slopes over $500\le N\le16{,}000$ at $\theta=\frac12$ and $\frac78$ are $-0.49$ and $-0.50$ (plain), $-0.66$ and $-0.60$ (trapezoid) and $-0.58$ and $-0.52$ (trapezoid with control), not the $-2$ of the bound for $g\in C^2$. The sampling error of each entry is about $3.5\%$. The reference values $0$ and $\log4$ are those the criterion gives under the Riemann hypothesis and QRH(7/8); with no hypothesis they hold to within $7.4\times10^{-13}$ and $4.7\times10^{-14}$, a floating point computation. This is a computation and not a proof of a rate.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:tab:yks`.

<a id="why_the_trapezoid_rule_on_sorted_nodes_has_no_n_to_the_minus_four_bound_for_log_zeta"></a>

### The integrand of the Cauchy average of log of zeta is not C^1 on the unit interval, so the N to the minus four bound of Yakowitz, Krimmel and Szidarovszky does not apply

Proposition 35.6.4, page 1247 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $\frac12\le\theta<1$, $f(\tau)=\log|\zeta(\theta+i\tau)|$ and $g=f\circ\tau$ with $\tau(u)=t_0+(1-\theta)\tan(\pi(u-\frac12))$, $u\in(0,1)$. If $\theta=\frac12$, $g$ is unbounded near $\tau^{-1}(\gamma)$ for every ordinate $\gamma$ of a zero on the line. If $\frac12<\theta<1$, $g'$ is unbounded near $u=0$ and near $u=1$. In both cases $g\notin C^1[0,1]$, so the bound $\mathbb{E}(T_N-\mathbb{E}_Pf)^2=O(N^{-4})$ of Yakowitz, Krimmel and Szidarovszky (1978) for the sorted trapezoid rule $T_N$ with $N$ uniform nodes, which assumes $g\in C^2[0,1]$, does not apply. The proof for $\frac12<\theta<1$ uses the mean value theorems $T^{-1}\int_1^T|\zeta(\theta+it)|^2dt\to\zeta(2\theta)$ and $T^{-1}\int_1^T|\zeta(\theta+it)|^4dt\to\zeta(2\theta)^4/\zeta(4\theta)$ and the inequality $\zeta(4\theta)<\zeta(2\theta)^2$.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:prop:rate`.

<a id="balazard_saias_yor_identity_on_a_half_disc_with_green_function_and_harmonic_measure"></a>

### The Balazard, Saias and Yor identity on a half disc: exact local form with the Green function of the half disc and zeros on the diameter subtracted

Theorem 35.6.6, page 1249 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $c=\theta+it_0$, $R>0$, $H=\{|s-c|<R,\operatorname{Re}s>\theta\}$, $z\in H$ and $\omega_z$ the harmonic measure of $\partial H$ seen from $z$. Let $h\not\equiv0$ be analytic on a neighbourhood of $\overline H$, with no zero on the closed arc $\{|s-c|=R,\operatorname{Re}s\ge\theta\}$, with zeros $\rho_1,\dots,\rho_n$ of multiplicities $m_1,\dots,m_n$ on the open diameter, and $h(z)\ne0$. Then $\int_{\partial H}(\log|h|-\sum_jm_j\log|s-\rho_j|)\,d\omega_z=\log|h(z)|-\sum_jm_j\log|z-\rho_j|+\sum_{\rho\in H}G_H(z,\rho)$, the last sum over the zeros of $h$ in $H$ with multiplicity, and the integrand on the left is real analytic on each of the two closed pieces of $\partial H$. In the coordinate $w=(s-c)/R$ with $w_z=(z-c)/R$, $w^*=-\overline{w_z}$ and $G_D(a,w)=\log|(1-\bar aw)/(w-a)|$, the Green function is $G_H(z,\cdot)=G_D(w_z,\cdot)-G_D(w^*,\cdot)$; on the arc $w=e^{i\phi}$, $|\phi|\le\frac\pi2$, the harmonic measure has density $\frac{1-|w_z|^2}{2\pi|e^{i\phi}-w_z|^2}-\frac{1-|w^*|^2}{2\pi|e^{i\phi}-w^*|^2}$ with respect to $d\phi$, and on the diameter $w=iy$ the density with respect to $dy$ is $\frac1{2\pi}\partial_x[G_D(w_z,x+iy)-G_D(w^*,x+iy)]$ at $x=0$. Both densities are real analytic up to the corners $w=\pm i$, where they vanish to first order. In particular $h$ has no zero in $H$ if and only if the identity holds without the Green sum.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:thm:halfdisk`.

<a id="half_disc_identity_tends_to_the_balazard_saias_yor_identity_as_the_radius_tends_to_infinity"></a>

### The half disc identity becomes the Balazard, Saias and Yor identity on the half plane as the radius tends to infinity

Remark 35.6.7, page 1250 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $h_\theta(s)=\zeta(s)\frac{s-1}{s-2\theta+1}$ and $z=1+it_0$. Along radii $R_k\to\infty$ with $|t_0\pm R_k-\gamma|\ge c/\log R_k$ for every zero ordinate $\gamma$, the arc term of the half disc identity tends to $0$ (on the arc the density is at most $CR^{-1}\cos\phi$, so the part of the arc with $\theta\le\operatorname{Re}s\le2$ has harmonic measure $O(R_k^{-3})$, and there $|\log|h_\theta||=O(\log^2R_k)$, while $|\log|h_\theta(s)||=O(2^{-\operatorname{Re}s}+R_k^{-1})$ on the rest of the arc), the density on the diameter increases to the Cauchy density of scale $1-\theta$ and centre $t_0$, and the Green sum increases to the sum of the Green potentials of the zeros right of the line. So the half disc identity becomes the Balazard, Saias and Yor identity at $1+it_0$. That the arc carries vanishing harmonic measure would not suffice by itself: for $h(s)=e^{s-\theta}$ the arc contributes $1-\theta$ for every $R$.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:rem:halfplane`.

<a id="exact_bias_and_variance_of_the_sorted_trapezoid_rule_at_independent_uniform_nodes"></a>

### The sorted trapezoid rule at independent uniform nodes: exact leading bias and variance of order N to the minus five, so mean square N to the minus four, and N to the minus five when the end slopes agree

Lemma 35.6.8, page 1250 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $g\in C^4[a,b]$ and let $T_N$ be the trapezoid rule on the sorted $N$ independent uniform nodes on $[a,b]$ with the end points $a$ and $b$ added. Then $\mathbb{E}T_N-\int_a^bg=\frac{(b-a)^2(g'(b)-g'(a))}{2(N+1)(N+2)}+O(N^{-3})$ and $\operatorname{Var}T_N=O(N^{-5})$. So the mean square error is $O(N^{-4})$, and $O(N^{-5})$ when $g'(a)=g'(b)$.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:lem:trap`.

<a id="half_disc_boundary_integral_by_sorted_trapezoid_rule_has_mean_square_rate_n_to_the_minus_four_and_minus_five"></a>

### Half disc identity: the sorted trapezoid rule on the two smooth pieces of the boundary has mean square error O(N^-4), and O(N^-5) after a change of variable

Result 35.6.5, page 1251 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. In the half disc identity, each of the two pieces of the boundary integral is a smooth integrand on a closed interval vanishing at the ends. By the sorted trapezoid rule lemma the rule with $N/2$ nodes on each piece has mean square error $O(N^{-4})$, its bias $\frac{2(b-a)^2(g'(b)-g'(a))}{(N+2)(N+4)}+O(N^{-3})$ vanishing to that order only if the end slopes agree. The change of variable $y=\Phi(v)=v+\sin(\pi v)/\pi$ on each piece, written on $[-1,1]$, makes the transformed integrand $g(\Phi(v))\Phi'(v)$ vanish to at least fifth order at the ends, since $\Phi'(\pm(1-r))=\frac{\pi^2}2r^2+O(r^4)$ and $1-|\Phi(\pm(1-r))|=\frac{\pi^2}6r^3+O(r^5)$; both end slopes are then zero and the mean square error is $O(N^{-5})$. These are upper bounds.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:res:halfdisk_rates`.

<a id="computed_errors_of_the_sorted_trapezoid_rule_on_the_half_disc_identity_for_zeta_and_davenport_heilbronn"></a>

### Computed errors of plain Monte Carlo and the sorted trapezoid rule, with and without the change of variable, on the half disc identity for zeta and for Davenport and Heilbronn

Table 35.5, page 1252 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Computed in floating point on the half disc identity with $R=1$, $t_0=85.7$, $z=c+\frac12R$, over $200$ replications with $N/2$ nodes on each boundary piece, slopes fitted for $N\ge1024$ (in brackets). For $\zeta$ at $\theta=\frac34$ (target $0.028322$): plain $1.2\times10^{-3}$ ($-0.49$), sorted trapezoid $3.4\times10^{-9}$ ($-2.07$), with the change of variable $2.7\times10^{-9}$ ($-2.49$). For $\zeta$ at $\theta=\frac12$ with the zero $\frac12+84.7354\ldots i$ on the diameter subtracted (target $0.048774$): $2.7\times10^{-3}$ ($-0.52$), $1.9\times10^{-9}$ ($-2.28$), $5.1\times10^{-9}$ ($-2.49$). For the Davenport and Heilbronn function at $\theta=\frac12$ with its zero $0.8085\ldots+85.6993\ldots i$ in the half disc, so that the target $-0.365254$ includes $G_H(z,\rho)=1.12940$: $2.1\times10^{-3}$ ($-0.50$), $7.8\times10^{-9}$ ($-2.16$), $1.4\times10^{-8}$ ($-2.51$). Gauss and Legendre quadrature of the boundary integral agrees with the right side to $5\times10^{-15}$. These are computations and not proofs; at these $N$ the change of variable is not the more accurate rule for $\zeta$ and the Davenport and Heilbronn function at $\theta=\frac12$, and whether the rules cross beyond $N=32{,}768$ was not computed.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:tab:halfdisk`.

<a id="tail_of_the_cauchy_average_of_log_zeta_beyond_height_t_under_rh"></a>

### Under RH, the Cauchy tail of log of zeta beyond distance T from the centre is O(log T / (T^2 (log log T)^2)) at level one half and O(T^-2 log T) at levels above

Result 35.6.6, page 1252 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: conditional on The Riemann hypothesis: every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part 1/2.

Statement. Assume the Riemann hypothesis. Let $t_0\in\mathbb{R}$ and $P_{1/2}(t_0-\tau)$ the Cauchy density of centre $t_0$ and scale $\frac12$. Using the estimate $\int_T^t\log|\zeta(\frac12+iu)|\,du=O(\log t/(\log\log t)^2)$ for $3\le T\le t$ (Bui, Lester and Milinovich 2014) and integration by parts, $\int_{|\tau-t_0|>T}\log|\zeta(\frac12+i\tau)|\,P_{1/2}(t_0-\tau)\,d\tau=O_{t_0}(\log T/(T^2(\log\log T)^2))$. At a level $\theta\in(\frac12,1)$, under the same hypothesis, the integral of $\log\zeta$ around the rectangle with vertices $\theta+iT$, $\theta+it$ and $+\infty$ bounds the primitive of $\log|\zeta(\theta+iu)|$ by $O_\theta(\log t)$, and the tail of the Cauchy average (scale $1-\theta$) beyond $T$ by $O_\theta(T^{-2}\log T)$. The case $t_0=0$, $\theta=\frac12$ is a theorem of Bui, Lester and Milinovich; the extension to every centre and to the levels above one half is the book's.

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:res:tail`.

<a id="computed_truncation_error_of_the_cauchy_average_by_the_shifted_trapezoid_rule_on_the_whole_line"></a>

### Computed errors of the truncated shifted trapezoid rule for the Cauchy average of log of zeta over a window at height 85.7, with zeros deflated at level one half

Table 35.6, page 1253 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: computed.

Statement. Computed in floating point at $t_0=85.7$: the error of the shifted trapezoid rule for the Cauchy average of $\log|\zeta(\theta+i\tau)|$ over $|\tau-t_0|\le T$, minus $\log|h_\theta(1+it_0)|$, mean over $10$ random shifts. At $\theta=\frac34$ (step $0.02$): errors $-9.47\times10^{-4}$, $-3.40\times10^{-5}$, $+4.36\times10^{-6}$, $+6.47\times10^{-8}$, $-1.36\times10^{-7}$ at $T=10,40,160,640,1280$. At $\theta=\frac12$ (step $0.01$, the zeros with $|\gamma-t_0|\le T+1$ deflated and their window means added back): $-2.09\times10^{-3}$, $-5.37\times10^{-5}$, $+1.05\times10^{-5}$, $+7.84\times10^{-8}$ at $T=10,40,160,640$, with $10,33,123,742$ zeros deflated. In this range $T^2\cdot|\mathrm{error}|$ stays below $0.27$, and the spread over the shifts is at most $8.1\times10^{-7}$. The shifted grid is unbiased for the window integral, so the mean error is minus the Cauchy tail. This is a computation and not a theorem about the rule: at a fixed step the discretisation error of one shift need not tend to $0$ as $T$ grows, and the bounds on the tail are conditional on the Riemann hypothesis. Adding back the whole line means of the deflating functions instead would add their tails, and for that variant $T^2\cdot|\mathrm{error}|$ grows from $0.15$ at $T=10$ to $1.24$ at $T=640$ (computed).

Source: [`ch/bsy2.tex`](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/computing_rh/blob/v1.4.1/ch/bsy2.tex), label `bsy:tab:trunc`.

<a id="rates_of_the_shifted_trapezoid_grid_for_the_smoothed_riesz_integrand"></a>

### Rates of the randomly shifted product trapezoid rule on the torus (every power for a smooth periodic integrand, order N to the minus one with a logarithmic singularity) and N to the minus three halves for Voronoi and Delaunay weights at independent uniform nodes

Proposition 35.7.2, page 1256 of Polson and Sokolov (2026), *Computing the Riemann Hypothesis: Thorin Measures, Pólya Densities and Hitting Times*, edition 1. New in this book.

Status: proved.

Statement. Let $g$ be square integrable on the torus $[0,1)^2$ and $Q(\delta)=m^{-2}\sum_{j\in\{0,\dots,m-1\}^2}g(j/m+\delta)$, with $N=m^2$ nodes and $\delta$ uniform on $[0,1/m)^2$. Then $\mathbb{E}_\delta Q=\int g$ and $\mathbb{E}_\delta|Q-\int g|^2=\sum_{\ell\ne0}|\hat g(m\ell)|^2$.
